full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/Brazil

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Did you talk to Xi about—did you talk to Xi about the Ukraine war?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Because China and Brazil together has a proposal to bring Russia and Ukraine to talk.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, that's good. That's fine. I'm ready. That's good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When are you going to talk with the Brazilian President?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. How did Brazil get involved?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Brazil is involved.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. This is a new one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes. When are you going to talk to Lula?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Are you from Brazil?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I'm from Brazil.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Ah.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When are you talking——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. That's why they're involved, I guess.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When are you going to talk with the Brazilian President? How do you see your relationship with Latin America and Brazil?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Great. Should be great. They need us much more than we need them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We don't need them. They need us. Everybody needs us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, are you going to go to China?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: European Defense Spending Levels/Spain

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What can we expect of the countries in NATO that spend the least amount of money, like Spain, France, below the 5 percent that you just mentioned?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Spain is very low.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. How can you increase that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And yet aren't they a BRICS nation?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They're a BRICS nation, Spain.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. How is that so?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You know what a BRICS nation is? Well, you'll figure it out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But—and if the BRICS nations want to do that, that's okay, but we're going to put at least a 100-percent tariff on the business they do with the United States. You know what the BRICS is, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You guys know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Brazil, Russia——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You know what I'm saying, right? You know what I'm saying.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Sir, this is a——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But Spain is not in the BRICS.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So it's not even a threat. In fact, since I made that statement, Biden said, "Well, they have us over a barrel." I said, "No, we have them over a barrel." And there's no way they're going to be able to do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. This is an Executive order relating to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. They are risking hundred-percent tariffs, those countries, like Spain?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. As a BRICS nation, yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But how is it a BRICS nation?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They'll have a hundred-percent tariff if they so much as even thinking about doing what they thought.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you had said you would end the Russia-Ukraine war on your first day in office. Where do things stand right now? And how do you intend to make that happen?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, this is only half a day. I have another half a day left. We'll see. We want to get it done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Sir, this is an order creating and implementing the "Department of Governmental Efficiency," known as DOGE.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Okay, that's a big one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Greenland

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. About Greenland, you have shown interest in buying it, but is there any other option that would satisfy you?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. About what?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Greenland, instead of buying it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Finland?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Greenland.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Oh, Greenland. Greenland is a wonderful place. We need it for international security. And I'm sure that Denmark will come along. I think, you know, it's costing them a lot of money to maintain it, to keep it. The people of Greenland are not happy with Denmark, as you know. I think they're happy with us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We had representatives—my son and representatives went up there 2 weeks ago, and they like us. So we'll see what happens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But Greenland is necessary—not for us, it's necessary for international security. You have Russian boats all over the place. You have China boats all over the place, warships. And they can't maintain it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When are you going to be talking to Vladimir Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you plan to meet President Putin, sir?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Who?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you plan to meet President Putin, sir?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I'll be meeting with President Putin.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When, do you think?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't know. I can't—it's being set up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you said you were going to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——I think I'd probably go there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——end the wars first day. How do you plan to end the Ukraine war?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, we're going to try and get it done as quickly as possible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you want to push Israel and Saudi Arabia——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It should have never started. You know, the war with Ukraine and Russia should have never started. It would have never started if I were president.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, when do you think you'll speak to—when do you plan to speak to President Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Could be very soon.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And you talked a bit about Ukraine and Russia, but how long do you think it would take to end that conflict and——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I have to speak to President Putin. We're going to have to find out. He's not— he can't be thrilled. He's not doing so well. I mean, he's grinding it out, but most people thought that war would have been over in about 1 week, and now you're into 3 years. Right? So he can't be—he can't be thrilled. It's not making him look very good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, eventually, you know, I mean, it's a big machine, so things will happen. But I think he would be very well off to end that war. We have numbers that—almost a million Russian soldiers have been killed. About 700,000 Ukrainian soldiers are killed. Russia is bigger. They have more soldiers to lose. But that's no way to run a country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You said you plan to speak with President Putin soon. What about President Zelenskyy? And what's your message to him?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, I—would. But he has told me he wants to make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Zelenskyy told you that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: The President. He wants—Zelenskyy wants to make a deal. [The President signed an Executive order.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What kind of a deal?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't know if Putin does. He might not. I don't know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: He should make a deal. I think he's destroying Russia by not making a deal. I think Russia is going to be in big trouble—you take a look at their economy, you take a look at the inflation in Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I would—I would hope—I got along with him great. And you know, I would hope he wants to make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Iran

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, are you keeping U.S. sanctions on Russia until he makes a deal?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, sanctions or tariffs. I think the word "tariff" is much better because it keeps your dollar stronger. I think tariffs are more effective.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I mean, I used sanctions on Iran. Iran—Iran was broke. When I left office, Iran was broke. They had no money for Hamas or Hizballah. None. They were flat broke. And October 7 would have never happened, and I think you all know that. It would have never happened. They had no money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now they're rich, but you know, they're weakened in a different way. I would say that the one attack by Israel really set them back. It really set them back—the pagers—the pagers and others. You know, the attack on air defense was a—that was a bad attack for Iran.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What are you signing now, sir?

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. It's an Executive order relating to reforms to the Federal workforce, including to the Senior Executive Service.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President signed a memorandum titled, "Restoring Accountability for Career Senior Executives."]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We're getting rid of all of the cancer—I call it "cancer"—the cancer caused by the Biden administration.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You've called for a cease-fire—you've called for a cease-fire in Ukraine. If Vladimir Putin doesn't come to the table to negotiate with you, will you put additional sanctions on Russia?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Sounds likely, yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And do you think that the war should be frozen, currently, along current battle lines?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. The war should have never started. If you had a competent President, which you didn't, the war wouldn't have happened. The war in Ukraine would have never happened if I were President, but that couldn't happen because the election was rigged.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Cease-Fire and Hostage-Release Deal Between Israel and Hamas

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you have an update on the Gaza cease-fire? And are you planning to travel to the Middle East soon?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We're thinking about going to the Middle East. Not yet. We have a thing called "the hostages are coming back" going on right now, and they are coming back. Some of them have been very—you know, very damaged. You look at the young lady with her hand practically blown off.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know how that happened, right? Did you know that happened? When you find out, you're not going to be too happy, because it was terrible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But the hostages are starting to come back. Oh, if I—if I weren't here, they wouldn't be back ever. They would have never come back—they would have all died.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If this were done a year earlier, if the—if Biden would have done this deal a year and a half, two years ago or—frankly, it should have never happened. October 7 should have never happened. Nobody should be dead. But through weakness, they allowed it to happen, and then it was a disaster from there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you go back just 6 months ago, many of these young people were living. You know, young people don't die like that. They're just dying. And young people aren't dying at 22 and 23 years old. They don't die. But now they're dying, and you wonder why they're dying. They're being killed, and they have been killed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But they say, 6 months ago, you would have had 11 more living hostages. Think of that: six months ago. But Biden couldn't get it done. And it was only the imposition by—that I put on it as a deadline that got it done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it's a very sad situation. Should have—it should have never happened. I'll tell you, two things should have never happened—three things. Inflation should have never happened. It would have never happened, except for what they did to energy and their crazy spending. And Ukraine would have never happened, never.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: By the way, Russia never would have gone into Ukraine. I had a very strong understanding with Putin. They would—it would have never, ever happened. He disrespected Biden. Very simple. He disrespects people. He's smart. He understands. He disrespected Biden.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And also, the Middle East would have never happened because Iran was broke. They had no money. They had no money for Hamas. They had no money for Hizballah. It would have never happened. October 7 would have never happened. But it did happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So this is the cards I've been given, and we're getting the hostages back. That would have never happened under Biden. They would have never come back. They were just dying very—not that slowly. They were dying or being killed. But that was what was happening.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/North Atlantic Treaty Organization

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you going to keep sending weapons to Ukraine, or are you going to send—turn off the tap soon?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, we'll look into that. We're talking to Zelenskyy. We're going to be talking with President Putin very soon. And we'll see what—how it all happens. We're going to look at it very—one thing I do feel: The European Union should be paying a lot more than they're paying. Because, under Biden, I mean, we're in there for $200 billion more. Now, it affects them more than it affects us. We have an ocean in between—right?—a little thing called an ocean. The European Union should equalize. We're in there for $200 billion more than the European Union.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I mean, what are we, stupid? I guess the answer is yes, because they must think so. But the European Union takes advantage of us tremendously on trade, and they now take advantage of— and always have.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If I didn't get involved—years ago, my first term, one of the first things I noticed was that they're not paying enough. They're not paying. And a lot of those countries weren't even paying— the NATO countries, they weren't paying. Only 7 out of 28 were paying. We were one of them, and Poland was one. And they had a few of them that were paying, and some were paying very proudly. Usually, the closer to the borderline of Russia they were, the faster they paid. Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The ones that were further away tended not to pay so fast. And one thing on that: I think they should lift their number, not to 2 percent, but to 5 percent. NATO should be at 5 percent, not at 2 percent. Two percent is ridiculous.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, is that meeting that you mentioned with President Zelenskyy—will that take place here? And when and where will you meet with President Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't know. I mean, look——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——President Zelenskyy would like to have peace. He's told me that very strongly. He'd like to have peace. But it takes two to tango. We'll see what happens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When will you meet with President Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Anytime they want, I'll meet. I'd like to see that end. Millions of people are being killed. And they're being killed—it's a vicious situation. And they'll—now, largely, soldiers. A lot of people's—people have been killed in the cities. They look like demolition sites—buildings—massive buildings, bombed and coming down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The thing with Ukraine is that many more people died than you're reporting. You're not reporting the real numbers, and I'm not blaming you for that. I'm blaming, maybe, our government for not wanting to release those numbers. Many more people died than what you know about.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When those big buildings come down and they say two people were injured. No, no. Many people—thousands of people are being killed. But the people—the real killing now is on the warfront. It's a very flat land, and the only thing that stops a bullet is somebody's body. And you have young soldiers.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So Russia has lost about 800,000 soldiers now. Ukraine's lost about 600- or 700,000. I think the numbers are low that they're giving out. And—but they'll—they've lost massive numbers of young soldiers, and that war should stop.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's very flat. You know, it's beautiful farmland, and it's flat and really beautiful in a different kind of a way, but they don't have any protection. The only thing that stops a bullet is a body, and those bodies are stopping a lot of bullets, and they're getting—they're being decimated, both sides.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President addressed a gathering of global business leaders in Davos, Switzerland, by videoconference.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, thank you very much, Klaus. And hello to everyone in beautiful Davos.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This has been a truly historic week in the United States. Three days ago, I took the oath of office, and we began the golden age of America. The recent Presidential election was won by millions of votes and all seven—every one of them—all seven swing States. It was a massive mandate from the American people like hasn't been seen in many years. And some of the political pundits, even some of my so-called enemies, said it was the most consequential election victory in 129 years. That's quite nice.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What the world has witnessed in the past 72 hours is nothing less than a revolution of common sense. Our country will soon be stronger, wealthier, and more united than ever before, and the entire planet will be more peaceful and prosperous as a result of this incredible momentum and what we're doing and going to do.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My administration is acting with unprecedented speed to fix the disasters we've inherited from a totally inept group of people and to solve every single crisis facing our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This begins with confronting the economic chaos caused by the failed policies of the last administration. Over the past 4 years, our Government racked up $8 trillion in wasteful deficit spending and inflicted nation-wrecking energy restrictions, crippling regulations, and hidden taxes like never before. The result is the worst inflation crisis in modern history and sky-high interest rates for our citizens and even throughout the world. Food prices and the price of almost every other thing known to mankind went through the roof.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Biden totally lost control of what was going on in our country, but in particular, with our high-inflation economy and at our border. Because of these ruinous policies, total Government spending this year is $1.5 trillion higher than was projected to occur when I left office just 4 years ago. Likewise, the cost of servicing the debt is more than 230-percent higher than was projected in 2020.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The inflation rate we are inheriting remains 50-percent higher than the historic target. It was the highest inflation probably in the history of our country. That's why, from the moment I took office, I've taken rapid action to reverse each and every one of these radical left policies that created this calamity, in particular, with immigration, crime, and inflation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: On day one, I signed an Executive order directing every member of my Cabinet to marshal all powers at their disposal to defeat inflation and reduce the cost of daily life. I imposed a Federal hiring freeze, a Federal regulation freeze, a foreign aid freeze, and I created the new "Department of Government Efficiency."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I terminated the ridiculous and incredibly wasteful Green New Deal—I call it the "Green New Scam"; withdrew from the one-sided Paris climate accord; and ended the insane and costly electric vehicle mandate. We're going to let people buy the car they want to buy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I declared a national energy emergency—and it's so important—national energy emergency to unlock the liquid gold under our feet and pave the way for rapid approvals of new energy

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: infrastructure. The United States has the largest amount of oil and gas of any country on Earth, and we're going to use it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Not only will this reduce the cost of virtually all goods and services, it will make the United States a manufacturing superpower and the world capital of artificial intelligence and crypto.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My administration has also begun the largest deregulation campaign in history, far exceeding even the record-setting efforts of my last term.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In total, the Biden administration imposed $50,000 in additional regulatory costs on the average American household over the last 4 years. I have promised to eliminate 10 old regulations for every new regulation, which will soon put many thousands of dollars back in the pockets of American families.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: To further unleash our economy, our majorities in the House and Senate—which we also took, along with the Presidency—are going to pass the largest tax cut in American history, including massive tax cuts for workers and family and big tax cuts for domestic producers and manufacturers. And we're working with the Democrats on getting an extension of the original Trump tax cuts, as you probably know by just reading any paper.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My message to every business in the world is very simple: Come make your product in America, and we will give you among the lowest taxes of any nation on Earth. We're bringing them down very substantially, even from the original Trump tax cuts. But if you don't make your product in America, which is your prerogative, then, very simply, you will have to pay a tariff— differing amounts, but a tariff—which will direct hundreds of billions of dollars and even trillions of dollars into our Treasury to strengthen our economy and pay down debt.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under the Trump administration, there will be no better place on Earth to create jobs, build factories, or grow a company than right here in the good old U.S.A.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Already, American's economic—and you can see this, I think, maybe even in your—in your wonderful, wonderful room that you're all gathered together—so many of my friends—but, Americans, the economic confidence is soaring like we haven't seen in many, many decades, maybe not at all.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Upon my election, it was just announced that small-business optimism skyrocketed by 41 points in a single month. That's the highest ever. There's never been anything like that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: SoftBank has announced between a $100 and $200 billion investment in the U.S. economy because of the election result. And just 2 days ago, Oracle, SoftBank, and OpenAI announced a

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: $500 billion investment in AI infrastructure. Other companies, likewise, have announced billions and billions and billions—adding up to trillions—of investment in America, in the United States.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's also reported today in the papers that Saudi Arabia will be investing at least $600 billion in America. But I'll be asking the Crown Prince, who's a fantastic guy, to round it out to around $1 trillion. I think they'll do that because we've been very good to them. And I'm also going to ask Saudi Arabia and OPEC to bring down the cost of oil. You've got to bring it down, which, frankly, I'm surprised they didn't do before the election. That didn't show a lot of love by them not doing it. I was a little surprised by that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If the price came down, the Russia-Ukraine war would end immediately. Right now the price is high enough that that war will continue. You've got to bring down the oil price; you're going to end that war. They should have done it long ago. They're very responsible, actually, to a certain extent, for what's taking place—millions of lives are being lost.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: With oil prices going down, I'll demand that interest rates drop immediately. And likewise, they should be dropping all over the world. Interest rates should follow us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: All over, the progress that you're seeing is happening because of our historic victory in a recent Presidential election, one that has become quite well known throughout the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think a lot of things are happening to a lot of countries. They say that there's light shining all over the world since the election. And even countries that we aren't particularly friendly with are happy because they understand what—there is a future and the—how great the future will be.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under our leadership, America is back and open for business. And this week, I'm also taking swift action to stop the invasion at our southern border. They allowed people to come in at levels that nobody has ever seen before. It was ridiculous. I decided a—and declared to do—and very, very importantly—a national emergency on our border; immediately halted all entry of illegal border crossers, of which there were many; and began properly returning the illegal trespassers back to the place from which they came.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That action, as you've probably seen, has already started very strongly. I have deployed Active Duty U.S. military and National Guard troops to the border to assist in repelling the invasion. It was really an invasion. We will not allow our territory to be violated.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: After 4 long years, the United States is strong and sovereign and a beautiful nation once again. It's a strong, sovereign nation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In addition, I'm pleased to report that America is also a free nation once again. On day one, I signed an Executive order to stop all Government censorship. No longer will our Government label the speech of our own citizens as misinformation or disinformation, which are the favorite words of censors and those who wish to stop the free exchange of ideas and, frankly, progress.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We have saved free speech in America, and we've saved it strongly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: With another historic Executive order this week, I also ended the weaponization of law enforcement against the American people—and frankly, against politicians—and restored the fair, equal, and impartial rule of law.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My administration has taken action to abolish all discriminatory diversity, equity, and inclusion nonsense—and these are policies that were absolute nonsense—throughout the Government and the private sector. With the recent, yet somewhat unexpected, great Supreme Court decision just made, America will once again become a merit-based country. You have to hear that word: merit-based country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I've made it official—an official policy of the United States that there are only two genders, male and female, and we will have no men participating in women's sports, and transgender operations, which became the rage, will occur very rarely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Finally, as we restore common sense in America, we're moving quickly to bring back strength and peace and stability abroad. I'm also going to ask all NATO nations to increase defense spending to 5 percent of GDP, which is what it should have been years ago—it was only at 2 percent, and most nations didn't pay until I came along; I insisted that they pay, and they did—because the United States was really paying the difference at that time, and it's—it was unfair to the United States. But many, many things have been unfair for many years to the United States.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Before even taking office, my team negotiated a cease-fire agreement in the Middle East, which wouldn't have happened without us, as I think most of the people in the room know. Earlier this week, the hostages began to return to their families. They are returning, and it's a beautiful sight. And they'll be coming in more and more. They started coming back on Sunday.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our efforts to secure a peace settlement between Russia and Ukraine are now, hopefully, underway. It's so important to get that done. That is an absolute killing field.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Millions of soldiers are being killed. Nobody has seen anything like it since World War II. They're laying dead all over the flat fields. It's a flat field—farmland, and there's millions of Russians and millions of Ukrainians. Nobody's seen anything like it since World War II. It's time to end it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And here in America, we have big events coming up. Next year we have the 250th anniversary of America's founding. I'm so honored to be President during that. That's been a big event. They've been talking about it for 10 years. We also have the World Cup, and I understand Gianni—Gianni is in the room—Infantino. He was very instrumental in helping us get it—he's there with you someplace, I think—and I want to thank him for that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then we have the Olympics coming up, which I was instrumental in getting, also, in my first term. And who would have known that by skipping a term, I would get the Olympics? I was upset. I said, "You know, I got the Olympics to come, and I won't be President." But it turned out, through a stroke of luck or whatever you might call it, that I'm going to be President during the World Cup and the Olympics and the 250th anniversary. So that's going to be three big events.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we've accomplished more in less than 4 days—we have really been working 4 days— than other administrations have accomplished in 4 years, and we're just getting started. It's really an amazing thing to see, and the spirit and the light over our country has been incredible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under the last administration, our Nation has suffered greatly, but we are going to bring it back and make it greater, bigger, stronger, better than ever before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I want to thank everybody for being with you. I would have been there myself, except the inauguration was 2 days ago. I thought it might be a little bit quick to make it the first stop, but we'll get there one day. We hope to get there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I do appreciate—I heard the audience is fantastic, and many of my friends are in the audience. And I will be taking questions now from some very distinguished people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you all very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: World Economic Forum President and Chief Executive Officer Børge Brende
full_topic_context.text: World Economic Forum President and Chief Executive Officer Børge Brende. Thank you. Thank you very much, Mr. President, for that very powerful speech, and I think you could hear the applause all the way from Davos to the White House. But next year, it will be even better, because then you can get the applause here in Davos. So we wish you welcome to our village next year. We hope to see you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: Mr. Brende. So, we also know, Mr. President, that you open up for interaction here. We have a great panel with some of the most distinguished businesspeople in the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: Let me start with someone that you know really well, that I think is almost a neighbor of you in Mal-a-Lago in Florida, Mr. Steve Schwarzman, chairman, CEO, and cofounder of Blackstone Group.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: So, Steve, floor is yours.

full_topic_context.speaker: Blackstone Group Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and Cofounder Stephen A. Schwarzman
full_topic_context.text: Blackstone Group Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and Cofounder Stephen A. Schwarzman. Well, Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Hello, Steve.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Schwarzman
full_topic_context.text: Mr. Schwarzman. ——I'm sure the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia will be really glad you gave this speech today. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I hope so.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Deregulation/U.S. Economy/Canada-U.S. Trade/National Debt/Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Ms. Botín
full_topic_context.text: Ms. Botín. We are a big investor in the United States. We have many million customer, 12,000 employees. We're one of the largest auto lenders, and we recently launched a fully digital bank called Openbank.

full_topic_context.speaker: Ms. Botín
full_topic_context.text: We strongly believe banks have a pivotal role in the economy, and we can accelerate growth and help many more customers. That's what we do in the United States. So, as Brian pointed out, we very much welcome your focus on deregulation and reducing bureaucracy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Ms. Botín
full_topic_context.text: So my question is: What are your priorities in this regard, and how fast is this going to happen? Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I think it's going to—thank you and congratulations. I know very much about your bank, and you've done a fantastic job. Congratulations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We are going to move very quickly. We've moved very quickly. We've done things in the last 3 days that nobody thought were possible to do in years. And it's all taken—it's all taking effect. It's going to have a huge impact on the economy, a huge positive impact. Money was being wasted on crazy things.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I mean, the Green New Deal was such a total disgrace—what—how that was perpetrated. And it was conceived of by people that were average students—less-than-average students, I might add—and never even took a course in energy or the environment. It was just a game.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Remember, the world was going to end in 12 years? Remember that? Well, the 12 years has come and gone. It was going to end. It was going to all foam into earth. But you know, the time has come.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The—these people—and they really—they really scared the Democrats largely—I can't say the Republicans. Republicans maybe could have fought harder to stop it, but it's been a tremendous waste of money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, during my 4 years, we had the cleanest air, we had the cleanest water, and yet we had the most productive economy in the history of our country. We had the most productive economy. Until COVID came, we had the most productive in the history of our country, by far.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And actually, you could look worldwide, we—we're—we were beating everybody from China to everybody else. So—and we think we really—now, with what we have learned and all of the other things that have taken place, we think we can even far surpass that—actually, far, far surpass it. But we do—one thing we're going to be demanding is, we're going to be demanding respect from other nations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Canada. We have a tremendous deficit with Canada. We're not going to have that anymore. We can't do it. It's—I don't know if it's good for them. As you probably know, I say: "You can always become a State, and if you're a State, we won't have a deficit. We won't have to tariff you, et cetera, et cetera."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But Canada has been very tough to deal with over the years, and it's not fair that we should have a $200 billion or $250 billion deficit. We don't need them to make our cars, and they make a lot of them. We don't need their lumber because we have our own forests, et cetera, et cetera. We don't need their oil and gas. We have our—we have more than anybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, you know, just as an example, with Mexico—we're dealing with Mexico, I think, very well. And we're just—you know, we just want to be treated fairly with other nations, because there's hardly a nation in the world—and I blame this on us, and I blame it on politicians that for some reason—and probably mostly it's stupidity, but you could also say other reasons, but mostly stupidity—they've allowed other nations to take advantage of the U.S. And we can't allow that to happen anymore.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we have debt. It's a very small debt when you compare it to value—the value of the assets that we have, but we don't want to do that. We want to just have debt be obliterated, and we'll be able to do that fairly rapidly. And a lot of good things are going to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And—honestly, good things are going to happen for the world, and good things are going to happen for the people that are dealing with us—allies and beyond allies.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: One thing—very important—I really would like to be able to meet with President Putin soon and get that war end—ended, and—and that's not from the standpoint of economy or anything else. It's from the standpoint of millions of lives are being wasted. Beautiful, young people are being shot in the battlefield. You know, the bullet—a very flat land, as I said, and the bullet goes—there's no—there's no hiding. And a bullet—the only thing going to stop the bullet is a human body. And you have to see—I've seen pictures of what's taken place. It's a carnage.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we really have to stop that war. That war is horrible. And I'm not talking economy, I'm not talking economics, I'm not talking about natural resource. I'm just talking about: There's so many young people being killed in this war, and that's not including the people that have been killed as the cities are being, you know, knocked down building by building. So we really should get that stopped.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Likewise, in the Middle East, I think we've made a lot of progress in the Middle East, and I think that's going to—that's going to come along pretty well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: China-U.S. Relations/Coronavirus Pandemic/Russia/Ukraine/Denuclearization Efforts

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: Mr. Brende. Thank you, Mr. President. We know that most consequential relationship in the world is between the U.S. and China. U.S., 28 percent of the global economy; China close to 20. That's almost half of the global GDP.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: And we know that you called President Xi Jinping last Friday. We heard that you had a good discussion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: How do you see the relationship between the U.S. and China in the next 4 years under your leadership?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. He called me. But I see it very good. I think that we're going to have a very good relationship. All we want is fairness. We just want a level playing field. We don't want to take advantage. We've been having massive deficits with China. Biden allowed it to get out of hand. He's—$1.1 trillion deficit. It's ridiculous, and it's just an unfair relationship.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have to make it just fair. We don't have to make it phenomenal. We have to make it a fair relationship. Right now it's not a fair relationship. The deficit is massive, as it is with other countries—a lot of Asian countries, actually. But we have deficits that are very big, and we can't keep doing that, so we're not going to keep doing that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I like President Xi very much. I've always liked him. We always had a very good relationship. It was very strained with COVID coming out of Wuhan. Obviously, that strained it. I'm sure it strained it with a lot of people, but that strained our relationship. But we always had a great relationship, I would say, and we look forward to doing very well with China and getting along with China.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Hopefully, China can help us stop the war with, in particular, Russia-Ukraine. And they have a great deal of power over that situation, and we'll work with them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I mentioned that with—during our phone conversation with President Xi, and hopefully we could work together and get that stopped.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We'd like to see denuclearization. In fact, with President Putin, prior to a—an election result, which was, frankly, ridiculous, we were talking about denuclearization of our two countries, and China would have come along. China has a—a much smaller, right now, nuclear armament than us or field than us, but they're—they're going to be catching it at some point over the next 4 or 5 years.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I will tell you that President Putin really liked the idea of cutting way back on nuclear. And I think the rest of the world, we would have gotten them to follow. And China would have come along too. China also liked it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Tremendous amounts of money are being spent on nuclear, and the destructive capability is something that we don't even want to talk about today, because you don't want to hear it. It's too depressing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we want to see if we can denuclearize, and I think that's very possible. And I can tell you that President Putin wanted to do it. He and I wanted to do it. We had a good conversation with China. They would have been involved, and that would have been an unbelievable thing for the planet.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I hope——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: Mr. Brende. Mr. President, when you're——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——it can be started up again.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: Mr. Brende. ——back here in Davos next year, will there be then a peace agreement with Ukraine and Russia by then?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, you're going to have to ask Russia. Ukraine is ready to—make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Just so you understand, this is a war that should have never started. If I were President, it would never have started. This is a war that should have never, ever been started. And it wasn't started during my—there was never even talk about it. I knew that it was the apple of President Putin's eye, but I also knew that there was no way he was going in, and he wasn't going to go in.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then, when I was out, bad things happened, bad things were said, a lot of stupidity all around, and you end up with what you have. Now you have all these bombed-out cities—they look like demolition sites—with many people killed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think the—the thing that you'll see about Ukraine is that far—far more people have died than is being reported. And I've seen that. But far, far more people have died.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When you look at a city that's become a demolition site, where big buildings have been collapsed by missiles hitting them and everything else, and they say, "One person was slightly injured." No, no, many people were killed. Those are big buildings. I was surprised at how—that was my business. These are buildings that go 2 and 3 blocks long. They're 20 stories high.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're big, powerful buildings. Then they were knocked down, and there were a lot of people in those buildings. They had announced that two people were injured. That's not true. So I think you're going to find that there were many more people killed in Ukraine and the Ukraine war than anybody has any idea.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But if you look now, so many of the people being killed are soldiers just facing each other with guns, rifles, and drones—the new form of warfare—drones. And it's a very sad thing to see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And when you see pictures of the fields that I see, nobody wants to see it. You'll never be the same.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: Mr. Brende. Thank you very much, Mr. President. On behalf of all the 3,000 participants here in Davos, we really, really underline that joining us, the third day in your Presidency, live, taking questions here, it's so appreciated. And we are already ready for receiving you next year in person.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mr. Brende
full_topic_context.text: So thank you very much, and all the best from Davos.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, do you think that sanctions on Russia will force President Putin to negotiate?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't know, but I think he should make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, welcome.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'd like to request a moment of silence for the victims and their families, please. [At this point, a moment of silence was observed.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I speak to you this morning in an hour of anguish for our Nation. Just before 9 p.m. last night, an American Airlines regional jet carrying 60 passengers and 4 crew collided with an Army Black Hawk helicopter carrying 3 military servicemembers over the Potomac River in Washington, DC, while on final approach to Reagan National Airport. Both aircraft crashed instantly and were immediately submerged into the icy waters of the Potomac. Real tragedy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The massive search and rescue mission was underway throughout the night, leveraging every asset at our disposal. And I have to say, the local, State, Federal, military—including the United States Coast Guard, in particular—they've done a phenomenal job. So quick. So fast. It was mobilized immediately.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The work has now shifted to a recovery mission. Sadly, there are no survivors.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This was a dark and excruciating night in our Nation's Capital and in our Nation's history, and a tragedy of terrible proportions. As one Nation, we grieve for every precious soul that has been taken from us so suddenly, and we are a country of—really, we are in mourning. This has really shaken a lot of people, including people, very sadly, from other nations who were on the flight.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: For the family members back in Wichita, Kansas, here in Washington, DC, and throughout the United States, and in Russia—we have a Russia contingence of very talented people unfortunately were on that plane—very, very, very sorry about that—whose loved ones were aboard the passenger jet, we can only begin to imagine the agony that you're all feeling. Nothing worse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: On behalf of the First Lady, myself, and 340 million Americans, our hearts are shattered, alongside yours, and our prayers are with you now and in the days to come. We'll be working very, very diligently in the days to come. We're here for you to wipe away the tears and to offer you our devotion, our love, and our support—there's great support.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In moments like this, the differences between Americans fade to nothing compared to the bonds of affection and loyalty that unite us all, both as Americans and even as nations. We are one family. And today we are all heartbroken. We're all searching for answers. That icy, icy Potomac—that was a cold, cold night, cold water.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're all overcome with the grief for many who have so tragically perished, who will no longer be with us. Together, we take solace that their journey ended not in the cold waters of the Potamic but in the warm embrace of a loving god.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We do not know what led to this crash, but we have some very strong opinions and ideas, and I think we'll probably state those opinions now, because over the years, I've watched as things like this happen and they say, "Well, we're always investigating." And then the investigation 3 years later—they announce it, "We think we have—have some pretty good ideas." But we'll find out how this disaster occurred, and we'll ensure that nothing like this ever happens again.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The FAA and the NTSB and the U.S. military will be carrying out a systematic and comprehensive investigation. Our new Secretary of Transportation, Sean Duffy—his second day on the job, when that happened—that's a rough one—will be working tirelessly. He's a great gentleman. A whole group is—these are great people, and they are working tirelessly to figure out exactly what happened. We'll—we will state certain opinions, however.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm also immediately appointing an Acting Commissioner to the FAA, Christopher Rocheleau, a 22-year veteran of the agency, highly respected. Christopher, thank you very much. Appreciate it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We must have only the highest standards for those who work in our aviation system. I changed the Obama standards from very mediocre at best to extraordinary—you remember that— only the highest aptitude; they have to be the highest intellect and psychologically superior people—were allowed to qualify for air traffic controllers. That was not so prior to getting there, when I arrived in 2016.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I made that change very early on because I always felt this was a job that—and other jobs, too—but this was a job that had to be superior intelligence. And we didn't really have that, and we had it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then when I left office and Biden took over, he changed them back to lower than ever before. I put safety first. Obama, Biden, and the Democrats put policy first. And they put politics at a level that nobody has ever seen, because this was the lowest level. Their policy was horrible, and their politics was even worse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, as you know, last week, long before the crash, I signed an Executive order restoring our highest standards for air traffic controllers and other important jobs throughout the country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So it was very interesting. About a week ago, almost upon entering office, I signed something last week that was an Executive order—a very powerful in restoring the highest standards of air traffic controllers—and others, by the way.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And my administration will set the highest possible bar for aviation safety. We have to have our smartest people. It doesn't matter what they look like, how they speak, who they are. It matters—intellect, talent—the word "talent." They have to be talented, naturally talented geniuses.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You can't have regular people doing that job. They won't be able to do it. But we'll restore faith in American air travel. I'll have more to say about that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I do want to point out that—various articles that appeared prior to my entering office, and here's one: the "FAA's diversity push includes focus on hiring people with 'severe intellectual' and 'psychiatric' disabilities." That is amazing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then it says, "FAA says people with 'severe' disabilities are most underrepresented segment of the workforce." And they want them in, and they want them—they can be air traffic controllers. I don't think so. This was a—in January 14, so that was a week before I entered office. They put a big push to put diversity into the FAA's program.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Then another article, "The Federal Aviation Administration"—this was before I got to office recently, the second term. "The FAA is actively recruiting workers who suffer 'severe intellectual'

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: disabilities, psychiatric problems, and other mental and physical conditions under a diversity and inclusion hiring initiative spelled out on the agency's website."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Can you imagine? These are people that are—I mean, actually, their lives are shortened because of the stress that they have. Brilliant people have to be in those positions, and their lives are actually shortened—very substantially shortened—because of the stress. When you have many, many planes coming into one target, and you need a very special talent and a very special genius to be able to do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: "'Targeted disabilities are those disabilities that the Federal Government, as a matter of policy, has identified for special emphasis in recruitment and hiring,' the FAA's website states. 'They include hearing, vision, missing extremities, partial paralysis, complete paralysis, epilepsy, severe intellectual disability, psychiatric disability, and dwarfism.'" All qualify for the position of a controller of airplanes pouring into our country, pouring into a little spot, a little dot on the map, a little runway.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: "The initiative is part of the FAA's 'Diversity and Inclusion' hiring plan." Think of that. "The initiative is part of the FAA's 'Diversity and Inclusion' hiring plan, which says 'diversity is integral to achieving FAA's mission of ensuring safe and efficient travel.'" I don't think so. I don't think so. I think it's just the opposite.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: "The FAA website shows that the agency's guidelines on diversity hiring were last updated on March 23 of '22." They wanted to make it ever more so, and then I came in. And I assume maybe this is the reason.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: "The FAA, which is overseen by Secretary Pete Buttigieg"—a real winner. That's a guy who's a real winner. Do you know how badly everything was run since he's run this Department of Transportation? He's a disaster. He was a disaster as a mayor. He ran his city into the ground. And he's a disaster now. He's just got a good line of bullshit. The "Department of Transportation is a government agency charged with regulating civil aviation." Well, he runs it—45,000 people—and he's run it right into the ground with his diversity. So I had to say that it's terrible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Then it's—"A group within the FAA"—another story—"determined that the workforce was too White," that they had "concerted efforts" to get the administration to change that and to change it immediately. This was in the Obama administration, just prior to my getting there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we took care of African Americans, Hispanic Americans. We took care of everybody at levels that nobody has ever seen before. It's one of the reasons I won.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But they actually came out with a directive: "too White." And we want the people that are competent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But now we mourn, and we pray. And I would like to ask all Americans to join me in a moment of silence as we ask God to watch over those who have lost their lives and bring comfort to the loved ones.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I just want to say God bless everyone in this room.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This has been a terrible very short period of time. We'll get to the bottom of it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we all saw the same thing. We've seen it many times. I've had the honor of hearing tapes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The tapes are scary—very scary tapes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You had a airliner coming in—American Airlines. He was doing everything right. He was on track. He used the same track as everybody else that came in. It's probably the same track as they've had for 25 years or more. He's coming in the path, and, for some reason, you had a helicopter that was at the same height—obviously, when they hit, but pretty much the same height and going at an angle that was unbelievably bad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When the air traffic controller said, "Do you see"—you know, he was talking about "Do you see him?" But there was very little time left when that was stated.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then, also, he said, "Follow him in." And then almost immediately after that—you know, seconds after that—there was the crash that took place. Well, you follow him in—that means, like, "Everything's fine. Follow him in."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You had a pilot problem from the standpoint of the helicopter—I mean, because it was visual. It was a very clear night. It was cold, but clear—and clear as you could be. The American Airlines plane had lights blazing. They had all their landing lights on.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I could see it from the Kennedy Center tape. We had a tape up on the Kennedy Center that seems to be the primary thus far. I'm sure we'll see other tapes, because it's such a—an area where there—lot of cameras—a lot of cameras looking up in space—into the air, into space. So, we'll probably see many other shots of it before too much time goes by.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we had a situation where you had a helicopter that had the ability to stop. I have helicopters. You can stop a helicopter very quickly. It had the ability to go up or down. It had the ability to turn.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the turn it made was not the correct turn, obviously, and it did somewhat the opposite of what it was told. We don't know that that would have been the difference, because the timing was so tight. It was so—it was so little—there was so little time to think.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But what you did have is, you had vision. The helicopter had vision of the plane, because you had vision of it all the way—perfect vision of it all the way from—at Kennedy Center, where the tape was taken. And for some reason, there weren't adjustments made.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Again, you could have slowed down the helicopter substantially. You could have stopped the helicopter. You could have gone up. You could have gone down. You could have gone straight up, straight down. You could have turned. You could have done a million different maneuvers.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: For some reason, it just kept going and then made a slight turn at the very end. And it was— by that time, it was too late.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They shouldn't have been at the same height, because if it wasn't the same height, you could have gone under it or over it. And nobody realized or they didn't say that it's at the same height. At the same height would—it would—still wouldn't have been great, but you would have missed it by quite a bit. It could have been a thousand feet higher. It could have been 200 feet lower. But it was exactly at the same height, and somebody should have been able to point that out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So all of this is going to be studied, but it just seems to me—from a couple of words that I like to use, the words "common sense." Some really bad things happened, and some things happened that shouldn't have happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So you had a helicopter going in identical direction. You had a helicopter that was at the exact same height as somebody going in essentially the opposite direction. You had a plane that was following a track, which is a track that every other plane followed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I don't imagine—I know I've heard today that they might have been following the preceding plane—which was pretty close, but not that close—the preceding plane. But you wouldn't have even been able to see that because of the direction that the helicopter was coming in at.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So you had a confluence of bad decisions that were made, and you have people that lost their lives—violently lost their lives.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're going to take a few questions. I'd like to ask our new Secretary of Transportation to say a few words—Sean Duffy, a great gentleman. Just started. It's not your fault. And I know you agree with me very strongly on intellect and even the psychological well-being of—of the air traffic controllers. Such an important position.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think I can't emphasize stronger: I changed it when I first ran. In 2016, I changed it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We had the highest standard that you could have. And then they changed it back—that was Biden—to a standard you just—I read it to you. That was from one of your papers—one of the people in this room actually wrote that. And then I changed it back a few days ago. And unfortunately, that was—we'll see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We don't know that necessarily it's even the controller's fault. But one thing we do know: There was a lot of vision, and people should have been able to see that—you know, at what point do you stop? At what point you say, "Wow, that plane is getting a little bit close"?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So this is a tragedy that should not have happened. Please, Sean.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy. Thank you, Mr. President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: And I would just note: The President's leadership has been remarkable during this crisis. We have had a whole-of-government response—local, State, Federal. And when you see that kind of cooperation, it begins with the leadership in this body. So thank you for that, Mr. President. You make our jobs a lot easier.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: You made an important point that when we deal with safety, we can only accept the best and the brightest in positions of safety that impact the lives of our loved ones, our family members.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: And I think you make a really important point on that, Mr. President. That is the motto of your Presidency: "The best and the brightest." The most intelligent coming into these spaces.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: I want to take a moment and extend my condolences to the families of the loved ones. We commit to them that we are going to get to the bottom of this investigation—not in 3 years, not in 4 years, but as quickly as possible—with the NTSB, who is here today, as well as the FAA.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: What happened yesterday shouldn't have happened. It should not have happened. And when Americans take off in airplanes, they should expect to land at their destination. That didn't happen yesterday. That's not acceptable.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: And so we will not accept excuses. We will not accept passing the buck. We are going to take responsibility at the Department of Transportation and the FAA to make sure we have the reforms that have been dictated by President Trump in place to make sure that these mistakes do not happen again.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Transportation Sean P. Duffy
full_topic_context.text: And, again, I want to thank you for your leadership, Mr. President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Duffy
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Duffy. And I appreciate the confidence you've placed in me.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. Pete, would you like to say something?

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth. Sure.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: Well, thank you, Mr. President. Again, I want to echo what the Transportation secretary said about your leadership. From the moment we found out about this, we were in contact with the White House trying to determine exactly what happened. I would echo as well: No excuses.

full_topic_context.text: We're going to get to the bottom of this.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: We, first and foremost, from the Defense Department, want to pass our condolences to the 64 souls and their families that were affected by this—never should have happened—and certainly, the three servicemembers, the three soldiers—a young captain, a staff sergeant, and a CW2—chief warrant officer—on a routine, annual retraining of night flights on a standard corridor for a continuity of government mission.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: The military does dangerous things. It does routine things on the regular basis. Tragically, last night, a mistake was made. And I think the President is right. full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: But I want to echo what the Transportation Secretary and you, Mr. President, said, because it pertains to the DOD as well: We will have the best and brightest in every position possible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: As you said in your Inaugural, it is color-blind and merit-based—the best leaders possible, whether it's flying Black Hawks, flying airplanes, leading platoons, or in Government. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. J.D., please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance

full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, thank you very much, everybody. We have a lot of big signings, good signings—one, in particular, which we'll save for the end. And I'll ask Will to go over these individually, and we can see how we do.

full_topic_context.text: White House Staff Secretary William O. Scharf. Yes, sir. First for your review, we have 56 subcabinet-level appointments. This includes, probably most notably, seven Ambassador appointments. Those will be the first Ambassadors, I believe, that you've——

full_topic_context.text: The President. Right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. ——transmitted to the Senate.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, the President signed the appointments document.] Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Second, we have acting designations. We're actually designating Doug Collins to be the acting leader of both the Office of Special Counsel and the Office of Government Ethics.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President signed the designation document.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You know Doug, everybody, I think. He was in charge of the fake impeachment hearings—remember? That I won very conclusively—fake charges by the radical- left Democrats.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Next, sir, the—the Federal Executive Institute is a program that was set up during the Johnson administration to train senior-level government bureaucrats. As you've identified repeatedly in the last few years, the senior levels of our Federal Government are not adequately serving as stewards of taxpayer dollars, so we're recommending zeroing out that program, effectively.
