full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President signed an Executive order titled, "Eliminating the Federal Executive Institute."]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We're actually getting rid of a few programs that are just a waste—just really a waste.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Next, we have an Executive order relating to the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. As you have repeatedly identified, the way that this act has been enforced over the years has been devastating to American business opportunities and business competitiveness abroad. We are essentially ordering the Department of Justice to use its prosecutorial discretion in a way to ameliorate the negative effects of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act to allow Americans to do business abroad and to allow our foreign partners to do business with Americans without fearing unjust prosecution.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And for those of you that know this, it turned out to be—it sounds good on paper, but in practicality, it's a disaster. It means that if an American goes over to a foreign country and starts doing business over there—legally, legitimately, or otherwise—it's almost a guaranteed investigation, indictment. And nobody wants to do business with the Americans because of it. Nobody wants to do business.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They say: "Look, we can deal with China. They can do whatever they want. We can deal with Russia. We can deal with anybody, and we have a normal life. You deal with America, the FBI gets over there. They don't investigate death and murders on the street in New York and Los Angeles. They—they go over and investigate a business guy trying to do business."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So it made it very, very hard, from a practical standpoint, to make deals. They want to deal with the Americans, but they don't want to be under investigation every time they speak to an American, every time an American makes a phone call to somebody in a different country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's a disaster for this country, and the—I guess it was a Jimmy Carter concept. And it sounds so good, but it's so bad. It hurts the country. And many, many deals are unable to be made because of it. Nobody wants to do business because they don't want to feel like every time they pick up a phone, they're going to jail.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we'll sign this. And it takes courage to sign it, because you only get bad publicity when you sign it. It sounds so nice. The title is so lovely. But it's an absolutely horror show for America. So we're signing it because that's what we have to do to make it good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President signed an Executive order titled, "Pausing Foreign Corrupt Practices Act Enforcement To Further American Economic and National Security."]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay? Thank you. That's an important one. It's going to mean a lot more business for America. Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Next, this is an Executive order relating to the use of paper straws. As you've consistently identified, nobody really likes paper straws.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Number one trending. [Laughter] Can you believe it, a paper straw? It was number one trending for 3 days or something.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. The environmental impact of plastic straws versus paper straws is entirely unclear. This has cost both the Government and private industry an absolute ton of money and left consumers all over the country wildly dissatisfied with their straws.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: So we're asking aspects of—of the Federal Government, Federal departments and agencies, to look at their existing procurement processes, and we're asking your Domestic Policy Council to look holistically at this issue, to address it. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We're going back to plastic straws. These things don't work. I've had them many times, and, on occasion, they break. They explode. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going back to plastic straws. I think it's okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President signed an Executive order titled, "Ending Procurement and Forced Use of Paper Straws."]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I don't think that plastic is going to affect a shark very much as they're eating—as they're munching their way through the ocean. [Laughter] Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf
full_topic_context.text: Staff Secretary Scharf. Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Staff Secretary Scharf

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. And today, we're delighted to swear in our next Director of National Intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard. Most of you know Tulsi. She's a fantastic woman.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Tulsi, I want to just congratulate you; your husband, Abraham; your sister; and all of your friends—a lot of friends here. You have a lot of friends. I noticed that, huh?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. I'm grateful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They were all fighting—fighting for you. It worked out very well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Tulsi Gabbard is an American of extraordinary courage and exceptional patriotism. She has devoted her entire life to public service, and I've watched her for years on different shows and everything. I said, "She's a woman of great common sense." And, you know, we like the common sense. It's a word that's being used a lot. I think we started it, in terms of politics. But it's a word that's used a lot. It's usually pretty effective too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you really are. I've watched you even on "Larry King." You know, you're very young. I don't know how you were on "Larry King"—[laughter]—but you're very young. But you were. And you always had—you always had the situation covered properly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: At 21 years old, Tulsi became the youngest woman ever elected to the Hawaii State Legislature. After 9/11, she joined the Hawaii Army National Guard and deployed abroad three times and highly respected by everybody. So many people writing in letters saying she was so exceptional, even then.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She continues to serve as a Lieutenant Colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve. And Tulsi also served four terms in the United States House of Representatives, where she was a member of the House Armed Services Committee.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She is a former vice chair of the National Democratic Party. Can you believe that? And— and here she is. That's very nice. [Laughter] We have a few of them and—but she was never a Democrat. She was at—at heart, she was—[laughter]—she was a Republican. I—watched her. And was a 2020 Democrat candidate for President of the United States.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's not easy, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. No.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It's not so easy. [Laughter] People think it's easy. It's not easy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Throughout her service, Tulsi has always distinguished herself as a leader of the highest caliber. She's earned the respect and admiration, the love of Americans on both sides of the aisle, as her profound commitment to the values that keep us free—and she really does have those values as much as anybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In recent years, Tulsi has been a courageous and often lonely voice speaking out against radical left's attacks on free speech and the dangers of an unelected deep state.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I have to say, she was very, very strong for me when I was going through all of the— the fake news and all of the—the problems that we had with some very sick people. She was

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: always out there. Before I really knew her, as well, she was out there defending me. So, I appreciated that, Tulsi.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But the threat of a warmongering military-industrial complex and the weaponization of Government and governmental people that go out and persecute—they like to persecute people that are innocent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Tulsi herself became a target of that weaponization when she was outrageously placed on a suspected terrorist watch list by the Biden regime—it was a very evil regime—after criticizing their appalling abuses of power.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'm confident that as Director of the National Intelligence, Tulsi will work tirelessly to keep America safe. And she's been doing that her entire career. I think it's going to be a very natural day for you when you walk in. It's—just have to keep the way you are. Just stay the way you are.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She'll be clear-eyed, and she'll be focused on the threat of radical Islamic terrorism and—and lots of other threats, too, threats from within—and give no quarter to America's foreign enemies.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: At the same time, I'm entrusting Tulsi with the responsibility of overseeing urgently needed reforms to the U.S. intelligence community to protect the rights and the civil liberties of all Americans.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She'll provide the American people with transparency, eliminate corruption, shrink the bloated bureaucracy, and restore honesty, integrity, and trust to the national security state.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's only one thing I can say: that there's nobody like her for this job. This was a very easy one for me. She was recommended by some of the top people in that world. It's a little world. You know, it's a little, smart world. It sometimes can be an evil world when the wrong people are there, but we have the right one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She's had so many great recommendations. I would say Pam was right up there with her— Pam Bondi. She had a lot of—a lot—she—I didn't need—I know her a little bit better, and you're doing a fantastic job after about 3 or 4 days, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Pamela J. Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Pamela J. Bondi. Thank you—[inaudible].

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You've had—you've had a lot of experience, but you've never seen anything like this, Pam. But you're going to do fantastic as the Attorney General—fantastic. So, thank you, and congratulations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We did this with Pam a few days ago. And this is, again, my honor. So, congratulations to Tulsi, and I think Pam is going to administer the—oath. And when she does that, I'll sign your new certificate.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Good. Thank you. Thank you very much, everybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. Stand right there. All right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Please place your left hand on the Constitution and raise your right hand and repeat after me. I do solemnly swear.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. I, Tulsi Gabbard, do solemnly swear.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. That I will support and defend the Constitution of the United States.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. That I will support and defend the Constitution of the United States.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. Against all enemies, foreign and domestic.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. Against all enemies, foreign and domestic.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. And that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the same.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. And that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the same.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. That I take this obligation freely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. I take this obligation freely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. Without any mental reservation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. Without any mental reservation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. Or purpose of evasion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. Or purpose of evasion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. And that—and that I will well and faithfully.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. That I will well and faithfully.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. Discharge the duties of the office on which I am about to enter.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. Discharge the duties of the office on which I am about to enter.

full_topic_context.speaker: Attorney General Bondi
full_topic_context.text: Attorney General Bondi. So help me, God.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. So help me, God. Attorney General Bondi. Congratulations. The President. Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: How is the Oval Office looking? [Laughter] A little different look, right? It's the Oval Office.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Busy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Okay. We'll get a good one here. [At this point, the President signed the certificate.] Okay. Not bad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Ready? I'll stand up there. I think we'll do it right here. Come on over here, Abraham.

full_topic_context.speaker: Cinematographer Abraham Williams
full_topic_context.text: Cinematographer Abraham Williams. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President, Director Gabbard, and her husband Abraham Williams posed for a photograph.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Okay. I'm sure there are no questions. [Laughter] [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, when and where will you meet with Vladimir Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You know what? I'd like to have—let Tulsi say a few words first, then we can answer a couple of questions. Okay? Good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. Mr. President, first and foremost, I just want to say thank you from the bottom of my heart for the trust that you have placed in me to fulfill this critical position as Director of National Intelligence—at any time, but specifically during this time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Unfortunately, the American people have very little trust in the intelligence community, largely because they've seen the weaponization and politicization of an entity that is supposed to be purely focused on ensuring our national security.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. So, I look forward to being able to help fulfill that mandate that the American people delivered to you very clearly in this election to refocus our intelligence community by empowering the great patriots who have chosen to serve our country in this way and focus on ensuring the safety, security, and freedom of the American people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: As you've said, Mr. President, this is what I've dedicated my life to, and it is truly humbling to be in this position, to serve in your administration, help to rebuild that trust, and ultimately to keep the American people safe.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: Last thing I'll mention that, in your National Prayer Breakfast speech, you made a statement about your legacy of wanting to be remembered as a peacemaker. I know that I can speak for many of my fellow service members who are here today, veterans, Medal of Honor recipients, how deeply that resonates with us, for those who volunteer to put their lives on the line when duty calls, but to have a President and Commander-in-Chief who recognizes the cost of that sacrifice and ensuring that war is the last resort, not the first. So, thank you for your leadership.

full_topic_context.speaker: Director Gabbard
full_topic_context.text: On behalf of my friends here and all who wear the uniform, we're grateful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. Thank you, Tulsi.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: Director Gabbard. Thank you. The President. Congratulations. Director Gabbard. Thank you. The President. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. President Trump, thank you. When and where do you plan on meeting with Vladimir Putin? And were there any preconditions set to agree to this meeting?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, we had a great call, and it lasted for a long time—over an hour this morning. I also had, with President Zelenskyy, a very good call after that, and I think we're on the way to getting peace. I think President Putin wants peace, and President Zelenskyy wants peace, and I want peace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I just want to see people stop getting killed. We're very far away from that particular war, but that's a vicious war, probably a million and a half soldiers killed in a short period of time. I've never seen anything—I have pictures that are—you wouldn't believe it. You wouldn't believe what you have to look at: young, beautiful soldiers that are just being decimated.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it would be nice to end it immediately. But we had a very good talk with—people didn't really know what President Putin's thoughts were, but I think I can say with great confidence he wants to see it ended also. That's—good. And we're going to work toward getting it ended and as fast as possible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's—a horrible situation going over—it's flat land, and the bullet goes off, and the only thing it can hit is a body—a human body—a young human body. And they're losing just tremendous numbers of mostly soldiers. The—cities and towns have been largely demolished.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's a shame what's happened to that country. It would have never happened if I were President. That, I can tell you. It would have never happened. It's—to look at that—and October 7th would have never happened, either, by the way. Middle East.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we'll get it—I think we'll get it—we'll get something done. We're going to be meeting— actually, tomorrow, they're meeting in Munich, as you know, and we're going to have some other meetings.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we'll be—I'll be dealing with President Putin, largely on the phone, and we ultimately expect to meet. In fact, we expect that he'll come here, and I'll go there, and we're going to meet——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/U.S. Diplomatic Efforts

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——also, probably in Saudi Arabia. The first time, we'll meet in Saudi Arabia, see if we get something done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we want to end that war. That war is a disaster. It's a really bloody, horrible war.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, did you—[inaudible]——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Just to check, you said you'd make Saudi Arabia your—the first meeting will happen. Is that——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think so.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We think we're going to probably meet in Saudi Arabia, the first meeting.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Any idea when?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Hasn't been set, but not-too-distant future.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Did you also commit——

full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And will Zelenskyy be part of that meeting or——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We both understand—you know, we—we know the Crown Prince, and I think it'd be a—it'd be a very good place to meet.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So, it sounds like that would just be a meeting between you and Putin and perhaps the Crown Prince, but not President Zelenskyy. Is that right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Probably we'll have a first meeting, and then we'll see what we can do about the second meeting.

full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. President Zelenskyy said today, Mr. President, that—they received your vision. What is your plan for—to end this war? Like, today, Secretary Hegseth——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I'm not going to tell you my plan. I can just tell you we've made a lot of progress. We worked on it for 2 weeks.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: He was a—a fine man, and he was in there for 3½, almost 4 years, and they weren't able to do a thing, and I got him out. And as you know, I didn't pay $6 billion. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think long before President Putin, they said there's no way they'd allow that. This has been going on for many, many years. They—they've been saying that for a long time that Ukraine cannot go into NATO. And——

full_topic_context.text: Q. Was the call with——

full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.text: that?

full_topic_context.text: Q. He—if the war were to end, he says he wants guarantees of security.

full_topic_context.text: The President. We'll see what that means. We have—I think when the war ends—one thing he was very strong about, he wants—if it ends, he wants it to end. And that's—President Putin said that. He wants it to end. He doesn't want to end it and then go back to fighting 6 months later.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We talked about the possibility—I mentioned it—of a ceasefire so we can stop the killing. And I think we'll probably end up, at some point, getting a ceasefire in the not-too-distant future.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you view Ukraine as an equal member of this peace process?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. That's an interesting question.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think they have to make peace. Their people are being killed, and I think they have to make peace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would you support Zelenskyy ceding territory or exchanging territory in any agreement to end the war?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, he's going to have to do what he has to do, but, you know, his poll numbers aren't particularly great, to put it mildly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: He's got a country where, you know, it's been savaged and attacked. And he's got an army that's been very, very brave, actually, despite the fact that—you know, we've given them, in my opinion, $350 billion—that's what the real number is. You don't hear that number. And Europe has given, in my opinion, a hundred billion dollars, and they've done it in the form of a loan.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I have a Secretary of Treasury right now who's actually quite brave. He's over in Ukraine on a train, and there's a lot of things happening around that train that aren't so good. And he's going there to get a document done where we're going to be in—assured that we're going to, in some form, get this money back, because we're putting up far more money than Europe, and Europe is in far more danger than we are. We have an ocean in between. Europe has nothing in between.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So, does that mean——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You what they have in between? They have Ukraine in between.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Does that mean——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So—wait a minute. So, as you know, Europe is putting up money, and they're getting it in the form of a loan. And the United States, under Biden, didn't do loans. They just handed money. Every time somebody walked in from Ukraine, they just handed them money foolishly. This should have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It should have never started, and once it did, other things should have happened, other things should have taken place.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Does that mean you are not sending any more aid to Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, we are, but we want it secured, and the money is going to be secured.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, I mean, Russia did invade Ukraine——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When would the U.S. stop Ukraine funding?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When would the U.S. stop sending funding?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Because if we didn't do that, then Putin would say he won. We're the thing that's holding it back, and, frankly, we'll go as long as we have to go, because we're not going to let the other happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But President Putin wants to have peace now, and that's good. And he didn't want to have peace with Biden.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Was that conversation with Putin part of——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Just—sir, just to be clear——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And you tell me why that is. Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Release of Marc Fogel

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Was that conversation with Putin to start these negotiations part of the deal to bring Fogel home?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, but it was a—a nice thing that he allowed Marc Fogel to leave.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In fact, Marc is—wasn't feeling well, but he was—all of a sudden, about 2 weeks ago, he started being treated very nicely. He said they took him out for haircuts. They took him out— they—they helped him out a little bit and made him feel better, made him look better, and they were nice to him. And he said, "I saw—something happening." And it had to—it coincided with when I came into office.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Well——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So, that was nice.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And—he was—he's a fine person. He was so happy to be out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What does make you——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. He was there—he was there for 3½ years plus, and he shouldn't have been there at all. He should have—they should have had him out much faster than that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What does make you believe that Zelenskyy will agree with that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, just to be clear, do you see any future in which——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Wait.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Go ahead, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sorry. Sir, just to be clear, do you see any future in which Ukraine returns to its pre— 2014 borders?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well—well, I think Pete said today that that's unlikely, right? It certainly would seem to be unlikely. They took a lot of land, and they fought for that land, and they lost a lot of—they lost a lot of soldiers. But it would just seem to me—and I'm not—I'm not making an opinion on it, but I've read a lot on it, and a lot of people think that that's unlikely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Some of it will come back. I think some of it will come back. Yes, some of that land will come back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Because these—Mr. President, these are——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So, what does make you believe Zelenskyy will agree to your vision?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Ultimately, these are both Russia's key——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Who—who are you with?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sorry, me?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. AFP, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You're who?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. AFP, Agence France-Presse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I just wanted to ask you, you—the—things that the Secretary of Defense was talking about, the 2014 borders and the lack of NATO membership—ultimately, these are both demands that Russia has made in the past. Is there not a danger of handing Russia a, kind of, win on this?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And what does make you believe Zelenskyy will agree with that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I think that if you look at the war—the way the war is going, you'll have to make your own determination.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm just here to try and get peace. I don't care so much about anything other than I want to stop having millions of people killed—killed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Last night, you know, Kyiv got hit very, very hard.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I want to see people stop getting killed. That war is ridiculous. It should have never happened, and it would have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, a couple of more questions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Oh, thank you, sir. Two questions. One on Ukraine again, and then another one on the Kennedy Center. Do you think that by—as far as your negotiating tactics go, did Pete Hegseth take away some of your negotiating abilities with Putin by taking Ukraine sovereign integrity off the table, by taking membership in Ukraine off the table?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, I haven't done that. I'm backing Ukraine. I'm—I'm backing Ukraine.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Don't say that. I'm approving. But I do want security for our money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, Europe is getting security. You know that, right? They're giving their money in the form of a loan. Nobody knows that. And why are we at $350 billion and Europe, which doesn't separate with an ocean like we do—we have a little thing called an ocean in between— why is it that Europe is paying $200 billion less than us to help Ukraine? Very similar size.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If you add up all the European countries, it's a little bit smaller than the U.S. in terms of the economy. Why is it that they're not paying the kind of numbers that they should be paying?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then on top of it, and I've been saying this to Biden—I told Biden, I said, "You ought to be asking for either a loan or some kind of a security, like their oil and gas or something, for the money, because you're putting up much more money than Europe and you have no security." Europe's putting up a much smaller amount, and it's in the form of a loan, because we have people that were incompetent in the last administration—grossly incompetent. And we're changing it, but we change it, and we—all we do is we get hit by lawsuits from the radical left all the time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But here we are. We stand. And I guess we've done okay. Thank you very much, everybody. Thank you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: Canada-U.S. Trade Relations

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. How are negotiations going with Canada? There was obviously a delay in implementing——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——those tariffs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——I spoke to Governor Trudeau on numerous occasions—[laughter]—and we'll see what happens. But it just sets up so good for them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Look, the people would pay much less tax than they're paying right now. They'd have perfect military protection. They don't have any military protection because they essentially—because— and you take a look at what's going on out there: You have Russian ships, you have China ships—you have Chinese ships, you have a lot of ships out there, and, you know, people are in danger. This is a different world today. It's a different world. They need our protection.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.text: Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You had that major call yesterday with President Putin of Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. President Zelenskyy responded today, basically saying any agreements they won't accept unless they're made with Ukraine. Will Ukraine have a seat at that table for those negotiations, in your view?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Of course, they would. I mean, they're part of it. We would have Ukraine. We'd have Russia, and we'll have other people involved too—a lot of people, a lot of—a lot of forks in the—a lot of forks in this game. I'll tell you what, this is a very interesting situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But the Ukraine war has to end. The young people are being killed at levels that nobody's seen since World War II, and it's a ridiculous war, and it has to end.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We had a good talk with President Putin. I had a good talk with President Zelenskyy—very good talk. And somebody said, oh, I should have called Zelenskyy first. I don't think so. I mean, we have to find out whether or not Russia wants to make a deal. I know that Zelenskyy wants to make a deal because he told me that. But I now know that Russia wants to make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Did you ask Secretary Hegseth to walk back his comments yesterday, saying Ukraine won't join NATO and won't go back to pre-2014 borders——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——because those are——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——bargaining chips you could use?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, I didn't. Somebody told me to, but I thought his comments were good yesterday, and they're probably good today. They're a little bit softer, perhaps, but I thought his comments from——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is that at your direction?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I thought his comments yesterday were pretty accurate.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't see any way that a country in Russia's position could allow them—just in their position—could allow them to join NATO. I don't see that happening.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, are——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And long before President Putin, Russia was very strong on the fact that—I believe that's the reason the war started, because Biden went out and said that they could join NATO, and he shouldn't have said that. As soon as he said that, I said: "You know what? You're going to have a war now." And I was right about that. That—this is a war that would have never happened if I were President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But you don't think it's—you think it's President Biden's fault, not President Putin? I mean, he's the one who invaded.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think Biden is incompetent. And I think when he said that they could join NATO, I thought that was a very stupid thing to say. I thought when he said, "Well, it depends if

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: it's a minor incursion"—in other words, it's okay if Russia does a minor incursion—I thought that was a very foolish thing to say.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on auto——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would Elon Musk——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Those things got it started.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On MAHA——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. The other thing that got it started was how badly Milley and these stupid people—the bad generals—how badly they did with Afghanistan. I was going to pull out, but we were pulling out with dignity and strength, and we were going to take our equipment with us and everything else. They are—I mean, what they're doing is—what they did with that—I think Putin looked at that mess, and he said: "Wow, this is a great time. I'm going to go in."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But what—what the Americans said—I'm not blaming Americans, but I will say what they said had a big influence on his deciding to go in.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, on Ukraine, when Putin says that he really wants peace, do you believe him?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, I do. I believe he wants peace. I believe that President Putin, when I spoke to him yesterday—I mean, I know him very well. Yes, I think he wants peace. I think he would tell me if he didn't.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you trust him?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think he'd—I'd like to see peace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you trust President Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I believe that—yes, I believe that he would like to see something happen. I trust him on this subject. I think he'd like to see something happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think it could have happened a long time ago. I think Biden—number one, it shouldn't have started, but it did. And now all those cities are knocked down. They're like demolition sites.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But Putin knocked them down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. All those beautiful golden towers are knocked down. There's nothing going to replace them. But much more importantly, you lost millions of people—a lot of soldiers, but you lost millions of people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When they knocked down those cities—and they're all laying down on the side; they're lying down just in ashes and all crumbled-up concrete—they literally look like a world-class demolition site. And many of them—almost all of them, but many of them—and this should have been done by Biden years ago. This should have never been allowed to happen. I know he's a friend of yours.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But couldn't Putin just withdraw his troops today?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. He's a friend of CNN. [Laughter] That's why nobody watches CNN anymore, because they have no—no credibility.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On China, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.] The President. Who else? Yes, please.

full_topic_context.text: Russia/U.S. Diplomatic Efforts

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And do you expect the Russians and President Putin to attend the summit in Saudi Arabia?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Eventually, yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Not quite yet. It's a little early.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're having a meeting in Munich tomorrow. Russia is going to be there with our people. Ukraine is also invited, by the way. I'm not sure exactly who's going to be there from any country. But high-level people from Russia, from Ukraine, and from the United States going to be there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What's your message to Wall Street about the tariffs, sir?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Group of Seven (G–7) Nations

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you want to add Russia back to the G–7, sir?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I'd love to have them back. I think it was a mistake to throw them out. Look, it's not a question of liking Russia or not liking Russia. It was the G–8, and, you know, I've—I said: "What are you doing? You guys—all you talk about is Russia, and you—they should be sitting at the table."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think Putin would love to be back. Obama and a couple of other people made a mistake, and they got Russia out. It's very possible that if that was the G–8, you wouldn't have had the problem with Ukraine. And if I was President, you definitely wouldn't have had the problem with Ukraine. Russia would have never attacked Ukraine. But——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Can I ask you one on—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. But you ask a very good question—the G–8. It used to be the G–8, and then these people threw them out. And I was arguing with Trudeau and with—with—numerous of the people. Actually, Prime Minister Abe, a great man from Japan, agreed with me a 100 percent, and some of the others did too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I got there, it was the G–7, as you know. They—they had already been terminated. I think it would have been very helpful and it still would be helpful to have Russia be a part of that mix.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So they——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Russia——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And I think if they were, I don't think you would have had the problem that you have right now.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Russia is not a part of the G–20.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. They kicked them out, of course, because—they kicked them out, of course, because they illegally annexed Crimea. I mean, how would you have responded if Russia invaded or took over——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, you know——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——land that wasn't theirs?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——took Crimea during Obama.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Twenty-fourteen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They took—they took—well, now they're looking to take the whole thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Then they took a big chunk of land and people, as you know, during Bush. And now they're trying to take the whole thing during Biden. You know, the only one that didn't give them anything is Trump. They never took anything with Trump—nothing, not two inches of property, of—of land.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But they had—Crimea was Obama, and then Bush gave them a lot, you remember. And then, in fact, this is a sort of a standard little phrase—and Biden is giving them everything, because this is a war that shouldn't have been had. And the only one that didn't give him anything is Trump. It's just the way is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Tariffs/2024 Presidential Election

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What's your message to Wall Street about these tariffs, sir? There's been some nervousness on Wall Street about the impact——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't think so. I mean, there hasn't been very much, and I think it's going to make the United States stronger. And in many ways, it could make other countries stronger too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, other countries want to have a strong United States. They want to have a strong America. And I think it's going to make us very, very strong—much stronger.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have a lot of work we're doing on the military. Our military—already, I've authorized some contracts to be built that are very substantial. We're building the greatest equipment to do it. We have the greatest military equipment in the world. We're building it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: At some point, when things settle down, I'm going to meet with China and I'm going to meet with Russia—in particular, those two—and I'm going to say: "There's no reason for us to be spending almost a trillion dollars on military. There's no reason for you to be spending $400 billion." China is going to be at $400 billion. We're at a trillion—we're going to be at close to a trillion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. If Elon Musk——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And I'm going to say, "We can settle this on—we can spend this on other things. We don't have to spend this on military, because"—and I'm going to be meeting with China. You know, we were trying to de-escalate nuclear. And I was in a position where Russia had agreed and China had agreed we were going to start, and then we had a rigged election, so that never took place.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But this one was too big to rig. We won by so much that it was too big to rig.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/China

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You want to do the China meeting in the United States? Or would you travel to China for

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. For what?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. The China meeting. Would you do that here or there?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I tell people all the time, you know, the question is: "Who's going to have the

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: first meeting? Where you're going to"—I say this to Putin, to President Xi. I say to everybody. It never bothered me. You know, I'm willing to say, "I'll go first." It doesn't matter. It's the end result that counts, so it doesn't make any difference.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When do you want to have a conversation about global defense spending? You, China, Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I'd like to have that—as soon as things settle down, I'm going to have that conference, primarily with China and Russia, because those are the two that—that really are out there. And we're going to have them spend a lot less money, and we're going to spend a lot less money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I know they're going to do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you see that happening——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They agreed to it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We were talking about—denuclearize, and President Putin and I agreed that we were going to do it in a very big way.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's no reason for us to be building brandnew nuclear weapons. We already have so many, you could destroy the world 50 times over—100 times over.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And here we are building new nuclear weapons, and they're building nuclear weapons, and China is building new nuclear weapons. And China is trying to catch up, because, you know, they're very substantially behind, but within 5 or 6 years, they'll be even. And we're all spending a lot of money that we could be spending on other things that are actually, hopefully, much more productive.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Hopefully, there'll never be a time when we need those weapons. If there's ever a time when we need nuclear weapons, like the kind of weapons that we're building and that Russia has and that China has to a lesser extent but will have—that's going to be a very sad day. That's going to be probably oblivion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you see that as separate conversations——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you see that as a trilateral negotiation?

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——or do you see one giant summit with you, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, I could see that. Let things calm down a little bit.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, when I left, we had no Middle East problem. We had no Russia going into Ukraine. They never would have done it. Putin never would have done it. And I came back, and we got, like, the whole world is blowing up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, when we straighten it all out, then I want to have—one of the first meetings I want to have is with President Xi of China, President Putin of Russia. And I want to say, "Let's cut our military budget in half." And we can do that—and I think we——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: ——and I think we'll be able to do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/China

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You know, I'm just wondering about your conversations on defense spending. Would you want to do that as a trilateral, or would you use the existing body that also already includes China and Russia, the G–20?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, I—no, it's the people. It's President Putin, President Xi. I don't need bodies. I don't need anything. It's people. It's all about people. It's about relationship and people. And you know, I've had a good relationship with President Putin. I've had a good relationship with President Xi. It's about people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think when things straighten out, which I hope will be in the not-too-distant future, the meeting I want to have first is a meeting with China and a meeting with Russia on slowing down, stopping, and reducing nuclear weapons, in particular, and also on not having to spend the kind of money we're all spending on weapons—military weapons, generally.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I think my question is: Would you have those meetings separately with each of those leaders, or would you try to bring them all together?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/China/2024 Presidential Election

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Both. You start off separately, and—yes. That's what was happening. I was dealing with President Putin. We had, really, an understanding where we were going to denuclearize—what a beautiful term that is, right?—"denuclearize." What a great thing if we could do that. And, well, we were going to. He really liked the idea, and so did I. And we had then called China, and China was very open to it. And then the COVID hit, and then we had a rigged election.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. But now there's no rigged election. Now we have an election that was too big to rig. That's what—my whole theme was "too big to rig." And they tried, but they didn't pull it off.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, as part of the reciprocal tariffs, would you also direct agencies to study the impact they would have on prices in the U.S.?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, there's nothing to study. There's nothing to study. It's going to go well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You—the United States is going to become a very, very strong economic—economically— country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Tariffs

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, in the past, you have spoken against BRICS. India is part of BRICS. Do you want to dismantle BRICS? Or you want to be—U.S. want to be part of the BRICS?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I don't care, but BRICS is—was put there for a bad purpose, and most of those people don't want—they don't even want to talk about it now. They're afraid to talk about it, because I told them, if—if they want to play games with the dollar, then they're going to be hit with a 100-percent tariff the day they mention that they want to do it. And they will come back and say, "We beg you—we beg you not to do this."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: BRICS is dead since I mentioned that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But what——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. BRICS died the minute I mentioned that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I know—I remember when Obama and—Biden, in particular, I guess he said that, "Oh, they have us over a barrel." They don't have us over a barrel. We have them over a barrel.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If BRICS wants to play games, those countries won't trade with us, we won't trade with them, and if any trading gets through, it will be 100-percent tariff at least.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On your Cabinet, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What will be your——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And you know what? When they hear that, what do you think they're going to do? They're going to say, "Look what happened to BRICS." They don't even want to talk about it. They don't—they don't even want to admit that they were a member of BRICS. That's what's happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. How soon will you lift the sanctions on Russia, sir?
