full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, thank you very much, everyone. Great honor to be here with my friend.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm delighted to welcome President Macron back to the White House. We've been together quite often, but not that often in the White House. We honored the President, First Lady of France not so long ago. That was a beautiful evening, and we will not soon forget it. That was a beautiful day and evening and many fond memories.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I also want to thank Emmanuel for hosting me in Paris last December after a historic election win to witness the reopening of the spectacular Notre Dame Cathedral, where you did an outstanding job in bringing it back together. That was a sad day, watching that burn. And 5 years later, you had it up, and it was, they say, more beautiful than it was before. So I think that's a great achievement. That was not easy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: France is America's oldest ally. Our cherished partnership has been a force for freedom, prosperity, and peace from the very beginning. We're now working on some very interesting developments—one, in particular, as you know, the war between Russia and Ukraine.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In the American Revolution, French support helped us to seize our destiny as an independent nation. In the first and second World Wars, our citizens shed blood together on the battlefields of Europe. And I'll never forget joining President Macron 6 years ago on the 75th anniversary of D- Day. That was some day.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The purpose of our meeting today is to end another battle, a really horrible one—a war, something that we haven't seen since the Second World War—that is ravaging European soil. The deadliest and most destructive conflict that one can imagine. I've seen the pictures. I've seen the satellite photos and—and lots of other photos, and it's a horrible thing that's happening.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thousands of people are dying a week.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This very day is the third anniversary of the invasion of Ukraine, which would never have happened if I was President. That was not going to happen. The horrors of this gruesome and bloody war can scarcely be overestimated. Hundreds of thousands of people—Russians and Ukrainians, in particular—have needlessly died. An entire generation of Ukrainians and Russian men has been decimated. One-thousand-year-old cities have been turned into rubble. Those beautiful spires that you used to see there—they were the most beautiful in the world, they say— are lying in heaps of rubble, blasted to smithereens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's time to end this bloodletting and restore peace, and I think we're going to do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We've had some great conversations, including with Russia. Since my return to the White House, we've made more progress toward that goal in 1 month than occurred in the past 3 years.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I've spoken with both President Putin and President Zelenskyy. And, again, a lot of—a lot of good things toward peace are happening, moving it, I think, pretty quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, National Security Adviser Michael Waltz, and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff conducted successful talks in Saudi Arabia with the delegation from Russia, and I'd like to thank the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the King and Muhammad. Great people. They're really working hard to get this done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our focus is on achieving a cease-fire as soon as possible and ultimately a permanent peace. My meeting with President Macron today was another important step forward in that—well, that sphere, because he's been very much involved, right from the beginning, on trying to get it over with, and we're going to get it done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I believe that Emmanuel agrees with me on many of the most important issues. Chief among them is, this is the right time. It may be the only time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, that's a very interesting and horrible situation, and that could evolve into a third world war. We're not going to let that happen. It should have never started, but it did, and what a mess. What a horrible, bloody mess.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm also pleased that President Macron agrees that the cost and burden of securing the peace must be borne by the nations of Europe, not alone by the United States. And Europe must take that central role in assuring long-term security of Ukraine, which they want to do. And that's not a very big step. A big step is what's going to happen over the next few weeks.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The United States has put up far more aid for Ukraine than any other nation, hundreds of billions of dollars. We've spent more than $300 billion, and Europe has spent about $100 billion. That's a big difference. And at some point, we should equalize. But hopefully, won't—won't have to worry about that. We have other things happening that maybe take that out of the realm of necessity.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And while we've given vast amounts of military aid and money in form of grants, much of Europe's contribution has been economic relief structured as loans, for which they'll be repaid. Like the Europeans, I believe that taxpayers and the United States also deserve to recoup the colossal amounts of money that we've sent. The previous administration never even thought of that. They didn't think of a lot of things, like why did they let it start in the first place.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That is why we must have an agreement with Ukraine on critical minerals and rare earths and various other things as security. And I think that that's happening. I think we've made a lot of progress. I had a report just given to me before walking in that we've made, Emmanuel, a great deal of progress toward getting that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I've been elected by the American people to restore common sense to Washington and, indeed, to the world. And I believe strongly that it's in the best interest of the United States, the best interest in Europe, the best interest of Ukraine, and indeed, the best interest of Russia to stop the killing now and bring the world to peace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My administration is making a decisive break with the foreign policy failures of the past administration and, frankly, the past. I ran against a very foolish foreign policy establishment, and their recklessness has led to the death of many, many people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under our administration, we're forging a new path that promotes peace around the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And when I left office for the first administration—first term, we had no wars. We had no problems. We didn't have October 7 with Israel. We didn't have Russia and Ukraine going at it. We didn't have the problems in other parts of the Middle East. We didn't have inflation. It was a whole different world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you know what else we didn't have? Millions of people pouring through our borders, many of them criminals released from other nations and put right into our land: murderers and drug dealers, gangs. We didn't have any of that. It's a different time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But now we have it, and we're fixing it. We'll fix it all up. We'll get it done as quickly as possible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we've made a great deal of progress. People are saying it was the best month for a President in our country's history. I hope that's right, but—I feel it's right. We've—we've done a lot of things in a very short period of time, 4 weeks.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As I've said before, it's my hope that my greatest legacy, however, will be as a peacemaker and a unifier. I want to bring peace, not war.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I thank President Macron for joining us today in this urgent work we're doing. And we have some wonderful people up front right here that have worked so hard. Steve Witkoff, thank you very much. Michael Waltz, thank you. Scott, thank you very much. And, J.D., thank you. They've really done a—they've really done a job. They worked very hard. It's like—it's a real passion to get this war ended.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'd like to now invite Emmanuel to say a few words, and then we'll take questions. And, again, Emmanuel, it's a great honor to have you with us at the White House. Thank you very much. Please.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: President Macron. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, dear Donald. Ministers, ladies and gentlemen,

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: mesdames and messieurs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, President Macron spoke in French, and his remarks were translated by an interpreter as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Ladies and gentlemen, I'll be saying a few words in French.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, dear Donald, for your hospitality and for this visit. As you mentioned, we have had the opportunity to meet over the past few years. Since your first term, we've been able to discuss matters in Paris and also here at the White House, and it has always been a great joy to do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: And I would like to commend you, and thank you, Mr. President, for extending this friendship to France and taking part in the ceremony at Notre Dame that you mentioned before. It was a great honor for the French people to reopen the cathedral to the rest of the world, and your presence was a testament to that friendship.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: As the President said, this friendship dates back to the Revolutionary War, since the beginning of the United States. And whenever we've needed to, we've been able to come together and be on the right side. We've been able to be united to defend peace and sovereignty, namely, in the two World Wars that marked the 20th century, from Lafayette to Pershing and to the many Americans who landed on Omaha Beach.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: And we spoke earlier before, and you mentioned that one of those gentlemen was able to visit you here, one of the veterans. This is part of history which puts us in the world that we are in today. And as the President just said, there are many challenges in this world. And over the past few days, we have one main objective, which is the geopolitical situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Mr. President, I really wish to thank you for making changes to your schedule to meet with us so quickly. I think we've made very substantive steps forward during our discussions, and this is a major step in what we're experiencing today.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We had a video conference with all of the G–7 leaders, which was an opportunity for us to discuss this matter 3 days [years; White House correction] after the Russian war in Ukraine, and to express our support for President Zelenskyy, to the Ukrainian people, but also to speak and share about our desire for a lasting peace. This is what we have spoken about very forcibly over the past few weeks.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We thought that this war was only going to last a few weeks when it broke out in 2022. We admire greatly the courage of the Ukrainian people.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: And, Mr. President, I wish to thank you for this. You mentioned that there are responsibilities on Europe's side, and, indeed, we have invested $128 billion in aid to Ukraine and the Ukrainians. Ukraine has been able to hold the front of our collective security. It's fought over these past few years for its independence and for its sovereignty, but also for our collective security, because I think that no one in this room wants to live in a world where it's the law of the strongest and international borders can be violated from one day to the next by anyone.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Over the past few hours—and as you mentioned this, Mr. President—we've been able to see a few things take shape. First of all, allow me to commend you on your decision to work with President Zelenskyy and to conclude this agreement that's so important for the U.S. and Ukraine on rare earths, critical minerals, but also having substantive conversations with President Zelenskyy during this key phase of achieving this deal, which is a major commitment to Ukraine's sovereignty. And I think that's very commendable.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We also have a shared desire to build peace. We will have this responsibility. This is 10 years after the war started in Crimea, and then we saw the events in Donbas—in the Donbas region and along the northern part of the country. We want to save lives. We want to bring prisoners back and bring back families and children because there is also humanitarian tragedy affecting the Ukrainian people.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We had lengthy discussions with the President, and we spoke about our desire to bring an end to conflicts; to have a truce that is measurable, verifiable, and that enables negotiation of a lasting peace, where we will discuss not only Ukraine's reconstruction, its territories, but also the security guarantees, meaning maintaining peace over the long term.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: As I said to the President, we have experienced peace accords that were only cease-fires without ensuring security guarantees, Minsk I and II. And we want to make sure this doesn't happen again. And I know that the President has expressed the desire to be a player for peace in the region.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: I've spoken with some 30 European leaders and allies in recent days. We want to bring together these—alleys—allies, rather, and share the same vision. This peace must not mean a surrender of Ukraine. It must not mean a ceasefire without guarantees. This peace must allow for Ukrainian sovereignty and allow Ukraine to negotiate with other stakeholders regarding the issues it affects—that affects it, rather. But it is also a country in which we need to shoulder our responsibility so that we ensure security and stability for Ukraine and for the entire region. And for us Europeans, this is an existential issue.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We also spoke about these issues at length with the President. We've worked with President Zelenskyy and gotten to some of the details of the various phases of the negotiation, and we've also been able to speak about some of this work with our British partners to talk about deployments of peace forces on Ukrainian soil, which are part of these security guarantees. Other countries are ready to join in this effort.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Solidarity and support from the U.S. will be crucial to this. And I thank you, Mr. President, for beginning to work with us on this issue. And the agreement that you are preparing to sign with Ukraine and with all these discussions we've had are very solid guarantees that we are understood and that we have the same wish: peace as soon as possible; lasting, solid peace for everyone; and the renewal of an international situation where we are all able to shoulder our responsibilities— Europeans shouldering their responsibilities, alongside their American allies, who will shoulder their own responsibilities.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: I also wanted to be very clear, Mr. President, about Europe's commitment. We have committed to building a lasting peace. As Europeans, we have committed to being stakeholders in these security guarantees, and we are also well aware that Europeans need to do more for security in Europe, for defense in Europe, and to more fairly share the security burden that your country has been carrying for so many years.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Mr. President, you know how much friendship I show towards you and I have towards you since your first term. Europe is very clear eyed about this. We know what we need to do as Europeans, given the threats surrounding us and the responsibilities that we must shoulder.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We spoke about the Versailles agenda, which allowed the Europeans to take a historic step and increase their investments. Europeans are ready to do even more and to go even farther. And several leaders said that to me before I came here to meet you.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Mr. President, dear Donald, you spoke about this peace through strength. We fully share that, because we must recognize the sacrifices made by the Ukrainian people and what we owe to them.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: The President and I also spoke about economic matters and our desire to see more prosperity in the United States and in Europe. We had discussions which will be carried on by our teams, our ministers and secretaries, to flesh out some of those ideas. But the idea is to have fair competition and no bias within competition between our industries.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Now, the American and European economies are extremely intertwined—some $1.5 billion in trade—trillion, rather, in goods and services. And I know you've spoken about wanting to look at the balance of payments. We also have a trade deficit, and I know that we need to look not only at goods, but also digital items and goods which you export. And we want to make a sincere commitment towards fair competition, where we have smooth trade and more investments.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: You already invest a great deal in France. And France is the fifth most—the fifth largest investor in the United States. And I would like to recognize here all of the American investors who announced investments—some $120 billion that were announced at the AI summit.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: This is our wish. We want to have more prosperity on both sides of the Atlantic. We have a shared agenda in that regard.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: We also spoke about the Middle East, among other subjects. And here, again, we have the same desire. We don't want to see Iran obtain nuclear weapons. We don't want—or, rather, we want an approach with partners in the region that we can trust. Given Iran's nuclear activities, we want to limit its ballistic capabilities and avoid any type of regional destabilization.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: With respect to Syria and Iraq, we also share the same desire. We don't want to see Islamic terrorist groups resume any of their activities, because, for some time, our armies have very bravely been engaged in the Gulf, as you have led, and contributions have been significant and helped stability in the region.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: And I say this with great sincerity: France was affected by a terrorist attack in 2015, which was linked to the terrorist activity in Syria, and we are in that region, at your side, to work for more security.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we had extremely productive discussions this morning during the conference, and we spoke with our ministers and councilors and advisors. And I wish to say, after speaking with President Trump, I am—fully believe that there is a path forward. We share the same beliefs. We know what work needs to be done, and, in the weeks to come, we will work on that. Our teams will come together in various formats to make sure that we have this solid, lasting peace with great strength.

full_topic_context.speaker: mesdames
full_topic_context.text: Mr. President, thank you so much for welcoming me here today. Thank you so much for these productive discussions and for your commitment. Thank you, dear Donald.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much. Thank you, Emmanuel. Thank you very much. [President Macron spoke briefly in English as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: President Macron. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: President Macron. Thank you, Donald.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Okay. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Brian [Brian Glenn, Real America's Voice], would you like to ask a question? Go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine/U.S. Diplomatic Efforts in Saudi Arabia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you. Mr. President, you said before that you would like to see Russia——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——rejoining the G–7.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are there any conditions that you want Russia to meet before they can rejoin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: And your meeting in Saudi Arabia with—your meeting in Saudi Arabia with President Putin, will that happen, regardless of any progress on the Ukrainian—[inaudible]?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, I think the meeting in Saudi Arabia was a fantastic one. We met with the Crown Prince, who is just a fantastic young guy. He's young, but with great imagination and tremendously respected all over the world. And he goes right to the King, and the King is incredible. I've gotten to be friends with both of them very much. And they want to see this ended, and they're going all out to make sure that it is ended.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think Russia, likewise—I've spoken to President Putin, and my people are dealing with him constantly and his people, in particular. And they want to do something. I mean, that's what I do. I do deals. My whole life is deals. That's all I know is deals. And I know when somebody wants to make it and when somebody doesn't.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I will say this. Before I came here, there was no communication with Russia whatsoever, and Russia wasn't answering calls. They were not talking to anybody. They wouldn't talk to anybody. And people sort of accepted that as being that they want to go forward and just keep going without stop. But when I got here, one of the first calls I made was to President Putin, and we were treated with great respect.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they want to end this war. So that's a big thing, because I didn't know if I could say that, but it's a big thing. They want to do it. And the group in the front row that I introduced, they are very—all very active in it. And we're working on deals right now, transactions right now.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, in particular, the big one is to get the—the war stopped, whether it's ceasefire or direct to an agreement. I'd like to go directly to an agreement, but cease-fire will always happen a little bit quicker. And every day, you're saving thousands or at least hundreds—but thousands, in some cases—lives, so we want to see if we can get that done very quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters began asking questions at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. "The Art of the Deal," sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the—on the G–7, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, for the President, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you. Sylvie Corbet. I'm AP correspondent based in Paris. Question for both of you, actually. Mr. Macron, you were one of the last Western leaders to speak to Putin before Ukraine's invasion. What advice, what recommendation could you make to President Trump to make sure that, this time, you can get strong enough guarantee, sorry, from Putin to get a peace deal that lasts this time?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: And, Mr. President Trump, what makes you think you can trust Putin in those negotiations?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [President Macron spoke in English as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: President Macron. Look, I will never give any advice to President Trump. We have friendly and trustful discussion.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: But my experience with President Putin is the following. Number one, I always think it's good to have discussion with other leaders and especially when you—when—when you disagree. I stopped my discussion with President Putin after Bucha and the war crimes because I considered that—I mean, we had nothing to get from him in the time.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: Now this is a chance—there is a big change, because there is a new U.S. administration, so this is a new context. So there is good reason for President Trump to reengage with President Putin.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: But my experience is the following, and I shared it with President Trump and the team. In 2014, our predecessors negotiated peace with President Putin, but because of the lack of guarantees and especially security guarantees, President Putin violated this peace. And I had several discussion, especially beginning of 2022, several times—7 hours with President Putin— 15 days before launching of the—the attack. He denied everything, but we didn't have security guarantees.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: So this is why being strong and having deterrence capacities is the only way to be sure it will be respected. And I insisted on that, and this is why I believe that the U.S. has the capacity to do so. And this is why I think we should never say, "I will never send any boots on the ground," because you give a blank check to violate any type of a commitment.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: So I think it's good to have discussion. I think it's useful to have negotiation. I think it's super important to go to the peace. But my strong point was to say, let's try to get something first which is—which can be assessed, checked, and verified, and let's be sure that we build sufficient guarantees on the short run. And this is where we are ready to be engaged, as for France. A lot of my European colleagues are ready to be engaged.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: But we no—do need this American backup, because this is part of the credibility of the security guarantees, and this is our collective deterrence capacity. And I have the feeling that the President has this capacity.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes. I think it's very much to the benefit of Russia to make a deal, and I feel that we'll do that. It is what it is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Again, it's a war that should have never been started. It's a war that would not have been started if I were President, but it did start, and it's at a terrible level, where cities are burned down and shot down to the ground. It looks like demolition sites, a whole big pile of demolition sites. And we got to get it stopped. Too many people, too much agony. The whole culture is destroyed, when you rip down some of those ancient—really ancient or near-ancient buildings. It's so sad to see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I think it's very much to the benefit of—there's tremendous distrust on both sides. That's why it's good that I'm coming in now. But I think it's to the very much benefit of Russia to make a deal and to go on with—go on with leading Russia in a very positive way. That's what you have to do.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I really believe that he wants to make a deal. May be wrong, but I believe he wants to make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters began asking questions at once.] Yes. Go ahead, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance/Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, France

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. President Trump, President Macron, first of all, you said, "I would like to make a deal with Putin." So, when you do a deal, it's a win-win deal, what are you giving to him, and what is he going to give you, to America?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: And I was impressed by the way you referred to Notre Dame, and that you were impressed by the reconstruction of Notre Dame. A lot of American have sent money to Paris to participate to the reconstruction of Notre Dame. As a President of the United States, are you going to contribute to the reconstruction of Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The reporter then spoke in French, and his remarks were translated by an interpreter as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: President Macron, what, for you, is the main area of progress in your meeting with President Trump? Can you confirm that there is an agreement to send European peacekeeping troops? Will France participate in that? How many troops? What would they be doing? Would this represent a great danger to send French and European troops to Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I guess it's a little strange question, because you ask whether or not we're going to, on behalf of the United States, contribute to Ukraine. I mean, we're in there for about $350 billion. I think that's a pretty big contribution.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I do appreciate the first part of your question, however, because I think they've done an incredible job with the Cathedral of Notre Dame. I think the President has done—I know he headed it up, and I know he—how hard he worked, and it took a period of time but really not a long period of time, considering what that was. So delicate, so beautiful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I was there, and I saw the work. And I'm very good at construction. I know good construction, and I know bad construction. They did a beautiful job, and this man has to be given a lot of credit for that. It's an incredible cathedral. Most people thought it couldn't be saved, and, if it was, it would have to be built in a different form. And we didn't want to see a different form. We wanted to see the same form that you built.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I just want to congratulate you. That was an amazing job. I don't think you've gotten enough credit for it. Someday you will. Someday you will.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: President Macron. Thank you, Donald.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [President Macron spoke in French, and his remarks were translated by an interpreter as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: To go back to your question, today's discussion showed several areas of progress. First, we have been working a great deal with President Zelenskyy to have a proposal that's acceptable to

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine. President Trump has confirmed that he will be meeting with President Zelenskyy very soon to finalize the agreement on critical minerals and rare earths and to speak together about that matter. That's a very important step forward.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: The second thing is that, during our discussions, we were able to go into some of the details about the proposal that we have just made to have a truce, a peace, and be able to measure that and then structure our discussions on that basis. France and several other European countries, along with Ukraine, are hard at work to build this lasting peace with very specific points, including security guarantees. The territories that belong to Ukraine, the issue of reconstruction, the economy, and critical minerals—we've been able to go into the details of those proposals.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: The third area of progress, which really mark a turning point, is the fact that we were able to talk about the details of the security guarantees. And the President has shown this over the past few days, and he said so a moment ago: We want peace. He wants peace. We want peace swiftly, but we don't want an agreement that is weak.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: The fact that there are Europeans that are ready to engage to provide for these security guarantees and now there's a clear American message that the U.S., as an ally, is ready to provide that solidarity for that approach, that's a turning point, in my view, and that is one of the great areas of progress that we've made during this trip and during this discussion.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: When it comes to troops, in the past—a year ago, specifically—we saw a reason to talk about sending troops to—for strategic regions. Today, when we talk about troops, we're talking about sending them in after we've negotiated a lasting peace. And once we have that solid, lasting peace that's part of an agreement signed by Ukraine, signed by Russia, and for which we will provide the guarantees—then, at that point—and recently, France has worked with the U.K. to provide its contributions. We've worked on plans. We've worked with our militaries—not to go to the front lines, not to go into occupied territories, but as a show of support to show that we have a negotiated peace signed by both sides, and that is a peace we will preserve.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: So these would be peaceful deployments of troops, not for combat. These would be deployments of an assurance force. They would be limited, but they show solidarity.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: I have also spoken with all of our allies, and they are European and non-European allies who are ready and willing to take part in that effort. Countries have helped Ukraine maintain its military capabilities in terms of the number of soldiers it has, equipment, whereas others have provided logistical support on the ground. The question is whether or in what form the U.S. will contribute.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: And during our discussions and during the discussions with Russia, we've understood that this would be acceptable to Russia. And that's a very important area of progress, and that means that, in this context, the Europeans will shoulder their part of the burden, their share of the burden. We have a strong alliance that we have built over the decades, we have our solidarity, and we have deterrence capacities.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: What does it mean? Would it be dangerous? If there is an agreement signed by Ukraine and Russia, thanks to the efforts of President Trump, and if we provide the guarantees and Russia violates the agreement, then it would be in conflict with everyone who is engaged in the peace process. And that is a change. That was something we did not see in the past. That's not what we saw in 2014, so that is the real change that we're marking.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: We have this deterrence capacity on the American side. We have the capacity for engagement on the European side, and that's something we're going to continue working on together. It's not dangerous, but it's credible. It's less dangerous than things that could happen in the long term. And I think this is what we need to do to ensure security.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: And I say this very clearly, we're also talking about security for Europeans. I've been saying this for weeks now. If we do not guarantee the security of this territory within Europe, then how can we guarantee our own security for one and all? We live just 1,500 kilometers from Ukraine, and the Germans and Polish are even closer. So our collective security is important. We need to answer this call for Europeans to be more engaged, and Americans will be there still in solidarity.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: Europeans are working for their collective security, but I really think this was a turning point today in our discussions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Emmanuel, thank you very much. Great job. And it's been wonderful being with you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Say hello to your beautiful wife, and we will see you again soon. We'll be speaking often, and we'll get this thing worked out. We're going to get it done. So important. And great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: President Macron
full_topic_context.text: President Macron. Thank you. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you. Thank you very much. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/Critical Minerals Supply

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is it true that President Zelenskyy is coming on Friday to meet with you? And is the mineral deal sorted out? Is it done?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, I hear that. I hear that he's coming on Friday. Certainly, it's okay with me if he'd like to. And he would like to sign it together with me. And I understand that it's a big deal, a very big deal. And I think the American people, even if you look at polling, they're very happy because, you know, Biden was throwing money around like it's cotton candy, and it's a very big deal. It could so—it could be a trillion-dollar deal. It could be whatever. But it's rare earths and other things.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, look, we're spending hundreds of billions of dollars on Ukraine and Russia fighting a war that should have never, ever happened. That's a war that should—would have never happened if I were President, and it didn't happen for 4 years. People say, "How do we know that?" It didn't happen for 4 years.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It would have never happened. And nevertheless, this guy went into this situation, and he spent money like nobody has ever seen: $350 billion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The other thing that we don't like is that Europe has spent $100 billion. We've spent $350 billion. Europe gets their money back because they spent it in the form of a loan, and we just gave them—whether it's $300 or $350 billion, nobody really knows. They can't even tell me the answer to that. Probably—means it's probably more than that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So what we're doing is, now we're saying: "Look, we want to be secured. We want to get that money back."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're helping the country through a very, very big problem—a problem like very few people have had. Shouldn't have had this problem, because it shouldn't have happened. But it did happen, so we have to straighten it out. But the American taxpayer now is going to get their money back, plus.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/European Security Assistance/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, yesterday with Emmanuel Macron, you said you had spoken to Putin about the idea of peacekeepers in Ukraine, that Putin was fine with it. The Kremlin, I guess, has said that that's actually unacceptable to them. What's real here?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, that's not what I was told. But you're going to need some form of peacekeeping. So something will be done that's going to be satisfactory to everybody. We need peacekeeping too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Any situation where there's——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It's actually——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——American troops involved?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It's actually something I did discuss, but a form of peacekeeping that's acceptable to everybody. Ultimately, we'll be able to agree on something, I'm sure.

full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Critical Minerals Supply

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. With Ukraine and this mineral deal, what does Ukraine get in return, Mr. President?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Three hundred and fifty billion dollars and lots of equipment and military equipment and the right to fight on and, originally, the right to fight.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Look, Ukraine, I will say, they're very brave and they're good soldiers, but without the United States and its money and its military equipment, this war would have been over in a very short period of time. In fact, I was the one that gave the Javelins. You remember the famous Javelins? That was me. That wasn't Obama. It wasn't Biden. It wasn't anybody else. It was me. And they wiped out a lot of tanks with those Javelins. And the expression was that Obama gave sheets and I gave the Javelins. That was a big deal at the time. It wiped out—that was the beginning, where people said, "Wow, that's something."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Well, that was American equipment. Without American equipment, this war would have been over very quickly. And American money too. I mean, a lot of money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So you said that war-fighting equipment and the ammunition—that's sustained going forward for Ukraine? And how long is it sustained?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, it could go forward for a while, and maybe until we have a deal with Russia. Look, if we're going to—we need to have a deal with Russia. Otherwise, it's going to continue.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But now, when Americans put up their money, the taxpayer money, and the President approves it, we're getting our money back in some form. But it could go on for a while, or it could be settled quickly. I think it's going to be settled quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I spoke with President Putin. I think he wants to settle it and wants to get on with life. It's horrible. What's happening: horrible. Thousands of soldiers a week are being killed, and others too, but especially on the battlefield. Thousands a week are being killed. And we want that to end.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, Brian [Brian Glenn, Real America's Voice].

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on Ukraine, would you provide military support for Ukraine in the future under a peace agree—agreement?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Say it again louder.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would you provide military support for Ukraine in the future as part——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You mean like security?

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——of a peace agreement? Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, people are going to do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Security guarantees.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think Europe will largely be responsible for that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But Macron——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. European countries will be responsible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But Macron asked for a U.S. backup. Will you be——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, we'll see. I mean, right now, we're just in the process of negotiating.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We've pretty much negotiated our deal on raw earth and various other things. We'll be looking at that. Security—you're talking about general security for Ukraine later on. I don't think that's going to be a problem.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Air defense? Aircraft?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. There are a lot of people that want to do it. And I spoke with Russia about it. They didn't seem to have a problem with it, so I think they understand. They're not going back in. Once we do this, they're not going back in.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So not even air defense or aircraft?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on the gold card——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/European Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would the U.S. provide, for instance, air defense for Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I just told you. We're—right now we're not providing anything. You know, it's about Europe too. Europe put in $100 billion, and we put in $350 billion. It's not a fair thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we would normally say, and we—I say it now anyway, but we want equalization. They should put up, actually, more money than us, because they're right there. We have an ocean in between.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we've had very good talks with Russia. We've had very good talks with Ukraine. And we think it maybe will come to an end and we'll stop killing young people all over the battlefield— and elsewhere.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Critical Minerals Supply

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, when you spoke to Vladimir Putin, did he raise or did you discuss at all the possibility of a minerals deal on the Ukrainian land that Russia now controls——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I didn't discuss——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——that—striking a deal with Russia?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No. I'd like to buy minerals on Russian land too, if we can. The rare earth.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They have very good rare earth also—they both do, I would say that—and oil and gas. Look, it's a great thing. If we settle this, it's great for Russia too——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Does——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——because we can do deals there. They have very valuable land that isn't utilized. So something like that could take place, yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/U.S. Sanctions

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Have you put raising—or lifting sanctions against Russia on the table as you're negotiating the—[inaudible]—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, we haven't lifted any sanctions on anybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is it on the table as part of any negotiations?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I guess it will be at some point. But right now, we haven't agreed to lift sanctions on anybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Special Immigration Program

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On that gold card, getting back to that. I'm fascinated by this, Mr. President and——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You should be fascinated by it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——and Secretary Lutnick. Would——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Your taxes will go down to nothing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would a Russian oligarch be eligible for a gold card?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, possibly. Hey, I know some Russian oligarchs that are very nice people. [Laughter] It's possible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Care to elaborate?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They're not quite as wealthy as they used to be. [Laughter] They're not as wealthy as they used to be. I think they could afford $5 million.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So they have sanctions on them——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, a lot of people are going to want to—a——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——and yet they would be eligible for a gold card?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. A lot of people are going to want to be in this country. And they'll be able to work and provide jobs and build companies and pay taxes, all of those things. It's an incredible thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I mean, you're—this is the group that is the first to hear it. Nobody's heard about it. Nobody ever thought about it. But we've been thinking about it very, very strongly over the last week.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I was going to announce it sometime next week, and I figured: "Why not? We have a lot of cameras blazing right now." [Laughter] "Might as well—we might as well do it now." We'll have Karoline announce it the next time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No, it's a great thing, the gold card. Remember the words: the gold card. Somebody said, "Can we call it the Trump gold card?" I said: "If it helps, use the name Trump. I'll give it to you for free." [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Lutnick
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Lutnick. I like it, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you probably just launched 10,000 stories. Do you want to elaborate a little bit more on what Russian oligarchs you know or don't know?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I know. Isn't it interesting how many stories we do tell? [Laughter] And they all turn out to be true. And they all turn out to be ultimately correct, huh? You know, "Trump was right about everything."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Do you have one of those "Trump was right about everything" hats? I'm going to give it to this gentleman. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Get me one of those hats. Get me—get me one of them—[inaudible]. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Lutnick
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Lutnick. But they're all going to be vetted.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, when would it—when would it start, the gold card program?

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Lutnick
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Lutnick. Everybody who comes in gets vetted.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When would it start?

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Lutnick
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Lutnick. Okay? They get vetted. So you've got to—you know—

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When does it begin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes, when does it begin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Lutnick
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Lutnick. We're going to begin in 2 weeks.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. About 2 weeks. The sale will start in about 2 weeks. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, do you see a more active role for Zelenskyy now, given the status with the——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I hope so. I mean, look, I think that we want to get that country back on its feet, and right now, it's been destroyed. It's so——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Here, give me this. Here. Give me all of them.

full_topic_context.text: White House aide. Sure.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [The President was handed a stack of hats.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: in.

full_topic_context.text: Somebody said that. I said—these were sent in by a fan. I said, "I think we should make

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: some of them," right? But we were, pretty much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You want one?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Are you allowed to take one?

full_topic_context.text: Q. Probably not.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Because he'll consider it. I know him well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, I'll take one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You're sort of a stiff.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I said you were right from day one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, Brian, you're not a stiff. [The President tossed a hat to a reporter.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. He's sort of a stiff guy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Appreciate it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. He'll take other things, but not a free hat. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Lutnick
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Lutnick. Always say yes to the President. Always say yes to the President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President. Mr. President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Would anybody like one?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, an easy question, perhaps, for you. Maybe it's difficult. I'm going to ask you this question about the Super Bowl.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Who do you work for?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I work for two news organizations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Who?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I work for two news organizations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, who are they?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I work for Gray Television, America's second largest broadcaster. And I work for iHeartRadio. So there you go.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Okay. All right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Professional Golf

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What's the main obstacle holding up this PGA Tour-LIV Golf deal?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, they have to get together. You know, they've had a lot of discussion back and forth. They both are meaning well, and a deal will ultimately happen. I think it will happen pretty quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What's your role——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It will be nice to see the golfers—the best golfers be able to play against each other.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What's your role been in this whole process?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Just to help expedite it. Tiger was here. Adam Scott was here. Jay Monahan was here the other day. Just to really help expedite it. We had Yasir here from Saudi Arabia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Great guy. These are all great people, and they want to work it out, so if I can help them work it out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I don't get anything out of it. If I can help them work it out—I just think golf, it's very much of an individual sport, and you want to see the best players playing against each other, not playing in two different locations, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What's going to be more challenging: a PGA-LIV deal or a Russia-Ukraine deal?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think the PGA deal is much more complicated. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Israel/West Bank Settlements/Joint Chiefs of Staff/Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, may I ask another Middle East question, if I may? What's your take on what's happening in the West Bank and what Israel is doing there?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, it's a—there's some movement up there that a lot of people are concerned about, and there's been a lot of Israeli movement. They're up there for a reason all of a sudden. Maybe they're not feeling so good about that. So that would be terrible. I hope that doesn't happen. But there is movement up there that nobody knew about. Right? You know that, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes. And when you say—are you concerned about it as well?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I'm concerned about everything. I want the world to be peaceful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, when I left here, we had no war. We had defeated ISIS in less than 4 weeks. In fact, I took the general that defeated ISIS, and I put him in charge of the whole ball game, because that's what we want. We want winners. "Razin" Caine. You know "Razin"? When I heard that name, I said: "I like that name. That's the kind of general I like." So we'll see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But he was great. He was a great soldier. Not a politician, a soldier—a real soldier. You know that, Brian.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. This guy was for real.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I do.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. This guy's the real——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I've heard that story a million times.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes. This guy is the real deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. He is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And I think he's going to do a great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But think of it. We had no wars. We had no problems. We had no inflation. We had no problems. And then, all of a sudden, you have October 7 in Israel, which was horrible. And then you see what happened with—Ukraine would have never—Russia would have never gone in if the election weren't rigged.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It was a rigged election. The 2020 election was rigged. And we got out of it, and you see what happened. You see what happened to our country: inflation, Afghanistan—that horrible withdraw from Afghanistan. I think when Russia saw what happened in Afghanistan, they said, "Wow, that's a paper tiger." We're not a paper tiger. We are the strongest military force in the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And by the way, Pete Hegseth is doing a great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we didn't have wars. We didn't have inflation. We had a strong border. We had everything going good. And then Biden got in, and he's, my opinion, the worst President in the history of our country. I think Jimmy Carter was a very happy man when he passed away——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So what are you——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——2 weeks [months; White House correction] ago.

full_topic_context.text: The President. Okay. Thank you very much. We appreciate you being here. And we've put together a great Cabinet. And we've had tremendous success. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're going to solve a lot of problems.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're doing very well with Russia-Ukraine. President Zelenskyy is going to be coming on Friday. That's now confirmed. And we're going to be signing an agreement, which will be a very big agreement. And I want to thank Howard and Scott for the job you guys did in putting it together. Really did an amazing job. And that will be on rare earth and other things.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, as you know, we're in for, probably, $350 billion and Europe is in for $1 billion—$100 billion. And that's a big difference. So we're in for, probably, three times as much. And yet it's very important to everybody, but Europe is very close. We have a big ocean separating us. So it's very important for Europe. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The previous administration put us in a very bad position, but we've been able to make a deal where we're going to get our money back, and we're going to get a lot of money in the future.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think that's appropriate, because we have taxpayers that are—shouldn't be footing the bill, and they shouldn't be footing the bill at more than the Europeans are paying.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So it's all been worked out. We're happy about it. And I think that, very importantly, we're going to be able to make a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Most importantly, by far, we're going to make a deal with Russia and Ukraine to stop killing people. They'll stop killing young Russian soldiers and young Ukrainian soldiers and other people, in addition, in the towns and cities. And so we'll—keep you advised.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Scott, that was a very good job you did. You've done that before, haven't you? [Laughter] Wow.

full_topic_context.text: So Scott Turner is a terrific young guy. He's heading up HUD, and he's going to make us all very proud, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Turner
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Turner. Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. Great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In just over 1 month, illegal border crossings have plummeted by numbers that nobody has actually ever seen before. It's much more than a hundred percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we've unleashed American energy at levels that will soon be reported, but we think we're going to get it going very quickly. We have incredible people on the energy front.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think we have really great people on every front. I'll let you know if they're not good, but I think they really are.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're fighting every day to get the prices down. The inflation is stopping slowly, but part of the reason it's stopping is because of high interest rates and other problems that we inherited. But we have to get the prices down—not the inflation down—the prices of eggs and various other things. Eggs are a disaster.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The Secretary of Agriculture is going to be showing you a chart that's actually mindboggling what's happened—how low they were with us and how high they are now. But I think we can do something about it——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——Madam Secretary.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Rollins
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Rollins. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And I think you're going to do a fantastic job in that position.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: One of the most important initiatives is DOGE, and we have cut billions and billions and billions of dollars. We're looking to get it maybe to a trillion dollars. If we can do that, we're going to start getting to be at a point where we can think in terms of balancing budgets, believe it or not, something you haven't heard in many, many years—decades, actually. And it's a big— whether it's this year or next year, I think we'll be very close to balancing budgets. And the DOGE is very important.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Elon is here to give you a summary of what's happening, some of the things they found—some of the horrible things they found—some of the theft and fraud, and we call it waste and abuse, but a lot of fraud, and probably some fraud that we're not going to be able to prove is fraud, but when you hear the names and the places where this money is going, it's a disgrace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we've requested that a lot of people—we want to make sure that the people are working.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So letters were sent out, and I think everyone at this table is very much behind it. And if they aren't, I'd want them to speak up. But they're very much behind it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Letters were sent out to people just to find out, if the people exist, do they work? Who do they work for? Where are they? You know, where have they been working? full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the letter asks some simple questions like, "What have you done lately?" And if they can answer that—because I can. I can tell you everything I've done for the last long period of time, a lot more than a week.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And in many cases, we haven't gotten responses. Usually, that means that maybe that person doesn't exist or that person doesn't want to say they're working for another company while being paid by the United States Government.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So there's a lot of interesting things. It's very unique, but we have a very unique situation because we have a lot of people that were scamming our country. We have a lot of dishonest people. We have a lot of people that took advantage of a lot of different situations, and we're not going to let that happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I'm going to ask, if it's possible, to have Elon get up first and talk about DOGE, because it seems to be of great interest to everyone.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I will say that there is a large group of people in this country that have such admiration for what we're doing. I got elected with a tremendous vote, winning every swing State, winning the popular vote, winning the counties by thousands of counties. I think it was 2,800 to 500. 2,800 counties to 500 counties. Think of that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And so we have a mandate to do this, and this is part of the reason I got elected. I got elected based on taxes and based on many things, the border, but also based on balancing budgets and getting our country back into shape, and this is a big part of it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, Elon, if you could get up and explain where you are, how you're doing, and how much we're cutting. And it's an honor to have you. He's been a tremendously successful guy. full_topic_context.text: So I'd like to have Elon Musk please say a few words.

full_topic_context.text: We spend a lot on the Defense Department, but we're spending, like, over a trillion dollars on interest. If this continues, the country will go—become de facto bankrupt. full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser Musk
full_topic_context.text: But if we don't do this, America will go bankrupt. That's why it has to be done. full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser Musk
full_topic_context.text: And obviously, that can only be done with the support of everyone in this room. And I'd like to thank everyone for your support. Thank you very much this. This can only be done with your support.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser Musk
full_topic_context.text: So this is—it's really—DOGE is a support function for the President and for the agencies and departments to help achieve those savings and to effectively find 15 percent in reduction in fraud and—and waste.

full_topic_context.text: And we bring the receipts. So people say, like, "Well, is this real?" Just go to DOGE.gov.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser Musk
full_topic_context.text: So, for example, with USAID, one of the things we accidentally canceled, very briefly, was Ebola—Ebola prevention. I think we all wanted Ebola prevention. So we restored the Ebola prevention immediately, and there was no interruption.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser Musk
full_topic_context.text: But we do need to move quickly if we're to achieve a trillion-dollar deficit reduction in financial year 2026. It requires saving $4 billion per day, every day from now through the end of September. But we can do it, and we will do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser Musk
full_topic_context.text: Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You look at Social Security as an example. I mean, you have so many people in Social Security where, if you believe it, they're 200 years old. And what we're doing is finding out: Are checks going out for that and is somebody cashing those checks who's maybe 35 years old?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So there's a lot of dishonesty. There's a lot of fraud.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I think at this moment, I'll take Elon off the spot. full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/Critical Minerals/Electricity Supply

full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on Ukraine. Can you talk a lot—a little bit about what type of security guarantees you're willing to make?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I'm not going to make security guarantees beyond very much. We're going to have Europe do that, because it's in—you know, we're talking about Europe is their next- door neighbor. But we're going to make sure everything goes well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, as you know, we'll be making a—we'll be really partnering with Ukraine in terms of rare earth. We very much need rare earth. They have great rare earth. We'll be working with Secretary Burgum and with Chris. You'll be working on that together.

full_topic_context.text: And we're going to be able to have tremendous—I mean, this gives us—because we don't have that much of it here. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We have to double our electric capacity. We have to do many things. We have to really triple, if you think of it, the electric capacity from what we have right now, if you can believe it. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.text: The President. So I just say this. So the deal we're making gets us—it—brings us great wealth. We get back the money that we spent, and we hope that we're going to be able to settle this up.

full_topic_context.text: We want to settle it. We want to stop—I tell you what. I'm doing it for two reasons, but the number one reason, by far, is to watch—all these people being killed. They're being decimated, because equipment today—military equipment is so powerful and so devastating. And number one, I want to see people stop.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they're not from here. They're from primarily two other countries.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then, by the way, let's talk about the Middle East. We've got to solve that problem too. And that's come a long way. We're doing very well in that also. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My number-two thing is, I don't want to have to pay any more money, because we've— Biden has spent $350 billion without any chance of getting it back. I mean, we've provided something very important, and we'll be working with Ukraine and—because we'll be taking that—we're going to be taking what we're entitled to take.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, they spent $350 billion, and Europe spent $100 billion. Now, does anybody really think that's fair? But then we find out, a little while ago—not so long ago, a few months ago, I found out that the money they spent, they get back, but the money we spent, we don't get back. I said, "Well, we're going to get it back."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we'll be able to make a deal. And again, President Zelenskyy is coming to sign the deal. And it's a great thing.
