full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But Europe will be watching it very closely. I know that U.K. has said and France has said that they want to put—they volunteered to put so-called peacekeepers on the site. And I think that's a good thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Don't forget: We got rid of ISIS in 3 weeks. People said it would take 5 years. We did it, because when I came in, I let them do what they had to do. And the man that headed that operation is now going to be your Chairman, right?

full_topic_context.text: Certainly, General "Razin" Caine, who's on his way in, was not a part of that. Instead, was a part of leading the effort against ISIS by untying the hands of war fighters and finishing the job properly and then bringing our troops home.

full_topic_context.text: So we're taking a very different view, obviously, than the previous administration, and there will be full accountability.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.text: That was a horrible display. And you know, I've dealt with the parents and the family of the 13 that were killed. It was so terrible, the way that was handled.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it should have been gone through Bagram. We have a big base with big fences that nobody can get in, and you have, you know, hundreds of acres, instead of a little local airport where the whole place went crazy. That was so badly handled. And I would think that most of those people are going to be gone.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are we going to take Bagram back?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So I'll tell you what—what has bothered me very much—very, very much: We give billions of dollars to Afghanistan. Nobody knows that. Nobody knew that. Do you know

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: we give billions of dollars to Afghanistan? And yet we left behind all of that equipment, which wouldn't have happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we were getting out under me. I'm the one that got it down to 5,000 people. We were going to get out, but we were going to keep Bagram, not because of Afghanistan but because of China, because it's exactly 1 hour away from where China makes its nuclear missiles.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So they—we were going to keep Bagram. We were going to keep a small force on Bagram.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We were going to have Bagram Air Base, one of the biggest air bases in the world. One of the biggest runways, one of the most powerful runways, in the sense that it was very heavy concrete and steel. You could carry about anything. You could land anything on those runways.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We gave it up. And you know who's occupying it right now? China. China. Biden gave it up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to keep that, and we're going to have a withdrawal, and we're going to take our equipment. We're going to do it properly. We're going to do it very—we're going to keep the equipment.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Well, they ran out. It was—what happened there was a disgrace—in fact, you know, in all fairness to Putin, when he saw that, he said, "Well, this is our time to go and go into Ukraine," I guess, because it was—the timing seemed to be about right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we send them billions of dollars in aid, which nobody knows. If they—if the American public knew that—they know it now. And if we're doing that, I think they should give our equipment back. And I told Pete to study that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we left billions—tens of billions of dollars' worth of equipment behind. Brandnew trucks. You see them display it every year on their little roadway someplace where they have a road and they drive the—you know, waving the flag and talking about America. Beautiful equipment that's all—I mean, the top-of-the-line stuff, brandnew stuff. Now it's getting older.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you know what? If we're going to pay them, I think we should get a lot of that equipment back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know that Afghanistan is one of the biggest sellers of military equipment in the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know why? They're selling the equipment that we left. We're first. They were second or third. Can you believe it? They're selling 777,000 rifles, 70,000 armor-plated—many of them were armor-plated trucks and vehicles—70,000.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If you think of a used car lot, the biggest one in the country, you have—I would say, J.D., if somebody had 500 cars, that would be a lot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance. Yes, that would be quite a lot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. This is 70,000 vehicles we had there, and we left it for them. I think we should get it back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, of all the deals that you've done in your life, all the people you've sat across from and negotiated with, is President Putin distinct in any way?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. He's a very smart guy. He's a very cunning person. But I've dealt with some people that—I've dealt with some really bad people. But I will tell you, as far as this is concerned, we've—you have to understand, he was—he had no intention, in my opinion, of settling this war. I think he wanted the whole thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When I got elected, we spoke, and I think we're going to have a deal. I can't guarantee you that. You know, a deal is a deal. Lots of crazy things happen in deals, right? But I think we're going to have a deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If I didn't get elected, I believe he would have just continued to go through Ukraine, and over a period of time, a lot of people—a lot of people—would have been killed. It would have lasted for a period of time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the reason that Ukraine—and I give—I have great respect for the Ukraine as fighters. They have great fighters. But without our equipment, that war would have been over, like people said, in a very short period of time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is there a timeline—[inaudible]——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And if you remember, I gave the Javelins, and the Javelins are the things that knocked out those tanks right at the beginning of the war. They said that Obama, at the time, gave sheets, and Trump gave Javelins. Well, I was the one that did that. But I want to see it come to an end.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Will he have to make concessions—President Putin?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, he will. He will. He's going to have to. And——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: 2024 Presidential Election

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Can you preview that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And I think—I believe that, because we got elected, that war will come to an end. And I also believe, if we didn't get elected, if this administration didn't win the election by a lot, that that war would go on for a long time, and he would want to take the whole thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What concessions? What concessions?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. The big question I had is: Does he want to take the whole thing? But the reason—and the Ukrainians are good fighters, I have to say, but without the equipment—without our equipment—we have the best equipment in the world. We have the best military equipment in the world. Without our equipment, that would have been over very quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What concessions would you like to see?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the—[inaudible]—sir? On—on the——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What concessions would you like to see?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Oh, I don't want to tell right now. But I can tell you that NATO, you can forget about. That's been—I think that's probably the reason the whole thing started. And I think, J.D., we can say that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What—do you have a statement on that? You've been very much involved.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I gave him the beauty.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. Great. You gave me the hardest question, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Concessions from Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. I mean, look, as the President said, we're not going to do the negotiation in public with the American media. He's going to do it in private with the President of Russia, with the President of Ukraine, and with other leaders. And I think that's how this has to go.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: I think the—I just want to push back against some of the criticism I've seen in the administration on this, because every single time the President engages in diplomacy, you guys preemptively accuse him of conceding to Russia. full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/European Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, would you—would you send U.S. peacekeepers to just—to support the European peacekeepers? Would you do any sort of U.S.——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, we're going to support Europe, yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And how would we do that? How would the United States do that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We're very friendly with Europe. We have a great relationship with Europe. I mean, you could ask—you could talk about France. You could talk about any of them. Yes, we have a great relationship with Europe.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But how will we—how will the United States do that? Would there be boots on——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, how? I mean, you're asking me a question: What are we doing in the — let's worry—I hope we have that problem, where we can worry about peacekeeping. We got to get there first.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Secretary Lutnick knocked on the table.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I hope we have the problem of worrying about peacekeeping. That will be the easiest problem, I think, J.D., that we've ever had. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. I think so, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. That would be part of the deal, presumably, that the Ukrainians——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We'll—we're——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——would want——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We'll do it at the time, but we'll—peacekeeping is very easy. It's making the deal that's very tough.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, again, nobody was speaking to Russia at all. But the thing with that war is that you're highly underestimating the number of people that have been killed. Far more people have been killed in that war than you talk about. You know, you like to talk about numbers, like, a million people. Well, they had much more than a million soldiers killed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you have a lot of cities that have been knocked to the ground. They're demolition sites. Literally, demolition sites. No. No. People were killed by the thousands.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And there are a lot more people killed in that war than the media wants to talk about, because Biden did a horrible, horrible job. He should have prevented that war. He could have prevented that war.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Putin would have never gone in. I'll tell you one thing: He would have never gone in. That war would never have taken place if I were President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/European Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I think what people are trying to understand, Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——is how would the United States—what would you be willing to do to support this European peacekeeping effort? Would there be——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Again, you're asking me the same question? [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I'm just trying——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. How many times do you have to answer it? You're talking about after we make peace. Let me make peace first.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Once we make peace, I'll give you all the answers you want. But how many times can you ask the same question?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on the Middle East. Did you receive——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is loosening the sanctions on——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, go ahead. Behind.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/U.S. Sanctions

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is loosening the sanctions on Russia a potential option as part of an overall deal?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Not now, no. No. We have sanctions on Russia. No, I want to see if we make a deal first. But I think we will. I've had very——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But is it a bargaining chip, I'm asking.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I've had very good conversations with President Putin. I've had very good conversations with President Zelenskyy. full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, just——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But if Mr. Putin gets to keep his——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——just to bring this——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——the land that was claimed by force, if the Russians get to keep the territory that they—they claimed by force, doesn't that send a dangerous message, let's say, to China about Taiwan?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Oh, okay. You try and take it away, right? We're going to—we're going to do the best we can. full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, just to bring this full——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And we'll—cut it out after maybe this question. Go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. To bring this full circle, back to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Unless it's a bad question, and then we'll—[inaudible]. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And back to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. You always like to—you always like to finish on a good one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. But, sir, they want you to negotiate with them instead of President Putin.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I know. I know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Back to the question about the——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They want to continue to talk about the peacekeepers. [Laughter] They're— you have—you have a lot of confidence in us, because you assume there's going to be peace. You know, it's possible it doesn't work out. There is possibility.

full_topic_context.text: Q. And I had——

full_topic_context.text: The President. But I hope it does, for the sake of humanity, because if you look at the pictures that I've looked at, you don't want to look at them.

full_topic_context.text: Go ahead.

state_or_delegation_favorable_evidence.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much. It's a great honor to have Prime Minister Starmer in the Oval Office. It's a very special place, and he's a special man. And the United Kingdom is a wonderful—this is a wonderful country that I know very well. I'm there a lot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'll be going there, and we expect to see each other in the near future. We'll be announcing it. But we're going to be discussing many things today. We'll be discussing Russia- Ukraine. We'll be discussing trade and lots of other items. And I think we can say that we're going to be getting along on every one of them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We've had a tremendous relationship. And frankly, the Prime Minister and I have met twice before, and we—we get along very famously, as you would say. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I look forward to it very much. We look forward to the day and the meeting. We'll be having a luncheon after this, and then another work session. And I believe we're going to have a press conference at the end, so I look forward to it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, Mr. Prime Minister, thank you very much. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Thank you, Mr. President. Can I say thank you for your hospitality, for your leadership?

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: We have met a number of times, we've talked a number of times, and we have had a very constructive conversation. I'm sure we will today.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: And of course, our countries have been bound together for a very long time now, the closest alliance, I think, of any two countries——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——when it comes to prosperity and security. And I know that, together, we will strengthen that even further.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: And on issues like Ukraine, thank you for changing the conversation to bring about the possibility that now we can have a peace deal. And we want to work with you to make sure that peace deal is enduring, that it lasts, that it's a deal that goes down as a historic deal that nobody breaches. And we'll work with you to make sure that that absolutely happens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: And it is my pleasure to bring from His Majesty the King a letter. He sends his best wishes and his——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Great gentleman.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——regards, of course. But he also asked me to bear this letter and bring it to you. So can I present——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——the letter from the King to you?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much. Am I supposed to read it right now?

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes, please do. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I will do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. I've got to tell him what your reaction is. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, he's a——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. So I need to know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. He is—he's a great gentleman. A great, great gentleman. [At this point, President Trump read the letter.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Oh, that's—wow.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Well, that is really nice. I must make sure his signature is on that. [Laughter] Because, otherwise, it's not quite as meaningful. And it is. [Laughter] It is. And that's quite a signature, isn't it? Huh? Beautiful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What did it say?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. He is a beautiful man, a wonderful man. And we appreciate it. I've known him—gotten to know him very well, actually—first term and now second term.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Perhaps you'd like to say what that very important paragraph——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes, so this is a letter from His Majesty the King. It's an invitation for a second state visit.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: This is really special. This has never happened before. This is unprecedented. And I think that just symbolizes the strength of the relationship between us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: So this is a very special letter. I think the last state visit was a tremendous success.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. It was.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. His Majesty the King wants to make this even better than that. So this is truly historic and unprecedented second state visit.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's a great, great honor.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. And he wants to talk that through with you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And that says at Windsor. That's really——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's really something.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes. What I haven't got yet is your answer. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. The answer——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. I do need to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. The answer is yes. On behalf of our wonderful First Lady, Melania, and myself, the answer is yes. And we look forward to being there and honoring the King and honoring, really, your country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Your country is a fantastic country, and it will be our honor to be there. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Well, thank you very much, Mr. President. I shall happily take that back to His Majesty.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. It's beautiful. Prime Minister Starmer. Thank you. President Trump. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you. I'm going to keep that one. [Laughter] Prime Minister Starmer. You're going to keep that one. [Several reporters began asking questions at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, could you be persuaded, as part of a peace settlement in Ukraine, to provide air cover, a backstop security position to the contributions that Europe might make as well?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, so President Zelenskyy is coming to see me on Friday—Friday morning. And we're going to be signing, really, a very important agreement for both sides, because it's really going to get us into that country. We'll be working there. We'll have a lot of people working there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And so, in that sense, it's very good. It's a backstop, you could say. I don't think anybody is going to play around if we're there with a lot of workers and—having to do with rare earths and other things, which we need for our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we appreciate it very much, and I look forward to seeing him. We'll be talking about it, and we'll also be talking about that today with the Prime Minister.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes, I mean, we—as you know, we've already indicated that we'll play our full part in making sure that any deal, if there is one—and I hope there is, and I think this is a historic moment—to make sure it's a lasting deal. And we are about to have a discussion about how we can make that work.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But I have to say this, as I said yesterday, you know, you're talking about a peacekeeping force. We have to make a deal first. Right now, we don't have a deal. We have Russia. We have Ukraine. I think we're very well advanced. I think Russia has been acting very well. We have representative Steve Witkoff and Scott and Marco and J.D. We're all involved, every one of us, and a lot more.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I think we're very well advanced on a deal, but we have not made a deal yet, so I don't like to talk about peacekeeping until we have a deal. I like to get things done. I don't want to give it the bad luck sign. We don't want to do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we've had very good talks with Russia, and we've had very good talks, as you know, with Ukraine.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: United Kingdom/European Union/North Atlantic Treaty Organization/Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you obviously can do business with our Prime Minister, Keir Starmer. You said yesterday that the EU was constructed to "screw" the U.S. when it comes to trade. What can our Prime Minister say to you to persuade you not to impose tariffs on the United Kingdom?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, did I use the word that you said——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I thought——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——that bad word?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. I think so. I'm sorry to repeat it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. [Inaudible]—I'm sorry.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I think that the EU——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You said, "take advantage of."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, I've had problems with the EU because—and we're not talking about—we happen to have a great relationship with you, but we did have and we do have problems with the EU because they've tariffed us. They do it in the form of a VAT tax, which is about 20 percent, and many other taxes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They sue our companies. They sued Apple—got $16- or $17 billion, which was, I think, totally a ridiculous decision. And they're suing Google for a lot of money. They're suing a lot of other companies, and we don't like the way they're treating our people, no. We don't like the way they're treating our companies.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They sell us cars. We don't sell them cars. They don't take our cars. They don't take our— much of our agriculture. And we have a deficit with them of about $350 billion, so I wouldn't say it's been such a great relationship, personally, but other people did because it's politically correct to say that it's been good. But it hasn't been good. And we're going to change that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we are going to have reciprocal tariffs. We're not going to have tariff; we're going to have reciprocal. Whatever they charge us, we're going to charge them. Which, for many years, foolishly—I would have done that, but then, all of a sudden, we had COVID, and we had other things to think about. So it took me a little while to get that on, and we—but we had—in my first 4 years, we had the greatest economy in the history of, I think, the world, but certainly in the history of our country. I think we're going to have that again. But the EU was very, very tough on us in—from the standpoint of trade.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Then you could take it a step further and go into NATO, and that was a very tough situation for us. I mean, that's been a very tough situation because we were paying a disproportionate share, and it wasn't good. So, as you know, they paid hundreds of billions of dollars after I got involved, and they evened it out a little bit, but not very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then, if you look at the war, we're in for $300 billion plus, and they're in for $100 billion. They get their money back, and now we'll get our money back also.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But under Biden, you wouldn't have done that. Biden did a terrible job, I have to say. I hate to say that about somebody that sat here just before me, but he did a terrible, terrible job. That war should have never happened—the war between Russia-Ukraine.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Frankly, October 7 should have never happened—Israel. That should have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What happened there should have never—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Inflation should have never happened. Afghanistan should have never happened. The way they got out—not getting out, but the way they got out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So—but I can say that as far as—we're here for a different reason. We're talking about a very different place. And this is some place that I—I have investments there. I own Turnberry.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes, of course.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I own Aberdeen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And I own a great place called Doonbeg in Ireland. So, you know, I have a great warm spot for your country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. On our trade, obviously, it is fair, balanced, and, in fact, you've got a bit of a surplus. So we're in a different position there. And obviously, we contributed hugely in real—relation to Ukraine. And taken together with Europe, it was about 50 percent——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. It will work out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——when it's all in. President Trump. It will work. It's going to work out. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes. Go ahead, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you. So does that mean there won't be any sanctions on the U.K., then?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We'll have to take a look.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Any tariffs?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I mean, we're going to have a good discussion today. And we have some very talented people on the other side, and we have some people that probably aren't as talented to them, but they're pretty good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Marco, what do you think? [Laughter] Our people are pretty good. No, we're going to have a good discussion, and we'll be talking about that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine/President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, I just wanted to ask, Mr. Starmer—the Prime Minister has said that he believes that Vladimir Putin would be at risk of invading Ukraine again without a sufficient backstop. Do you think that Vladimir Putin would be likely to invade again——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. No.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——in the event of a peace deal?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I don't think so. I think when we have a deal, it's going to be the deal. I don't think if—if I didn't win the election, I don't think we'd be even talking to Putin right now or anybody else. I think it would just—you know, I don't know if you're looking at the stats, but thousands of people are being killed a week—soldiers, mostly, because the towns have been destroyed. But thousands of soldiers. This was a very bad week, by the way. I get——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——I get the stats.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Terrible numbers.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And you're talking about human life, number one. I want to see that—and it doesn't involve American soldiers, but it's Russian and Ukrainian soldiers. And I can think—I think I'm speaking for both.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes, yes. Nobody wants to see that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Number one, we want to see that stop.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And number two, I want to stop paying the kind of money that we're talking about. You know, we're helping, and we're helping NATO, but we're helping a lot more than anybody else, by far, and I want that to stop also.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President—Mr. President, the Europeans——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Jeff [Jeff Mason, Reuters]. Jeff, go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sorry. Mr. President, what would you be willing to do if Vladimir Putin did not stick to the terms of any deal on Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. If he not what?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. He did not stick to the terms of any deal on Ukraine, because he has a history of not sticking to his word when it comes to international agreements.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I think he'll keep his word. I think—I think he's—I've spoken to him. I've known him for a long time now. You know, I've known him—we had to go through the Russian hoax together. That was not a good thing. It's not fair.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That was a rigged deal and had nothing to do with Russia. It was a rigged deal with inside the country, and they had to put up with that too. They put up with a lot. It wasn't just us. They had to put up with it—with a phony story that was made up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I've known him for a long time now, and I think he will—I don't believe he's going to violate his word. I don't think he'll be back—when we make a deal, I think the deal is going to hold.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, they're going to have security. You're going to have security.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. You're going to have soldiers. I know France wants to be there. He's—the President has said he wants to have soldiers there. I don't think we're going to even be necessary.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I don't think there'll be any problem with keeping the deal with the security. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Oh, we're going to discuss this——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Please. Do you want to say something?

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. No, I was just going to say, I mean, the deal, if we get it, is going to be hugely important. I don't think it would have happened if the space hadn't been created for it by yourself.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: But if there's a deal in, we've got to make sure it's a deal that lasts, that it is not temporary, that lasts——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——and that's why we need to make sure that it's secure. And we've lent in and said we'll play our part. And we've talked and we will talk about how we work with yourself, Mr. President, to ensure that this deal is something which is not violated, because it's very important, if there is a deal, we keep it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And that will be—and I think I can say that will be the easy part. That's the part we look forward to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——because putting security there, that's the part we all look forward to.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That's easy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The difficult part is getting the deal made.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. So—but I think we've come a long way. Did you have something?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On a personal level——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. You have such a—he's got such a nice face.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Aww. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. He's smiling. But—no, he's smiling. But watch, he'll ask a total killer question. [Laughter] Those are the ones——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. No, I was going to ask a nice—I was going to ask a nice——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. I've known him a long time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. They're the ones that get you. [Laughter] No, he looks like a nice guy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Oh, that's very kind. Mr. President, it sounds as though one of you completely trusts President Putin and one of you doesn't trust him an inch. Have I got that right? And why do you trust him?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. No, look, you know, it's trust and verify. Let's call it that. And I think we both can be that way. It's—you have to verify, because you never know what's going to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I know a lot of people that you would say no chance that they would ever deceive you, and they're the worst people in the world. I know others that you would guarantee they would deceive you and—you know what?—they're a hundred-percent honorable. So you never know what you're getting.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No, I have confidence that if we make a deal, it's going to hold. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is there anything you can say tomorrow to President Zelenskyy to reassure him that his country's war hasn't been in vain and its sovereignty is not going to be threatened by any deal with Russia?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, you know, he's coming. Perhaps he's already on his way. And we're going to be signing the deal together, probably in front of the media, and we're going to be having a good conversation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No, we want to work with him, President Zelenskyy, she said before. We want to work with him, and we will work with him. I think the President and I actually have had a very good relationship. It maybe got a little bit testy because we wanted to have a little bit of what the European nations had.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, they get their money back by giving money. We don't get the money back. Biden made a deal. He put in $350 billion, and I thought it was a very unfair situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. We're not getting all of ours. I mean, some—quite a bit of ours was gifted. It was given. There were some loans, but mainly it was gifted, actually.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: North Atlantic Treaty Organization/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, the Euro—the Euro—Mr. President, the Europeans want Ukraine to be part of NATO as part of this deal. Are you willing to budge on that at all, or is it a firm no?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I could be very nice and say, "Oh, well, we'll work to it." Look, it's not going to happen. It's just not going to happen. That's what started this whole thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Biden said that, and, all of a sudden, the guns started. That was one of the primary reasons this started.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And this was long before President Putin. They never said—it was an impossibility.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we can say: "Oh, gee. Well, we'll try." But that's something that's just not going to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then the other question you'll ask is about the land. "Will you get your land back?" Well, they've fought long and hard on the land, and you and I will be discussing that, and we're going to certainly try and get as much as we can back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But on the NATO, it's just not—that's not going to happen. Yes, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/Critical Minerals Supply

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you talked about having common ground with Keir Starmer, but there are things you disagree on as well. You described Zelenskyy as a dictator. He describes President Putin as a dictator. Do you see that as a problem?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. The relationship between President Zelenskyy and President Putin is not a good one. You've noticed, right? It's not a good one. It's not a good relationship, and we're going to have to try and work something out. Sometimes that happens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I get along with both. I have a very good relationship with President Putin. I think I have a very good relationship with President Zelenskyy. And now we're—you know, we're doing the deal, and we're going to be in there. We're going to be actually in there, digging our hearts out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And hopefully—you know, we need the rare earth, and we have some here, but we don't have enough. We're—our economy is very strong, and we need a lot of things that, in some cases, we don't have here.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I think we're going to have a very good relationship, but the relationship between them is not the best.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, do you still think that Mr. Zelenskyy is a dictator?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Did I say that? I can't believe I said that. Next question.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.] President Trump. Yes, please. Go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes. George Parker from Financial Times. Can you see any situation where U.S. forces could be deployed as a backstop in a peacekeeping operation in direct confrontation with Russian forces?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, there is a backstop that—you know, first, you're got to have European countries because they're right there. We're very far away. We have an ocean between us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we want to make sure it works. So I don't know—when you say "backstop," you mean a backstop psychologically——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Militarily.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——or militarily or what?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Militarily.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But we are a backstop because we'll be over there. We'll be working in the country. We're going to be—that's a great thing economically for them, because, you know, when you talk about economic development, we're going to have a lot of people over there. So we'll be working in the country. So I don't—I just don't think you're going to have a problem.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think when we have an agreement—you can say whatever you want about security, who's going to do it or—that's going to be a very pleasant conversation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The hard conversation is will we have an agreement, and I think the answer is yes. I think Russia will agree, and I think that—I really believe Ukraine will agree also.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Peacekeeping Forces

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Just to follow up on that. If British troops are in Ukraine keeping the peace and get attacked by Russia, will you come to their aid?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. If the British people are in Ukraine——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. If British soldiers are——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——and they get attacked?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. If British soldiers are in Ukraine keeping the peace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. You know, I've always found about the British: They don't need much help. They can take care of themselves very well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. That sounds like a "no," you'd leave them to it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. You know what? No. It sounds like it's evasive, but it's not evasive. [Laughter] You know, the British are—have been incredible soldiers, incredible military, and they can take care of themselves. But if they need help, I'll always be with the British. Okay? I'll always be with them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But they don't need help. You look at their career, you have done very well over the years, haven't you, huh? Come here.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. We have. I'm very proud of our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Come here.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [President Trump and Prime Minister shook hands.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. And we have—but we've also always been there backing each other up——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——between our two countries. That is why this is the greatest alliance for prosperity and security, I think, the world has ever seen. Whenever necessary, we've absolutely backed each other up, and that's at the core of the relation- ——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Could you take on Russia by yourselves?

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Well—[laughter]. President Trump. All right. One or two more. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, ma'am.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. In his remarks at the Munich Security Conference, Vice President Vance condemned free speech violations in the U.K., particularly. Could you respond? What is your message——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I have an idea.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——to the U.K.?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We have the man right here. Come on. Let's go. [Laughter] Let's go, J.D. Let's—we're putting you on stage.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance. Great. Yes. Look—[laughter]—I said what I said, which is that we do have a—of course, a special relationship with our friends in the U.K. and also with some of our European allies, but we also know that there have been infringements on free

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance
full_topic_context.text: speech that actually affect not just the British—of course, what the British do in their own country is up to them—but also affect American technology companies and, by extension, American citizens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance
full_topic_context.text: So that is something that we'll talk about today at lunch. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. We've had free speech——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On Zelenskyy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. ——for a very, very long time in the United Kingdom. And it will last for a very, very long.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So you don't agree it's under threat, then?

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Starmer. Well, no. I mean, I—certainly, we wouldn't want to reach across

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: U.S. citizens, and we don't. And that's absolutely right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Starmer
full_topic_context.text: But in relation to free speech in the U.K., I'm very proud about our history there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, are there areas, specifically, of Ukraine that you're talking about in giving back—specifically Crimea? It—are—have you gotten to those details yet on such an agreement?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, we—you mean the areas that were taken?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. There are a lot of areas that were taken. Yes, we've talked about it. A lot of the sea line has been taken. And we'll be talking about that, and we're going to see if we can get it back or get a lot of it back for Ukraine if that's possible. We'll be seeing about that. Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much, everybody. Thank you very much. Appreciate it. Thank you.
