full_topic_context.text: [Several Members of Congress spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This also includes our great fire departments throughout the country. Our firemen and women are unbelievable people, and I will never forget them. And besides that, they voted for me in record numbers, so I have no choice.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: One year ago this month, 31-year-old New York police officer Jonathan Diller— unbelievably wonderful person and a great officer—was gunned down at a traffic stop on Long Island. I went to his funeral. The vicious criminal charged with his murder had 21 prior arrests, and they were rough arrests too. He was a real bad one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The thug in the seat next to him had 14 prior arrests and went by the name of "Killer." He was Killer. He killed other people. They say a lot of them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I attended Officer Diller's service, and when I met his wife and 1-year-old son Ryan, it was very inspirational, actually. His widow's name is Stephanie, and she is here tonight. Stephanie, thank you very much, Stephanie. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Stephanie, we're going to make sure that Ryan knows his dad was a true hero—New York's Finest. And we're going to get these cold-blooded killers and repeat offenders off our streets, and we're going to do it fast. Got to stop it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They get out with 28 arrests. They push people into subway trains. They hit people over the head—back of the head with baseball bats. We got to get them out of here.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I've already signed an Executive order requiring a mandatory death penalty for anyone who murders a police officer. And tonight I'm asking Congress to pass that policy into permanent law.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm also asking for a new crime bill, getting tough on repeat offenders—— [Several Members of Congress spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: ——while enhancing protections for America's police officers so they can do their jobs without fear of their lives being totally destroyed. They don't want to be killed. We're not going to let them be killed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several Members of Congress spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Joining us in the gallery tonight is a young man who truly loves our police. His name is D.J. Daniel. He is 13 years old, and he has always dreamed of becoming a police officer.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But in 2018, D.J. was diagnosed with brain cancer. The doctors gave him five months at most to live. That was more than 6 years ago.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Since that time, D.J. and his dad have been on a quest to make his dream come true, and D.J. has been sworn in as an honorary law enforcement officer, actually, a number of times. Pec-—the police love him. The police departments love him.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And tonight, D.J., we're going to do you the biggest honor of them all. I am asking our new Secret Service Director, Sean Curran, to officially make you an agent of the United States Secret Service.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [U.S. Secret Service Director Sean M. Curran presented D.J. Daniel with a Secret Service agent credential.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience members
full_topic_context.text: Audience members. D.J.! D.J.! D.J.!

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you, D.J.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: D.J.'s doctors believe his cancer likely came from a chemical he was exposed to when he was younger. Since 1975, rates of child cancer have increased by more than 40 percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Reversing this trend is one of the top priorities for our new Presidential Commission to make America healthy again, chaired by our new Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience member
full_topic_context.text: Audience member. MAHA, baby!

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. With the name "Kennedy," you would have thought everybody over here would have been cheering. [Laughter] How quickly they forget.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our goal is to get toxins out of our environment, poisons out of our food supply, and keep our children healthy and strong.

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience member
full_topic_context.text: Audience member. [Inaudible]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. As an example, not long ago—and we—you can't even believe these numbers——

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience member
full_topic_context.text: Audience member. [Inaudible]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——1 in 10,000 children had autism—1 in 10,000. And now it's 1 in 36.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's something wrong. One in 36. Think of that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to find out what it is, and there's nobody better than Bobby and all of the people that are working with you—you have the best—to figure out what is going on.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay, Bobby? Good luck. It's a very important job. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My administration is also working to protect our children from toxic ideologies in our schools.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: A few years ago, January Littlejohn and her husband discovered that their daughter's school had secretly socially transitioned their 13-year-old little girl. Teachers and administrators conspired to deceive January and her husband, while encouraging her daughter to use a new name and pronouns—"they/them" pronoun, actually—all without telling January, who is here tonight and is now a courageous advocate against this form of child abuse. January, thank you. Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Stories like this are why, shortly after taking office, I signed an Executive order banning public schools from indoctrinating our children with transgender ideology.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I also signed an order to cut off all taxpayer funding to any institution that engages in the sexual mutilation of our youth. And now I want Congress to pass a bill permanently banning and criminalizing sex changes on children and forever ending the lie that any child is trapped in the wrong body. This is a big lie.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And our message to every child in America is that you are perfect exactly the way God made

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Because we're getting wokeness out of our schools and out of our military, and it's already

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: out, and it's out of our society. We don't want it. Wokeness is trouble. Wokeness is bad. It's gone. It's gone. And we feel so much better for it, don't we? Don't we feel better?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our servicemembers won't be activists and ideologues. They will be fighters and warriors.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They will fight for our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, Pete, congratulations. Secretary of Defense, congratulations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And he's not big into the woke movement, I can tell you. [Laughter] I know him well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I am pleased to report that, in January, the U.S. Army had its single best recruiting month in 15 years and that all armed services are having among the best recruiting results ever in the history of our services. What a difference.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you know it was just a few months ago where the results were exactly the opposite. We couldn't recruit anywhere. We couldn't recruit. Now we're having the best results, just about, that we've ever had. What a tremendous turnaround. It's really a beautiful thing to see. People love our country again. It's very simple. They love our country, and they love being in our military again. So it's a great thing. And thank you very much. Great job. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're joined tonight by a young man, Jason Hartley, who knows the weight of that call of duty. Jason's father, grandfather, and great-grandfather all wore the uniform.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Jason tragically lost his dad, who was also a Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy, when he was just a boy, and now he wants to carry on the family legacy of service. Jason is a senior in high school, a six-letter varsity athlete—a really good athlete, they say—a brilliant student, with a

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: 4.46—that's good—GPA. [Laughter] And his greatest dream is to attend the U.S. Military Academy at West Point.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, Jason, that's a very big deal getting in. That's a hard one to get into. But I'm pleased to inform you that your application has been accepted. You will soon be joining the Corps of Cadet.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you. Jason, you're going to be on the Long Gray Line, Jason.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As Commander in Chief, my focus is on building the most powerful military of the future.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As a first step, I'm asking Congress to fund a state-of-the-art Golden Dome missile defense shield to protect our homeland, all made in the U.S.A.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Ronald Reagan wanted to do it long ago, but the technology just wasn't there, not even close. But now we have the technology. It's incredible, actually. And other place that have—they have it: Israel has it. Other places have it. And the United States should have it too. Right, Tim? Right? They should have it too. So I want to thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it's a very—very important. This is a very dangerous world. We should have it. We want to be protected. And we're going to protect our citizens like never before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: To boost our defense industrial base, we are also going to resurrect the American shipbuilding industry, including commercial shipbuilding and military shipbuilding. And for that purpose, I am announcing tonight that we will create a new Office of Shipbuilding in the White House and offer special tax incentives to bring this industry home to America, where it belongs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We used to make so many ships. We don't make them anymore very much, but we're going to make them very fast, very soon. It will have a huge impact.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: To further enhance our national security, my administration will be reclaiming the Panama Canal, and we've already started doing it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Just today, a large American company announced they are buying both ports around the Panama Canal and lots of other things having to do with the Panama Canal and a couple of other canals.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The Panama Canal was built by Americans for Americans, not for others, but others could use it. But it was built at tremendous cost of American blood and treasure. Thirty-eight thousand workers died building the Panama Canal. They died of malaria. They died of snake bites and mosquitoes. Not a nice place to work. They paid them very highly to go there, knowing there was a 25-percent chance that they would die. The most expensive project, also, that was ever built in our country's history, if you bring it up to modern-day costs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It was given away by the Carter administration for $1, but that agreement has been violated very severely. We didn't give it to China. We gave it to Panama, and we're taking it back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have Marco Rubio in charge. Good luck, Marco. [Laughter] Now we know who to blame if anything goes wrong. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No, Marco has been amazing, and he's going to do a great job. Think of it. He got a hundred votes. You know, he was approved with, actually, 99, but the 100th was this gentleman, and I feel very certain—so, let's assume he got 100 votes. And I'm either very, very happy about that or I'm very concerned about it. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But he's already proven—I mean, he's a great gentleman. He's respected by everybody. And we appreciate you voting for Marco. He's going to do a fantastic job. Thank you. Thank you. He's doing a great job. Great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I also have a message tonight for the incredible people of Greenland. [Laughter] We strongly support your right to determine your own future, and, if you choose, we welcome you into the United States of America.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We need Greenland for national security and even international security, and we're working with everybody involved to try and get it. But we need it, really, for international world security. And I think we're going to get it. One way or the other, we're going to get it. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience member
full_topic_context.text: Audience member. Boo!

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We will keep you safe. We will make you rich. And together, we will take Greenland to heights like you have never thought possible before. It's a very small population, but very, very large piece of land and very, very important for military security.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: America is once again standing strong against the forces of radical Islamic terrorism.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Three and a half years ago, ISIS terrorists killed 13 American servicemembers and countless others in the Abbey Gate bombing during the disastrous and incompetent withdrawal from Afghanistan—not that they were withdrawing; it was the way they withdrew. Perhaps the most embarrassing moment in the history of our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Tonight I am pleased to announce that we have just apprehended the top terrorist responsible for that atrocity, and he is right now on his way here to face the swift sword of American justice.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I want to thank, especially, the Government of Pakistan for helping arrest this monster. This was a very momentous day for those 13 families, who I actually got to know very well,

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: most of them, whose children were murdered, and the many people that were so badly—over 42

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: people—so badly injured on that fateful day in Afghanistan. What a horrible day. Such incompetence was shown that when Putin saw what happened, I guess he said, "Wow, maybe this is my chance." That's how bad it was. Should have never happened. Grossly incompetent people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I spoke to many of the parents and loved ones, and they're all in our hearts tonight. Just spoke to them on the phone. We had a big call. Every one of them called, and everybody was on the line, and they did nothing but cry with happiness. They were very happy—as happy as you can be under those circumstances. Their child, brother, sister, son, daughter was killed for no reason whatsoever.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In the Middle East, we're bringing back our hostages from Gaza. In my first term, we achieved one of the most groundbreaking peace agreements in generations: the Abraham Accords.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And now we're going to build on that foundation to create a more peaceful and prosperous future for the entire region. A lot of things are happening in the Middle East. People haven't been talking about that so much lately with everything going on with Ukraine and Russia, but a lot of things are happening in the Middle East. It's a rough neighborhood, actually.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm also working tirelessly to end the savage conflict in Ukraine. Millions of Ukrainians and Russians have been needlessly killed or wounded in this horrific and brutal conflict with no end in sight.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The United States has sent hundreds of billions of dollars to support Ukraine's defense with no security, with no anything.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Do you want to keep it going for another 5 years?

full_topic_context.speaker: Senator Elizabeth A. Warren
full_topic_context.text: Senator Elizabeth A. Warren. Yes!

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes. Yes, you—you would say—Pocahontas says, "Yes." [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience members
full_topic_context.text: Audience members. Boo!

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Two thousand people are being killed every single week—more than that. They're Russian young people. They're Ukrainian young people. They're not Americans. But I want it to stop.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Meanwhile, Europe has sadly spent more money buying Russian oil and gas than they have spent on defending Ukraine, by far. Think of that. They've spent more buying Russian oil and gas than they have defending. And we've spent, perhaps, $350 billion. Like taking candy from a baby, that's what happened. And they've spent $100 billion. What a difference that is. And we have an ocean separating us, and they don't.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we're getting along very well with them, and lots of good things are happening.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Biden has authorized more money in this fight than Europe has spent by billions and billions of dollars. It's hard to believe that they wouldn't have stopped it and said, at some point: "Come on. Let's equalize. You've got to be equal to us." But that didn't happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Earlier today, I received an important letter from President Zelenskyy of Ukraine. The letter reads, "Ukraine is ready to come to the negotiating table as soon as possible to bring lasting peace closer." "Nobody wants peace more than the Ukrainians," he said. "My team and I stand ready to work under President Trump's strong leadership to get a peace that lasts. We do really value how much America has done to help Ukraine maintain its sovereignty and independence. Regarding the agreement on minerals and security, Ukraine is ready to sign it at any time that is convenient for you."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I appreciate that he sent this letter. Just got it a little while ago.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Simultaneously, we've had serious discussions with Russia and have received strong signals that they are ready for peace. Wouldn't that be beautiful? Wouldn't that be beautiful? Wouldn't that be beautiful?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's time to stop this madness. It's time to halt the killing. It's time to end this senseless war.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If you want to end wars, you have to talk to both sides.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Nearly 4 years ago, amid rising tensions, a history teacher named Marc Fogel was detained in Russia and sentenced to 14 years in a penal colony. Rough stuff.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The previous administration barely lifted a finger to help him. They knew he was innocent, but they had no idea where to begin. But last summer, I promised his 95-year-old mother, Malphine, that we would bring her boy safely back home.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: After 22 days in office, I did just that, and they are here tonight. To Marc and his great mom, we are delighted to have you safe and sound and with us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As fate would have it, Marc Fogel was born in a small, rural town—in Butler, Pennsylvania—have you heard of it?—where his mother has lived for the past 78 years. I just happened to go there last July 13 for a rally. [Laughter] That was not pleasant. [Laughter] And that is where I met his beautiful mom, right before I walked onto that stage. And I told her I would not forget what she said about her son. And I never did, did I? Never forgot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Less than 10 minutes later, at that same rally, gunfire rang out, and a sick and deranged assassin unloaded eight bullets from his sniper's perch into a crowd of many thousands of people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My life was saved by a fraction of an inch, but some were not so lucky. Corey Comperatore was a firefighter, a veteran, a Christian, a husband, a devoted father, and, above all, a protector.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When the sound of gunshots pierced the air—it was a horrible sound—Corey knew instantly what it was and what to do. He threw himself on top of his wife and daughters and shielded them from the bullets with his own body.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Corey was hit really hard. You know the story from there. He sacrificed his life to save theirs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Two others—very fine people—were also seriously hit. But thankfully, with the help of two great country doctors, we thought they were gone, and they were saved. So those doctors had great talent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're joined by Corey's wife Helen, who was his high school sweetheart, and their two beloved daughters Allyson and Kaylee. Thank you. To Helen, Allyson, and Kaylee, Corey is looking down on his three beautiful ladies right now, and he is cheering you on. He loves you. He is cheering you on.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Corey was taken from us much too soon, but his destiny was to leave us all with a shining example of the selfless devotion of a true American patriot. It was love like Corey's that built our country, and it's love like Corey's that is going to make our country more majestic than ever before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I believe that my life was saved that day in Butler for a very good reason. I was saved by God to make America great again. I believe that. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: From the patriots of Lexington and Concord to the heroes of Gettysburg and Normandy, from the warriors who crossed the Delaware to the trailblazers who climbed the Rockies, and from the legends who soared at Kitty Hawk to the astronauts who touched the Moon, Americans have always been the people who defied all odds, transcended all dangers, made the most extraordinary sacrifices, and did whatever it took to defend our children, our country, and our freedom.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And as we have seen in this Chamber tonight, that same strength, faith, love, and spirit is still alive and thriving in the hearts of the American people. Despite the best efforts of those who would try to censor us, silence us, break us, destroy us, Americans are today a proud, free, sovereign, and independent nation that will always be free, and we will fight for it till death.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will never let anything happen to our beloved country, because we are a country of doers, dreamers, fighters, and survivors.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our ancestors crossed a vast ocean, strode into the unknown wilderness, and carved their fortunes from the rock and soil of a perilous and very dangerous frontier. They chased our destiny across a boundless continent. They built the railroads, laid the highways, and graced the world with American marvels, like the Empire State Building, the mighty Hoover Dam, and the towering Golden Gate Bridge.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They lit the world with electricity, broke free of the force of gravity, fired up the engines of American industry, vanquished the Communists, Fascists, and Marxists all over the world, and gave us countless modern wonders sculpted out of iron, glass, and steel.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We stand on the shoulders of these pioneers who won and built the modern age, these workers who poured their sweat into the skylines of our cities, these warriors who shed their blood on fields of battle and gave everything they had for our rights and for our freedom.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now it is our time to take up the righteous cause of American liberty, and it is our turn to take America's destiny into our own hands and begin the most thrilling days in the history of our country. This will be our greatest era.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: With God's help, over the next 4 years, we are going to lead this Nation even higher, and we are going to forge the freest, most advanced, most dynamic, and most dominant civilization ever to exist on the face of this Earth.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We are going to create the highest quality of life, build the safest and wealthiest and healthiest and most vital communities anywhere in the world. We are going to conquer the vast frontiers of science, and we are going to lead humanity into space and plant the American flag on the planet Mars and even far beyond.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, through it all, we are going to rediscover the unstoppable power of the American spirit, and we are going to renew unlimited promise of the American dream.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Every single day, we will stand up and we will fight, fight, fight for the country our citizens believe in and for the country our people deserve. Thank you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience members
full_topic_context.text: Audience members. Fight! Fight! Fight!

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. My fellow Americans, get ready for an incredible future, because the golden age of America has only just begun. It will be like nothing that has ever been seen before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you, God bless you, and God bless America. Thank you. Thank you, everybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you very much. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much. Appreciate it. [Applause] Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.text: Temporary Protected Status/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you considering revoking the TPS for the Ukrainians who live here in the U.S.?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. What about it?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you considering revoking the TPS status for the more than 200,000 Ukrainians who live here in the U.S.?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. What are you saying? I don't——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter

full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes.

full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you still believe him when he tells you that he wants peace?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, no, I believe him. I believe him. I think we're doing very well with Russia, but, right now, they're bombing the hell out of Ukraine. And Ukraine, I'm finding it more difficult, frankly, to deal with Ukraine. And——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Than with Russia?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And they don't have the cards. They don't have the cards.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As you know, we're meeting in Saudi Arabia on—sometime next week, early, and we're talking. I mean, they're—and they're bombing the hell out of them right now.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I put a statement in—a very strong statement: "Can't do that. You can't do that."

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Trying to—we're trying to help them. And Ukraine has to get on the ball and get a job done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Michael, could you come up here? I see Michael back there. Good. I'm glad. He's traveling all over the world. I just saw him come in the door.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Michael G. Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Michael G. Waltz. Yes. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Could you give a little definition of what's going on, please?

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Waltz. Sure.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: Well, the President has been crystal clear, and he's been clear to all sides: The fighting has to stop. Both sides need to get to the table.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: We had a good engagement at—both leaders have said only President Trump could do so, and only he has been able to do so. We had an initial engagement with the Russians. The Ukrainians had a great opportunity to bind our economies together through that mineral deal. Unfortunately, that didn't go so well, but we think we're going to get things back on track.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Rubio, myself, and the Ukrainian delegation will be meeting in Saudi Arabia next week to get these talks back on track, get a cease-fire in place, and drive peace home—

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: ——under President Trump's leadership.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you put out on that social——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think both parties want to settle.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I think if I wasn't President, this war would have had no chance of settlement. Zero chance. But I think we're going to get it settled and stopped. We got to stop. They're losing, on average, 2,000 soldiers a week.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. That's a lot of soldiers. Do you agree, Peter?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. It's a lot of soldiers on both sides, I agree.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Do you, Mr. President, think that Vladimir Putin is taking advantage of the U.S. pause right now on intelligence and military aid to Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, I actually think he's doing what anybody else would do. I think he's—I think he wants to get it stopped and settled. And I think he's hitting them harder than—than he's been hitting them, and I think probably anybody in that position would be doing that right now. He wants to get it ended. And I think Ukraine wants to get it ended, but I don't see—it's crazy. They're taking tremendous punishment. I don't quite get it, but I suspect, Michael, he probably wants to get it ended.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Waltz. He does, Mr. President. The Russians are taking incredible losses on the front, as the President has said.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. They both are.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Waltz. This is a meat grinder of people, of materiel, of national treasure, and no one else has any solutions, except to let this war continue forever.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: But I'll add, the President has had multiple conversations and a visit from President Macron of France, Prime Minister Starmer of the United Kingdom. full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: We will engage in the shuttle diplomacy, and we will continue to use his leadership and what leverage we have to get both sides to the peace table.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Waltz. It's not going to be easy, but President Trump is absolutely——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. This war should have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Waltz. ——going to get it done. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. It would have never happened if I were President. But it did happen, so—a lot of other things shouldn't have happened too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We shouldn't have 21 million people pouring into our country through open borders, many of whom are criminals, very bad criminals, including murderers, thousands of murderers. Many killed far more than one person, and they're roaming our streets. But Tom Homan and Kristi Noem are doing an incredible job, and we're getting them out of here. And we'll get them out. We'll get them all out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But all these things shouldn't have happened. We shouldn't have inflation. We shouldn't have had this horrible inflation, where the prices have gone up. Look at eggs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're doing a good job. We're doing a good job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, in regards to the pause on military assistance to Ukraine, you put out on your social media post today that Russia is "pounding Ukraine."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Why not provide Ukraine with air defenses? And what happens, Mr. President, when Ukraine runs out of the Patriot——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, because——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——missile batteries?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes. Yes. Good question.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Because I have to know that they want to settle. I don't know that they want to settle. If they don't want to settle, we're out of there, because we want them to settle. And I'm doing it to stop death. More important than anything else. Secondarily, way down the line, is the money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're in for $350 billion, and Europe is in for $100 billion. They should be in for the same or more than us. And you know, I watched, over the last week or so, what's going on in Europe. This thing could end up in World War III if we don't get it settled. This could really end up in a World War III. We've got to get it settled.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia/Hamas Attacks of October 7, 2023, on Israel/Iran

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Two questions. One, on peace. Why don't you think any other European countries are offering a peace deal? It seems like no one has come to the table for peace, except for you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes. It's a very good question. Sometimes questions aren't answerable.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're in a very unusual position. They don't know how to end the war. I think I do know how to end the war. Despite the "Russia, Russia, Russia" hoax, I've always had a good relationship with Putin. And you know, he wants to end the war. He wants to end it, and I think

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: he's going to be more generous than he has to be. And that's pretty good. That means a lot of good things, because, frankly, you could have made a great deal if you—if this war never started, you could have made a great deal. I don't know that anything would have had to be given up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This was not a war that was going to start, Brian. And it didn't start. For 4 years, it—you know, somebody said, "Well, how do we know that?" Well, for 4 years, it didn't start.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I used to speak to Vladimir about it. I used to speak to him about it at length. It was the apple of his eye, but there was no way he was going in. And he knew, you know, there were going to be consequences. But it did start.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I mean, think of—think of what happened. Inflation. You have the war with Ukraine and Russia. That wouldn't have happened. October 7 would have never happened—Israel. They had no money. Iran had no money. Iran was stone-cold broke, and now they have a lot of money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But—and that's going to be the next thing you'll be talking about is Iran—what's going to happen with Iran. And there'll be some interesting days ahead. That's all I can tell you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we're down to final strokes with Iran. That's going to be an interesting time. And we'll see what happens. But we're down to the final moments. We're at final moments. You can't let them have a nuclear weapon.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I would—I think that I would have had a deal within 1 month after the rigged election of 2020. They were all set to make a deal. And then, when I lost, they saw this person, who is a stupid person, very stupid person, and they said, "Let's not make a deal." And they were right. He took the sanctions off. full_topic_context.text: And I have a choice. I could just coast, and eventually, there'd be a blowup down the road, maybe a long way. But we owe $36 trillion, and we're going to get it back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're the biggest. We're the best. And I'm very optimistic. I have to tell you, I'm very optimistic about the country, much more optimistic this way than if I did it the easy way. I could have done it the easy way. I could have coasted.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Biden left us a mess. He left us tremendous inflation, tremendously high cost of products. He left us a mess.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But he also left us a mess with millions of people that poured into our country that are criminals. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But one of the things we're changing is, we're going to make our country really wealthy again. We're going to bring our jobs back. Right now we're like a chicken that's being plucked at from all over the world. We're not going to let that happen anymore.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter

full_topic_context.text: Now we have to go to Russia and hope President—hopefully, President Putin will agree to that also, and we can get this show on the road. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I think—I think it's a very big——

full_topic_context.text: Q. Is Zelenskyy invited back to the White House?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Federal Workforce Reduction Efforts/Department of Education

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the Department of Education, sir. Would you describe for us, is this meeting your vision by cutting about half the workforce? And what responsibility do you feel to the civil servants who have now lost their jobs? Many of them worked at the Department of Education—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——during your first term.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Sure, I do—I feel very badly, and—but many of them don't work at all.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Many of them never showed up to work. Many of them——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. They had—they had permission to work——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Many of them——

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——from home, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——never showed up to work, Kelly [Kelly O'Donnell, NBC News], and—unfortunately—and that's not good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And when we cut—you know, we go—and that's what—I had a number of meetings with a lot of people over the last couple of months. When we cut, we want to cut, but we want to cut the people that aren't working or doing—not doing a good job. We're keeping the best people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Linda McMahon is a real professional, a very—actually, a very sophisticated businessperson, and she cut a large number, but she kept the best people. And we'll see how it all works out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But our country was run very badly. I mean, whether it was that or contracts that were signed that were so bad—so obviously bad. And I go through them in speeches. I could go through them all day long. I could read—for billions and hundreds of billions of dollars. And all of that fat and waste and fraud and abuse is being taken out. But it's incredible what's happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, Department of Education is—maybe more so than any other place has a lot of people they can be cut. They're, number one, not showing up to work. Number two, they're not doing a good job. And if you take a look at our education process—and if you look at the charts, because they have numerous charts where they do the top 40—we're at number 37, 38, 39, and 40. And recently, they hit—during Biden's last few days, they hit last. So they were number 40. And yet we're number one in cost per pupil. So it's pretty bad. But—we have a——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, a number of the States that——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We have a dream. And you know what the dream is? We're going to move the Department of Education. We're going to move education into the States, so that the States— instead of bureaucrats working in Washington—so that the States can run education.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you have Norway. You have Denmark. You have Sweden. You have various— Finland—you have various countries that do very well. You also have China that does very well in education, which is a pretty big tribute to China, I must say—1.4 billion, and they're in the top 10, and it's pretty amazing. So we can't blame size anymore.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, normally you'd blame size. It's too big. How can you do it? But China does it. So we think, when you move it back to Iowa and Indiana and all the States that run so well—there's so many. I could name 30, maybe—almost 40. Those will be as good as Denmark. Those will be as good as Norway, and they'll be as good as any of these—I believe they'll be as good as any.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, then you're going to have 10 that won't be so great. You're going to have five that will not be good at all, but we'll work with them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Well, some States, sir, don't——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And we'll get them to be good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——have the tax base to support it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But what we want to do is always school choice, but we're going to do school choice, and we're doing it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we want education to be moved back where the States run education, where the parents of the children will be running education, where Governors that are doing a very good job will be running education, not run—I drive through the city, and I see, like, so many buildings— Department of Education, Department of—big buildings—the Department—and by the way, they're empty. Nobody shows up to work. So I think Linda did a very good job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, do you——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——do you have a meeting with Vladimir Putin scheduled or a conversation? What would be your message to him—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I won't comment on that, but we had a great success yesterday. We have a full cease-fire when it—if it kicks in. We have to see. It's up to Russia now. But we've had a good relationship with both parties, actually, and we'll see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We'll be knowing—people are going to Russia right now as we speak. And hopefully, we can get a cease-fire from Russia. And if we do, I think that would be 80 percent of the way to getting this——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. Absolutely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——horrible bloodbath finished. It's a bloodbath that's taking place over there. On average, 2- to 3,000 young people a week are being killed in that stupid war that would have never happened if I were President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we have people going over there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Mr. VP, do you have anything to say about it? Because you're very much involved. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President James D. "J.D." Vance. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. What's going to happened?

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. Well, we've got some conversations that are happening on the phone and in person with some of our representatives over the next couple of days. As the President said, we think that we're in a very good place where the Ukrainians have agreed to a cease-fire, and we're now going to see whether we can get the Russians to agree to a cease-fire too. And we'll certainly have news on that when we—when we find out that news.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Inflation

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you confident—are you confident that Vladimir Putin will keep the cease-fire, considering that he's broken them in the past before?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I haven't—we haven't spoken to him yet with substance, because we just found out and we just were able to get Ukraine to agree. So we're going to know very soon. I've gotten some positive messages, but a positive message means nothing. This is a——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What leverage do you have over them——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——very serious situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——if they don't comply?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. This is a situation that could lead to World War III, and Biden should have never let it happen. Incompetence allowed this to happen. This shouldn't have happened. October 7 in the Middle East should have never happened, with Israel. The horrible leaving—the way they left Afghanistan should have never happened. Inflation should have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we have great inflation numbers, by the way. Just got released. Inflation is way down. And it's based on what we've done, and we've done it in a very short period of time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we had virtually no inflation. For 4 years, we had almost no inflation. And when these characters took over, we went from no inflation to the worst inflation probably in the history of our country. So it's very interesting.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And by the way, I have to speak of inflation. I love these socks. What's with these socks? [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Show us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Vice President Vance
full_topic_context.text: Vice President Vance. It's in honor of the Taoiseach, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. [Inaudible]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Show us, Mr. Vice President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I'm trying to stay focused, but I'm very impressed with the VP's socks. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Northern Ireland/Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What does it say to you that the United States is recognized as having such an important role in the peace process, and yet half the parties from the Northern Ireland government have decided not to come to the St. Patrick's Day celebrations?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. They haven't—what?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. They haven't come over. They're boycotting the St. Patrick's Day celebrations in Ireland.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. What are they boycotting?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. They are talking about your position on Gaza as one of the reasons why——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Oh, I haven't heard that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——they've decided to stay away.

full_topic_context.speaker: Mixed
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I really haven't heard that. Look—— Prime Minister Martin. Could—could I just say, as a—— President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. ——to pay tribute to the President on the peace initiatives. The one thing we've learned in Ireland about the peace process that you've just spoken about—and I recall back in the early nineties when the first tentative steps to get peace in Ireland, people criticized people like John Hume or people like Albert Reynolds—the then-Taoiseach.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: But they kept going. And when we got that cease-fire in '93—okay, it took a number of years to get the comprehensive peace settlement, but, again, the guns, more or less, largely went silent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: The war in Ukraine is a devastating war on young people. And I think that very simple, straightforward narrative——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. ——is to be commended. We all have children. We—I mean, we— shocked at the prospect of young people losing their lives in that number, be they Ukrainian, be

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: they Russian, whatever. Anything we can do to stop the violence, I think, is an extremely positive thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: And there will be all sorts of people having qualifications and all the rest of it. It's our job then to work on it and to try and build it—Europe, U.S., and every——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I will say—and thank you for that. But I will say, last week, 2,500 young people died while we sit here and talk——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——and while they talk about peace. But they've been talking about peace—this should have never happened. This war should have never happened. It would have never happened if I was President. That's what makes me more angry than anything else, because you've had far more people die than they report—then these people report——

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. The media report.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——for whatever reason. But you had far more people—the numbers are far more devastating. You'll find that out someday.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it doesn't affect you very much. You're—they're not Irish, and they're not from my country. They're from Russia, mostly—almost all from Russia—and from Ukraine. And people could say: "Why are you doing this? Why are you involved in that?" Because they're—2,000 people a week are dying, and they have families, and they have mothers, and they have fathers, and they have sisters, and they have brothers and friends, and they're dying. And I've seen the pictures—the satellite pictures that we see all the time, and it looks like Gettysburg in its prime, because that was, they say, one of the most horrific battles ever.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You have kids lying all over these fields that are dead because the weapons today are unbelievable, between drones and various types of guns. I'm not even talking about—beyond that, with the—with the big babies. You understand what I mean.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I hate to even mention the name—the nuclear name. I hate to mention it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you have weapons today that are so powerful. And I see kids—every week, I see pictures of kids laying all over the field, dead. They're dead. Beautiful kids, they're dead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they're not from here, and they're not from where you are, but he's working very hard. We're all working hard to get this thing finished. It's crazy. Over nothing, and it's not going to go anywhere. It's just a terrible situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think we have a chance to get it done. So we've gotten——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We've gotten half of it as a cease-fire. And if we can get Russia to stop, and then we have a full cease-fire, and I think it will never go back to war. I think something will happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.] Say it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Nord Stream 2 Natural Gas Pipeline Between Russia and Germany/President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You said earlier that it is now up to Russia, in terms of a cease-fire.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is there anything you can do in terms of pressuring Russia or——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Q. ——
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——in terms of sanctions or—what can you do?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, we can, but I hope it's not going to be necessary. Sure, we can pressure. We can do that with Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Remember this: Russia took Georgia from Bush, right? They took Crimea from a man named Obama—Barack Hussein Obama, right? They're trying to take the whole thing from Biden. They're going for the whole ball of wax.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Who was the only one that ever took anything from? Trump. And in fact, I'm the one that stopped Nord Stream 2, the pipeline. The biggest pipeline anywhere in the world. I stopped it. It was dead. And then Biden got in, and he approved it. Nobody mentions that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What I did to Russia was very tough. I was the toughest ever. But nope, they never took anything from me. They took them from Obama and Bush, and they took it from Sleepy Joe Biden. With Biden, they wanted to take the whole country, but I think I've stopped that, but we'll see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But yes, there are things you could do that—that wouldn't be pleasant. In a financial sense— I can do things financially that would be very bad for Russia. I don't want to do that because I want to get peace. I want to see peace, and we'll see. But in a financial sense, yes, we could do things very bad for Russia. It would be devastating for Russia. But I don't want to do that because I want to see peace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're getting close to maybe getting something done. We've got Ukraine done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And as you know, I've always said that Ukraine might have been the more difficult party. You saw—you were here a week ago when some interesting things happened. I had somebody that didn't seem to want peace. Now he's agreed to peace. So we'll see what happens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, what about on Gaza?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Hey.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Brian [Brian Glenn, Real America's Voice]. Brian.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes, thanks.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. First, we'll congratulate you on your lower inflation core rates.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Gas prices going down, airline prices going down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: This is for our Irish gentleman here, if I can see him real quickly. Welcome to the United States. You look great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Nice suit. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's a—now you're feeling good. He knows.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. That's compliments too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. President Trump ran on MAGA—"Make America Great Again." If you could run on MIGA, "Make Ireland Great Again," what would your number-one issue be for people in Ireland right now to make your country stronger?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: And then I've got a two-part question to that as well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. Yes. The number-one issue in Ireland is housing, to be honest. And I think it was correctly pointed out, we've got to build more houses. We've got to build them faster to give the young people of Ireland an opportunity to afford to buy a house or to afford to rent a house.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: We have a lot of other good things happening. That's my number-one priority.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Wonderful. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you trying to infer, Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, thank you so much. You spoke to Vladimir Putin for quite a while on the phone.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So I want to know your assessment. When you take this deal to him now, what do you— how do you assess the chances of Putin saying yes?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I have no assessment, and I don't go by chances.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think it makes sense for Russia. A lot of downside for Russia too. And we have a very complex situation solved on one side, pretty much solved. We've also discussed land and other things that, you know, go with it. We're not just doing it and saying "cease-fire." We don't know what's happening.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We know the areas of land we're talking about, whether it's pulled back or not pulled back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we've discussed a lot of the details of what has to go because we don't want to be wasting time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We don't want to be wasting time while people are dying. I mean, as we're sitting here, you probably had two people die on that very open field. You know, it's dead flat. It's great farmland, and it's dead flat. There's no protection.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The only thing that stops a bullet is a human body, and these are bodies that are young people, and they're stopping a lot of bullets, because a lot of bullets are flying across those level fields—dead flat, no protection whatsoever. It is a disaster.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And so I hope he's going to have a cease-fire. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And you are using—you are using the American leverage to get a lot of political issues that you want across, right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I don't want to get into that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And I'm wondering——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But if I had to, I'm the only one that's dealt with him successfully.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Everyone else went through it. Bush didn't deal with him successfully. He dealt with him terribly. He got ripped off.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Obama was a disaster. You know——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So what leverage do you, sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——they had with Obama—he gave them sheets, and I gave them anti- tank missiles. You know that, right? It's called Javelin. You know the Javelin? I'm the one that gave them the Javelins. People don't say that. And then, they say, "Oh, Trump has a great relationship with Russia."

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But so what leverage do you have to use? But—Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I'm the one that gave them the Javelins. Obama gave them sheets. That's an expression. He gave sheets; I gave Javelins. So——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, how worried—how worried should the—how worried should the undocumented Irish be about your administration that you don't round them up and send them home again?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Oh, I think the Irish love Trump. We won the Irish with a tremendous amount of vote. I want to thank you very much. We won in the eighties with Irish. I got the Irish vote.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think I have it locked up pretty good, unless I did something very stupid, like drained your company—your wonderful place of all of its companies. If I drained Ireland of all the companies—maybe I'd lose the Irish vote. I don't know. [Laughter] But right now—no, I love—I love your—I love it. I've been there many times, as you know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Martin
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Martin. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And we don't want to do anything to hurt Ireland. We want to—but we do want fairness, and—and he understands that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on the markets. You often——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. No, that's enough, Kelly. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, is there anything that the Taoiseach could say to you today that would dissuade you from going ahead with the 25-percent tariffs on EU goods?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I can't hear.
