full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Hello, everybody. It's great to be with a friend of mine, who was Prime Minister of the Netherlands, so I got to know him very well. We had a great relationship always.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Absolutely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Mark Rutte. Now he's Secretary General of NATO and doing a fantastic job. Everybody—every report I've gotten is what a great job he did. And I'm not at all surprised when I hear it. We had to support him, and we supported him as soon as I heard the name.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But he was a fantastic Prime Minister, and he's doing a fantastic job—an even tougher job. Which is tougher: being the Prime Minister of Netherlands or——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. This job is quite tough. Yes. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. I would think this is a little tougher.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. But Dutch politics is also brutal. So—[laughter].

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes. But this is pretty tough.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But you're doing—you're doing good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We're going to be discussing a lot of things. Obviously, we'll be discussing what's happening with respect to Ukraine and Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: At this moment, we have people talking in Russia. We have representatives over there— Steve Witkoff and others. And they're in very serious discussions. As you know, Ukraine has agreed, subject to this—what's happening today—to a complete cease-fire, and we hope Russia will do the same.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thousands of people are being killed—young people, usually, mostly—young people. We were just talking about it. Thousands of young people are being killed a week, and we want to see that stop. And they're not Americans, and they're not from the Netherlands for the most part——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. No.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. They're not from—they're from Russia and they're from Ukraine, but they're people. And I think everybody feels the same way. We want it to stop.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's also a tremendous cost to the United States and to other countries. And it's something that would have never happened if I were President, and it makes me very angry to see that it did happen. But it happened, and we have to stop it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Mark has done some really good work over the last week. We've been working together, and he's done some really good work. So I'm very happy about that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We'll also be talking about trade and various other things, and I think we'll have a very, very strong day. We're going to have lunch afterwards. That will go. And then we'll see you all later.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, Mark, would you like to say something?

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes. First of all, thank you so much, Mr. President, dear Donald, again for hosting me and—but also for taking time in Florida a couple of weeks after you——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Right. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——you were reelected.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. And of course, our phone call a couple of weeks ago. And I must say, Trump 45—you basically—you originated the fact that in Europe we are now spending, when you take it to aggregate, $700 billion more on defense——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——than when you came in office in 2016—in 2017. But that was Trump 45. But, when look at Trump 47——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Going to be hard to top. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——what happened the last couple of weeks is really staggering. The Europeans committing to a package of $800 billion defense spending. The Germans now—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——potentially up to half a trillion extra in defense spending. And then, of course, you have Keir Starmer here, the British Prime Minister, and others all committing to much higher defense spending.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: They're not there. We need to do more. But I really want to work together with you in a runup to The Hague summit to make sure that we will have a NATO which is really reinvigorated under your leadership. And we are getting there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: We also discussed defense production, because we need to produce more weaponry. We are not doing enough—not in the U.S., not in Europe. And we are lagging behind when you compare to the Russians and the Chinese. And you have a huge defense industrial base, Europeans buying

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: —four times more here than the other—the other way around, which is good, because you have a strong defense industry.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: But we need to do more there to make sure that we ramp up production and kill the red tape.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: So I would love to work with you on that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: And finally, Ukraine, you broke the deadlock. As you said, all the killing, the young people dying, cities getting destroyed. The fact that you did that, that you started the dialogue with the Russians and the successful talks in Saudi Arabia now with the Ukrainians—I really want to commend you for this.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: So, well, the Hague is my hometown. I'd love to host you there in the summer and work together to make sure that——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We'll do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——that will be a splash, a real success, projecting American power on the world stage.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. What Mark is saying is: When I first went to NATO, my first meeting, I noticed that very few people were paying. And if they were, they weren't paying their fair share. There were only seven countries that were paying what they were supposed to be paying, which was—

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. It's even worse; there were three.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. That's even worse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. It could be even worse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. But there were just very few countries that were paying. And even the paying, they—it was at 2 percent, which is too low. It should be higher. It should be quite a bit higher.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you had Poland and—I remember Poland was actually paying a little bit more than they were supposed to, which was—very impressed with. And they've been actually terrific and some of the others. But most of them weren't paying or they were paying very little.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I didn't think it was appropriate to bring it up there, but I said, "It's going to be brought up at my next meeting." And my next meeting—you know, the first meeting, you want to give them a little break. The second meeting, it began.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I was able to raise——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. You did. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——hundreds of billions of dollars. I just said, "We're not going to be involved with you if you're not going to pay." And the money started pouring in. And NATO became much stronger because of my actions and working along with a lot of people, including Mark.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But they would not pay for other Presidents. And other—I don't think other Presidents even knew that they weren't paid. I asked—first question, "Has everybody paid up?" And literally, I mean, they showed—they told me seven. You could be right. It could be three. But—that makes it even worse—but they just weren't paying.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I said: "No, I won't protect if you're not paying. If you're delinquent or if the money isn't paid, why would we do that?"

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And as soon as I said that, got a little hit from the press, because they said, "Oh, gee, that's not very nice." But if you said the other, nobody would have paid. And the money started coming in by the billions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you know, hundreds of billions of dollars flowed into NATO, and NATO became strong.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And you remember that. And your predecessor, who I thought was a very good man actually.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Absolutely. Jens Stoltenberg. He sends his best greetings.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes. He was terrific.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Stoltenberg, Secretary General.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Great man.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And he made the statement that when Trump came in, the money started coming in like we never saw before. Hundreds of—it was actually probably close to $600 billion came in. And NATO became strong from that standpoint.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And now we have to use it wisely. And we have to get this war over with. And you'll be back to a normal—much more normal life.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And maybe we're close. We're getting words that things are going okay in Russia, and it doesn't mean anything until we hear what the final outcome is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But they have very serious discussions going on right now with President Putin and others. And hopefully, they all want to end this nightmare. It's a nightmare. It's a horrible thing, when you look. I get pictures every week. They give me the pictures of the battlefield, which I almost don't want to see. It's so horrible to see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. It's so terrible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Young people laying—arms and legs and heads laying all over the field.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's the most terrible thing that you'll ever see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's got to stop. These are young people with mothers and fathers and sisters and brothers and friends, and it's got to stop.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we, hopefully, are going to be in a good position sometime today to have a good idea. We'll have—we know where we are with Ukraine, and we are getting good signals outside of Russia as to where we are with Russia, and hopefully, they'll do the right thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's a really—humanity—we're talking about humanity. We're not talking about the money. But then you add the money to it, and you know, hundreds of billions of dollars is being spent and, really, wasted so unnecessarily. It should have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So it's an honor to have you here. They picked a great gentleman. I'll tell you, that was—I was so happy to hear, because you had somebody—Stoltenberg was really good. And you have somebody that's going to do an incredible job. And I was so much in favor of you, you have no idea.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They had another person that I did not like. [Laughter] I was not happy. And I think I kept him from—you know what I'm talking about. I said, "This is the right man to do it." And he really did. He was a great Prime Minister of the Netherlands. He did a great job. And that's what he's doing right now.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So thank you, everybody, for being here. And very great honor to have you. And we even have some of our great energy people here today, right? We have our—the Governor, and we have Chris. You know Chris.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes. Absolutely.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. He's supposed to be the most talented man in the world of energy, according to the Governor. [Laughter] So I don't know if he's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have—General, you've been fantastic. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have all—a lot of good people that won't be so much involved with this, but they wanted to see what was happening. It's become a little bit of a show—[laughter]—but we wanted—they wanted to see what was happening. And—and I think a lot of good things are happening.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, with that, if anybody would have a question.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, several reporters began asking questions at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, on Russia.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Please, go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Vladimir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine/North Atlantic Treaty Organization

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sorry. Sorry, Mary [Mary Bruce, ABC News]. Steve Witkoff's trip to Moscow, you spoke about it. What sort of agreement do you hope he comes away from there with?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, we'd like to see a cease-fire from Russia. And we have, you know, not been working in the dark. We've been discussing with Ukraine land and—pieces of land that would be kept and lost and all of the other elements of a final agreement.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's a power plant involved—you know, a very big power plant involved. Who's going to get the power plant and who's going to get this and that. And so, you know, it's—it's not an easy process.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But phase one is the cease-fire. A lot of the individual subjects have been discussed though. You know, we've been discussing concepts of land, because you don't want to waste time with the ceasefire if—if it's not going to mean anything. So we're saying: "Look, this is what you can get. This is what you can't get."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They discussed NATO and being in NATO, and everybody knows what the answer to that is. They've known that answer for 40 years, in all fairness.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So a lot of the details of a final agreement have actually been discussed. Now we're going to see whether or not Russia is there, and if they're not, it will be a very disappointing moment for the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And Vladimir Putin just said he is open to a cease-fire, but he does still have some concerns. He suggested that you two should speak directly. Do you have plans to speak to him soon? If so, when?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I would. Yes, sure.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And are you confident you can get this across the finish line?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Sure. He did say that today. It was a very promising statement, because other people are saying different things, and you don't know if they have anything to really—if they have any meaning, or I don't know. I think some of them were making statements. I don't think they have anything to do with it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No, he put out a very promising statement, but it wasn't complete. And yes, I'd love to meet with him or talk to him, but we have to get it over with fast. You know, every day people are being killed. It's not like—as we sit here, two people will be killed. Think of it. Two people are going to be killed during this little period of time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thousands of people a week are dying, so we really don't have very much time. We have to make this fast. It shouldn't be very complicated.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/U.S. Security Assistance

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, how does this new transatlantic cooperation—how do you envision it? What is it going to look like?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, we have—that's one thing. I mean, you know, we're the other side of the ocean, and they're right there. And yet, we're in for $350 billion because of Biden, and they're in for $100 billion. So it's a big difference, and it's unfair.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I said, "You have to equalize." They should equalize. They should have—it should have never happened, where Biden just gave his money away.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, as you know, we're—we have an agreement with Ukraine on the rare earths and other things, and that will get us something back—a lot back. It will get us our money back. We're not doing it for that though. We're doing—I'm just doing this to get the war stopped. I'm doing it, really, to save lives.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, at the same time, we were treated very unfairly, as we always are by every country. And we're in for very substantially more than the European nations are in for, and that shouldn't be.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, they're much more affected by it than we are, because we do have an ocean in between.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I don't know. I think good things are going to happen. I really do. I think good things are going to happen. I do say—we were talking before, and Mark was very nice. He said, "If you wouldn't get involved, there would be"—you'd just be going on, and we——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. This thing would have gone on for a long time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Breaking a deadlock. It was crucial.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, we broke a deadlock.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We did break a deadlock. I hope it's meaningful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, did you have one?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Greenland/Arctic Security Cooperation

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you, Mr. President. Greenland. What is your vision for the potential annexation of Greenland and getting them, potentially, to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. ——to statehood?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I think it will happen. And I'm just thinking—I—I didn't give it much thought before, but I'm sitting with a man that could be very instrumental. You know, Mark, we need that for international security—not just security, international. We have a lot of our favorite players, you know, cruising around the coast, and we have to be careful. And we'll be talking to you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's a very appropriate—really, a very appropriate question.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. It's an——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——an issue in the high north, so the Arctic. So what you did—so, when it comes to Greenland, yes or no, joining the U.S., I would leave that outside, for me, this discussion, because I don't want to drag NATO in that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: But when it comes to the high north in the Arctic, you are totally right. The Chinese and— are using these routes. We know that the Russians already arming. We know we have a lack of icebreakers. So the fact that the seven—outside of Russia, there are seven Arctic countries— working together on this, under U.S. leadership—it's very important to make sure that that region, that that a part of the world stays safe. And we know things are changing there, and we have to be there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Well, they just had an election there the other day. I mean, do you see a referendum, a plebiscite where the people of Greenland would be in a position to decide if they want to become part of the United States?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, it was a good election for us, as you know. It was not a referendum. It wouldn't be called that. It was an individual election. But the person that did the best is a very good person, as far as we're concerned. And so we'll be talking about it. And it's very important.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Mark mentioned the word "icebreaker." So we've ordered—we're in the process of ordering 48 icebreakers, and Canada wants to know if they could use them. I said, "Well, you know, you got to pay for them." Think of it. Canada. We pay for their military. You know, Canada pays very little for their military, because they think we're going to protect them, but—even with the icebreakers.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to order 48, and Canada wants to be part of the deal. I say: "You've got to get your own icebreakers. I mean, if you're a State, you can be part of the deal, but if you're a separate country, you've got to get your own icebreakers."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Russia, as you know, has about 40 of them, and we have 1 big icebreaker. But that whole area is becoming very important and for a lot of reasons. The routes are, you know, very direct to Asia, to Russia, and you have ships all over the place. And we have to have protection. So we're going to have to make a deal on that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Denmark is not able to do that. You know, Denmark is very far away and really has nothing to do.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I—what happens? A boat landed there 200 years ago or something, and they say they have rights to it. I don't know if that's true. I'm not—I don't think it is, actually.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we've been dealing with Denmark. We've been dealing with Greenland. And we have to do it. We—really need it for national security. I think that's why NATO might be—have to get involved in a way, because we really need Greenland for national security. It's very important.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we have a couple of bases on Greenland already, and we have quite a few soldiers that—maybe you'll see more and more soldiers go there. I don't know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What do you think about that, Pete? So—don't answer that, Pete. [Laughter] Don't answer that question——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we have—we have bases, and we have quite a few soldiers on Greenland already.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, you are a man of peace. You've said it several times and made it very clear. A man of peace dealing with belligerent people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. And I'm thinking, we saw you handled Zelenskyy in this very own room. What is your leverage on Putin? Are you thinking sanctions? What if he refuses to——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, I do have leverage, but I don't want to talk about leverage now, because right now we're talking to him. And based on the statements he made today, they were pretty positive, I think, so I don't want to talk about that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I hope Russia is going to make the deal too. And I think once that deal happens, you're never going to be in a process. I don't think they're going back to shooting again. I really believe if we had a—if we get a peace treaty, a cease-fire treaty, I think that leads to peace. That's going to really lead to a peace—I don't think anyone wants to go back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They've been doing this for a long time, and it's vicious and violent. And I think if— President Putin agrees and does a cease-fire, I think we're going to be in very good shape to get it done. We want to get it over with. That's why it was very important what I instructed everybody, including Steve, what we're looking for: to discuss concepts of land, concepts of——

full_topic_context.speaker: National Security Adviser Michael G. Waltz
full_topic_context.text: National Security Adviser Michael G. Waltz. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——of power plants because it's complicated. You know, you have a whole—you're sort of creating the edge of a country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The sad part is that country, if they didn't—if this didn't happen—and it wouldn't have happened—I don't know if they would have to give anything back. I guess Crimea?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, I said it last time, Crimea was given by Obama, Biden gave them the whole thing, and Bush gave them Georgia. And Trump didn't give them anything.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I gave them—you know what I gave them? I gave them—I gave them Javelins. And the Javelins were very effective, as you know. I gave them nothing——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. 2Twenty nineteen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And then also, if you take a look, I was the one that stopped the pipeline going into Europe. It was totally stopped: Nord Stream 2. Nobody ever heard of Nord Stream 2 before I came along.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I got along very well with President Putin. I got along with most of them. I get along great with President Xi. I got along great with Kim Jong Un. I got along great with all of them. And we had no wars. We had no problems. We wiped out ISIS in record time—General "Razin" Kane. And he wiped them out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And he is going to be our new chief, right? He's going to be——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth
full_topic_context.text: Secretary of Defense Peter B. Hegseth. Yes, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——the head of Joint Chiefs of Staff, and he's a highly respected man.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: He's going to be great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Pete is going to be fantastic. I have no doubt about it. We have a great team. A really great team.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, please. Go ahead, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, some of our allies have said that they're worried that they could be the next to be attacked by Russia. You've spoken directly with the Russian President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you think those fears are justified?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. No, I don't. I think when this gets done, it's done. They're going to all want to go home and rest. I don't see it happening. Nope, I don't see that happening. And we'll make sure it doesn't happen. Not going to happen. But we'll make sure it doesn't happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, go ahead, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Nuclear Disarmament Efforts

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Leaders from Russia and Iran are heading to Beijing tomorrow to discuss nuclear programs. What do you hope to get out of that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Well, maybe they're going to talk about nonnuclear programs. Maybe they're going to be talking about the deescalation of nuclear weapons, because, you know, I was talking about that with President Putin very strongly. And we could have done something. Had that election not been rigged, we would have had something. I think I would have made a deal with Putin on de-escalation, denuclearization, as they say. But we would have deescalated nuclear weapons, because the power of nuclear weapons is so great and so devastating.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And right now Russia and us have by far the most, but China will catch us within 5 years.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: China doesn't have—but they're in the process of building——

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. ——and they build. And within 4 or 5 years, they'll probably have the same.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. And by the way, you—this is a Republican tradition. Ronald Reagan, when he negotiated with Gorbachev——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——in the 1980s——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary General Rutte
full_topic_context.text: Secretary General Rutte. ——about bringing down the number of nuclear weapons is what you have been doing your first term. And it is important.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. It would be a great achievement if we could bring down the number. We have so many weapons, and the power is so great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we—number one, you don't need them to that extent. And then we'd have to get others, because, as you know, in a smaller way—Kim Jong Un has a lot of nuclear weapons, by the way—a lot—and others do also. You have India. You have Pakistan. You have others that have them, and we'd get them involved.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we started off with Russia and us. We have, by far—actually, by far, the most. And we were going to denuclearize, and that was going to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then we were going to China. And I spoke to China. I spoke to President Xi about it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And he really liked the idea. You know, he'd like not to spend trillions of dollars building weapons that, hopefully, he's never going to have to use. And—because they are very expensive also. So that would have been great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay, one or two more.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.] Yes, go ahead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, thank you very much. Thank you. Thank you, Pam, very much. What a job you're doing. And it is a true honor to be with you today in this very storied—this is a storied hall, if there ever was one. And based on the crowd, I think we broke the alltime record. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But as we begin a proud new chapter in the chronicles of American justice—this is really is something—we're turning the page on 4 long years of corruption, weaponization, and surrender to violent criminals. And we are restoring fair, equal, and impartial justice under the constitutional rule of law. And you're the people that are doing it. Very, very proud of all of you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under the Trump administration, the DOJ and the FBI will once again become the premier crime-fighting agencies on the face of the earth.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: People ask me what am I going to do about law enforcement all the time. The fake news back there—[laughter]—they're asking me that all the time. What am I going to do and "When are you going to do it?"

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I answer them by saying I've already done most of it by appointing the people that I've appointed. They're sitting right here. They've done most of it. I don't do it. They do it. Right, Pam? [Laughter] I think—oh, you are so tough. They just don't know yet. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Let me begin by congratulating the incredible people who will lead these historic reforms. And we start with somebody that you just saw: Pam Bondi. She's extraordinary. And I've known her very well for a long time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I watched her for a long time in Florida—for years in Florida. And highly experienced. She seems so young, but she's highly experienced. That I can tell you. She was a phenomenal attorney general in Florida and she's going to do a really amazing job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Also, our new Director of the FBI, Kash Patel. Kash. Great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: A man that I'm very proud of. I've known him and Emil for a long time, under tremendous pressure. I saw these guys under some of the most corrupt judges I've—it's not even imaginable how corrupt they were. And these guys never wilted. They never—they were not shy. They fought, and they weren't afraid, and they were brilliant, Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche and Principal Associate Deputy Attorney Emil Bove. And thank you both very much. Great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Great people. They're great people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The Chief of Staff, who is so highly respected: Chad Mizelle. Thank you, Chad. Chad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you, Chad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our next Administrator of the DEA, Terry Cole. Terry. Thank you, Terry. Good luck. You're going to do great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Senior Counsel to the Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights—boy, I've been watching him on television last couple of weeks; he is really a tough one, and he's a great one—Leo Terrell. You watch how good he's going to be. He's going to be so good. Thank you, Leo. Great guy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Assistant Attorney General of the Antitrust Division, who's got an incredible reputation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She'll do very, very well. Gail Slater. Thank you, Gail. Good luck. Great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're joined by many, many great friends and terrific friends. And I won't be able to— too many to name, but some that I just see very quickly. General Flynn, thank you for being here. He's a man who went through hell, by the way. And he shouldn't have. It was—he's a patriot. He went through hell.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're also pleased to be joined by Senator Chuck Grassley and House Majority Whip—hi— where's—hi, Chuck—House Majority Whip Tom Emmer. Tom, great job you're doing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Representative Guy Reschenthaler. One of the toughest names to say, but I got it—I got it perfectly, I think.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And State Attorney General Ken Paxton, thank you very much. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Somebody who was with us early on and she's really become a big star and very popular: Brenna Bird. Thank you, Brenna. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Steve Marshall, Alan Wilson, James Uthmeier, Chris Carr, Dave Sunday, Marty Jackley, as well as White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller. What a man Stephen is. He's become a big star. Right, Emil? [Laughter] Steve Miller. Steve has been something very special.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: For generations, the Federal Department of Justice was one of America's most revered institutions. The men and women of the DOJ brought down the Mafia; hunted down the killers, kingpins, and spies; tracked down terrorists and traitors; and tore down corrupt political machines all across America.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This department commanded the respect and admiration of the entire world. And with Pam and Kash and all of the people I introduced and far more, big numbers—and all of you sitting back there; I recognize so many of you—but with you leading the way, it will soon be the most admired and most respected of all. You're going to be more respected.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I really believe that there's—there's also a lot of things to solve, a lot of problems to solve. But that's going to put you in the upper tier and maybe the top tier. And I believe that's going to happen. I'm so proud of the people in this room.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, first, we must be honest about the lies and abuses that have occurred within these walls.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Unfortunately, in recent years, a corrupt group of hacks and radicals within the ranks of the American Government obliterated the trust and good will built up over generations.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They weaponized the vast powers of our intelligence and law enforcement agencies to try and thwart the will of the American people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You remember the 51 intelligence agents that said, as an example, that Hunter Biden's laptop from hell came from Russia when they knew it came right from his bedroom. They knew that. It was a big lie, and they knew it so well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They spied on my campaign; launched one hoax and disinformation operation after another; broke the law on a colossal scale; persecuted my family, staff, and supporters; raided my home, Mar-a-Lago; and did everything within their power to prevent me from becoming the President of the United States.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: With the help of radicals like Marc Elias, Mark Pomerantz—and these are people that nobody has ever seen anything like it. Just—and so many others. But these are people that are bad people—really bad people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They tried to turn America into a corrupt, communist, and third-world country. But in the end, the thugs failed, and the truth won. Freedom won. Justice won. Democracy won. And above all, the American people won.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There could be no more heinous betrayal of American values than to use the law to terrorize the innocent and reward the wicked. And that's what they were doing at a level that's never been

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: seen before. And it's exactly what you saw with Joe Biden, Merrick Garland, and their cronies. To do the building of the last 4 years, they ripped—what they've ripped down is incalculable, but what you're going to build up is, likewise, something that will be breaking all sorts of records.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They set loose violent criminals while targeting patriotic parents at school board meetings. They dropped charges against Antifa and Hamas supporters while labeling traditional Catholics as domestic terrorists. The Catholics.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We did very well with the Catholic votes. So I want to thank them for that. They imported— they really did. [Laughter] Record numbers. I would say: "What's with the Catholics? They're really after the Catholics." So I don't know. They were after a lot of people. Maybe they didn't even know why.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They imported illegal alien murderers, drug dealers, and child predators from all over the world to come into our country, while putting elderly Christians and pro-life activists on trial for singing hymns and for saying prayers. They went to jail for that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our predecessors turned this Department of Justice into the "department of injustice." But I stand before you today to declare that those days are over and they are never going to come back. They're never coming back.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, now, as the chief law enforcement officer in our country, I will insist upon and demand full and complete accountability for the wrongs and abuses that have occurred.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The American people have given us a mandate—a mandate like few people thought possible. We won every single swing State. We won the popular vote by millions and millions of people. We won districts—2,750—think of that: 2,750 districts compared to 505. So we won it at levels that have, I don't believe, ever seen before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That's the one where you see the map of the United States and it's all red. Red for Republican, not for communist. [Laughter] Red for Republican. They would like it to turn red for communist, but it didn't work out that way.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The American people have given us a mandate and, really, a far-reach—just a far-reaching investigation is what they are demanding into the corruption of our system. And that's exactly, I'm sure, what Pam and Kash and everyone else mentioned here and not mentioned is going to be doing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will expel the rogue actors and corrupt forces from our Government. We will expose and very much expose their egregious crimes and severe misconduct, of which was levels—you've never seen anything like it. It's going to be legendary. It's going to also be legendary for the people that are able to seek it out and bring justice.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will restore the scales of justice in America. And we will ensure that such abuses never happen again in our country. And that's why, on day one, I signed an Executive order banning all government censorship and directing the removal of every bureaucrat who conspired to attack free speech and many other things and values in America.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My administration stripped the security clearances of the disgraced intelligence agents who lied about Hunter Biden's laptop from hell. We revoked the clearances of deranged Jack Smith, Alvin Bragg, Letitia James, and the crooked law firms that aided their partisan persecutions. And I went through it. These are state and city courts, and the corruption is unbelievable.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We also terminated the clearances of the Biden crime family and Joe Biden himself. He didn't deserve it. In fact, he was essentially found guilty, but they said he was incompetent, and therefore, let's not find him guilty, I guess. Nobody knows what that ruling was, but I didn't want any part of it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think I would have rather been found guilty than what they found with him. [Laughter] They said he didn't know what the hell he was doing, and therefore, he's—let him go. I said: "You know, I'd rather be convicted, Pam." I think that that was not good. [Laughter] I said, "Please convict me. Don't say that."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I pardoned hundreds of political prisoners who had been grossly mistreated. We removed the senior FBI officials who misdirected resources to send SWAT teams after grandmothers and J6 hostages.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I—it was a great honor for me to fire—I will tell you this—a great honor to fire James Comey. A great, great honor. That was nothing—there was no better day. A lot of people said, "Oh, that's too bad you did that." And they said, "That's going to be"—and you know what?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They—a year later, they said, "That actually saved the administration," because a level of corrupt things that we learned after that turned out to be that they were doing, in fact, really bad things. He was a terrible person, did terrible things, and persecuted people. And all in the guise of being an angel, but he wasn't an angel.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We created a brandnew DOJ Task Force on anti-Christian bias.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And under Director Patel, we're getting the FBI agents out of the headquarters in Washington, DC, and back on the streets in pursuit of dangerous criminals, where they belong and where they want to be.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, you know, you have that big FBI building, and it's a very big building, and they were going to build an FBI headquarters 3 hours away in Maryland, a liberal state, but that has no bearing on what I'm about to say. But we're going to stop it. Not going to let that happen. We're going to build another big FBI building right where it is, which would have been the right place, because the FBI and the DOJ have to be near each other. You can't—every—that's one thing I did learn from this persecution: The FBI and the DOJ work together. [Laughter] Now, in my case, they worked together for bad purposes. But they do. They were always together. So how can you have one that's 3 hours away?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But one thing—I said to Kash, "Well, we're going to get a great building built. It's going to be a magnificent building." He said, "Sir, we don't need that kind of room." I said, "What do you mean?" He said: "I'm just going to take a old Department of Commerce building that's about 25 percent the size, and that's what I need. We're going to have the best staff that you've ever seen, and that's what I need. It's in a nice location, but I don't need that big building. Why don't you just sell the site to somebody, and we're going to be very happy?"

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they want to have far fewer people, but we also want to have them in DC. And if for no other reason, we like having law enforcement walking the streets of our Capital, because when the bad guys are out there and they see there's an FBI agent, that's the ultimate in law enforcement, and they're not going to be acting so bad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're cleaning up our city. We're cleaning up this great Capital. And we're not going to have crime, and we're not going to stand for crime. And we're going to take the graffiti down, and we're already taking the tents down, and we're working with the administration.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And if the administration can't do the job, we're going to take—we're going to have to take it back and run it through the Federal Government. But we hope the administration is going to be able. So far, they've been doing very well. The Mayor has been doing a good job. We said, "There are tents galore right opposite the State Department. They have to come down." And they took them down right away. And so, so far, so good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we want to have a capital that can be the talk of the world. When Prime Minister Modi of India, when the President of France, and all of these people—the head of—Prime Minister of

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: United Kingdom, they all came to see me over the last week and a half. And when they come in, I like to—I had—I had the route run. I didn't want to have them see tents. I didn't want to have them see graffiti. I didn't want to have them see broken barriers and potholes in the roads. And we had it looking beautiful. And we're going to do that for the city.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're going to have a crime-free Capital. When people come here, they're not going to be mugged or shot or raped. They're going to have a crime-free Capital again. It's going to be cleaner and better and safer than it ever was, and it's not going to take us too long.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's a new phenomenon that is taking place where these violent, vicious lawyers that we have all over, they play the ref. You know what playing the ref is? Like the great Bobby Knight, basketball coach, he'd scream and scream at the ref. He'd scream. I watched—by the way, I love Bobby Knight, because he endorsed me. And having—[laughter]—having Bobby Knight's endorsement in Indiana was an extremely good thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: A friend of mine said—I was running in Indiana at the time. This was early on, 2016, and I was doing great, but a friend came up and said, "Do you know Bobby Knight?" I said, "No, I don't, but I hear he was a tough cookie." He said, "He's not only tough"—he was beyond tough— "but he's the most popular guy you can imagine."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It turned out he wanted to endorse me. Called me—about 2 years before, he said, "Sir, I'd like to endorse you." I said, "Is this really Bobby Knight?" He said, "It's me." I could tell was Bobby Knight.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: He had been known for throwing the chair across the court and slapping a player. Can't— can't do things like that, right? [Laughter] And the man that came in fired him. He was a new administrator for the college—that guy didn't last very long. They were, like, 14–0, and they fired Coach Knight. That was not good. But he had a little chip on his shoulder, but he loved Trump.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And he came in and he—he said, "I'd love to endorse you." He said, "If you ever run, please call me."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So he said, "Do you know Bobby Knight?" I said, "Well, I don't know him, but he called me a couple of years ago." It was an amazing phenomenon. I took his number, and on each side of my desk in New York, I had stacks of paper, like, nice and neat, but about 2 feet high each. And I said, "You know, I wrote his number down and I put it here 2 years ago." And I said, "Let me see if I can find it." It was almost like a miracle.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I had other miracles that happened too. My ear is still throbbing. That was a miracle—that was a miracle also, wasn't it? That was a miracle also.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, the President gestured to a member of the audience.] How are you?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you. Thank you, Leo. Thank you. Thank you, my man. That was a miracle.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Anyway—okay, that's enough. [Laughter] That's very nice. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But—so he said, "Bobby Knight." So I said, "You know, I put his name down, and I wrote it down. It's in one of these stacks. Let me"—I lift it up. There were—have to be 2-, 3,000 pages in each stack. I lifted it up—the first one; had no idea—and there was his name on a little card, "Bobby Knight," with his number. It was, like, incredible. I tell that story all the time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I called him and dialed the number. He said, "I've been waiting for you to call." [Laughter] And he went out and he made a speech for me in a packed arena in Indiana, and it was over. It was over. He was a tough guy. He actually went a little far, you know, if you w-—if you

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: remember. He made a great speech, because he was actually a motivational type guy, to put it mildly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But he left the stage, and then I'm talking and he walks back onto the stage. I said: "Uh-oh, this is trouble. Why is he coming back?" He was a big guy too. I—"Why is he coming back?" He said, "May I say a few more words?" I said, "Yes, go ahead, Bobby. Say a few more words"—a little different. And he said, "And let me tell you something about this guy, Trump. This guy, if he has to, will use the nuclear weapons that we have." [Laughter] "He will use the nuclear—he has no fear. He's going to use. And that's the kind of guy"—and he walked off the stage.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I said, "I think I'm in big trouble," Pam. [Laughter] That was not good, but it worked out okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In the meantime—in the meantime, we won the state in a landslide, and it was great. And it was just an amazing period of time. But this is the most amazing period of time. I think this is more amazing. What's taken place is more amazing. I think it's more consequential.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And if we do the job—you know, one of the big media outlets said what we did was the most consequential election in the last 129 years. Well, if we do the job that we're all capable of doing, I think it's going to be—it's going to prove to be that and then some. And that's what we want to do. We have a real big shot at making this country so great. So great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What happened to our country was so sad. What they've done in 4 years to our country with the borders; with Afghanistan, the embarrassing—most embarrassing period of time; allowing the Russian situation—it was never going to happen—with Ukraine; allowing October 7 to happen— would have never happened because, under me, Iran was totally broke. They had no money. They weren't giving any money to Hamas or Hizballah. It was totally broke. But allowing inflation— look at what inflation has done to people. Been so devastating. And now you see that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: By the way, price of eggs is down 35 percent in the last week and a half. We're doing a good job. Brooke is doing a good job—Brooke Rollins and everybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And inflation is down. Interest rates are down. Gasoline has come down, down to a level that we haven't seen in a long time. All things that we wanted to do, because then everything else is going to be coming down. We want it to come down. We want bacon to come down and groceries. A term I used to use it—it's sort of an old-fashioned term, but I used to use it on the— on the campaign trail. Those last 90 perfect, beautiful days, we just hit it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I want to thank Susie. You have done a great job. Susie Wiles. Great job, Susie. A big magazine just named her the most powerful woman in the world, and that's okay with me. She is the most powerful woman, if you think about it, John. Right? The most powerful woman in the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But she's great, and we had a great 90 days. It was a perfect 90 days, and it was a great result. But we want to put that result to good use by doing a phenomenal job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I want to tell you that—Todd and Emil know this very well—we had a—an amazing judge in Florida, and her name is Aileen Cannon. And I didn't know her. I still don't know her. I don't believe I ever spoke to her, even during the trial, but I did appoint her Federal judge. And these fake lawyers, these horrible human beings were hitting her so hard public relations–wise. They were playing the ref.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I don't think it's legal. I don't think it's legal. They might as well go out and just shout it in a courthouse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They were saying she was slow, she wasn't smart, she was totally biased, she loved Trump. She—I didn't know her, other than I saw her the couple of days that I was in court, and I thought her decorum was amazing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Anything bad they could say, though, they were saying about her. It was whatever they could say bad about a human being. All made up, because, actually, she was brilliant. She moved quickly. She was the absolute model of what a judge should be, and she was strong and tough.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And how do you get them to stop, if you're a judge? How do you get them to stop with the playing the ref?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Bobby Knight would play the ref. That's why I brought up the Bobby Knight story. He would play the ref. He'd scream at the ref. He'd scream so hard. Oh boy, it was terrible, actually.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the people would come up, his assistant coaches would come up to: "Please, Coach.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Coach, don't do that. You just—don't do it. He said he's not going to change his tune, Coach. He called it. He's not changing."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: "I don't care." And he'd scream. And that's when he threw in a chair. He starts going crazy. And he said, "No, he's not going to change this time, but he's going to change for the next play." And sure as hell, he did.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, Bobby, by the way, had the last undefeated team in basketball. And relatively speaking, you know, he had a team. He always had a team. He never had that—he had a couple of great players, obviously, with some top NBA players, but very few, relatively. He had a team, but he had—he won the national championship three times. But he had the last undefeated team in basketball. And he would play the ref, and he would scream at him. He knew exactly what he was doing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're doing the same thing. He said, "No, he's not going to change now, but he's going to change for the next one." That's what he wanted to do. He wanted to scare the hell—they wanted to scare the hell out of the judges, and they do it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now—and how do you stop it, if you're a judge? Because you want to go home, you have a family, you have children. And the New York Times will write whatever these people say, and the Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal and MSDNC and the fake news CNN and ABC, CBS, and NBC. And they'll write whatever they say.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And what do you do to get rid of it? You convict Trump. All you have to do is be really tough on him and, ultimately, convict him, and they leave you alone. It's totally illegal what they do. I just hope you can all watch for it. But it's totally illegal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it was so unfair what they were doing to her. But they do it all the time with judges.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, in her case, she was very courageous, and it only made her angry. Wouldn't you say? It just made her angry. She didn't like it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: A lot of them say: "Oh, please don't say that about me. My family—what's my husband going to say? What's my wife going to say, or my kids? Please don't say that." And it had absolutely no impact on her.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the case against me, which was a case—I will not use a bad word. I promised—I promised my wife I would never use a bad word. So, just a little bad. The case against me was bullshit. [Laughter] And she correctly dismissed it. She correctly—she correctly—[laughter]— look at Emil. He's looking—he saying, "That's interesting." [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But these two guys were warriors. You'll—you've got a warrior here. You got two warriors, I can tell you that. You got a whole bunch of them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But—and they wouldn't quit. They wouldn't take no for an answer. They just wouldn't quit.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: These two people right up here, some others that are involved with it indirectly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And what the lawyers do is, they're doing it to the Supreme Court Justices, hoping that they'll be overcome by the horrible things they say about them. They say things about Supreme Court Justices and judges that are just horrible. They're playing the referee.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Remember the way they treated Justice Thomas and Justice Alito and Justice Kavanaugh, Justice Gorsuch? Chief Justice Roberts got treated unbelievably badly. And they're hoping that they can sway them to go along.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Because, again, what do they do? They're humans. You know, like any—it would be wonderful if everybody was just a perfect computer machine, but they're not. They're humans, and they don't want to be accused of many, many things, including gross incompetence. They don't like it, and they don't want it. There's not much they can do about it. You know, they're in a position—they can't really fight back, really, very well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And so what they do is, sometimes they get weak. I would say a majority, maybe, of the times. That's why I'm so impressed with Judge Cannon in Florida, how strong she was, how she held up. It actually made her more resolute than anything I've seen. I mean, it was amazing, because they were hitting her so hard. It was so sad to watch this.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it's sad what they do to other judges. It's very sad what they do to the Supreme Court. And all of—a lot of the judges that I had, if you look at them, they take tremendous abuse in the New York Times and the Washington Post, all of the different networks. They take such abuse. And honestly, they're simply—very simply, they're afraid of bad publicity. They don't want bad publicity. And it's, truly, interference, in my opinion. And it should be illegal, and it probably is illegal in some form.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's no difference than speaking to a judge or shouting to a judge, or doing whatever you have to do in a courthouse. They're doing it behind their back. They're usually doing it anonymously. They're saying, "Anonymously, off the record, the judge is no good."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But everybody knows where it's coming from, and it's totally coordinated. It's a campaign.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's by the same scum that you have been dealing with for years, like guys like Andrew Weissmann, deranged Jack Smith. There's a guy named Norm Eisen. I don't even know what he looks like. His name is Norm Eisen, of CREW. He's been after me for 9 years

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, CREW is a charitable organization. And the reason I'm saying this, Todd, is I'm only going to get one chance to say this. But these are bad people. I don't know who he is, I don't know what he looks like, but everything I read is "Norm Eisen of CREW." And CREW is a charitable organization, and that's a political thing. His sole life is to get Donald Trump. And he's been vicious and violent, and he's trying—and he probably had pretty good success over the years, but with me, how did he do? I think I'm President. [Laughter] Am I here because I'm President? I— but we had to take all of that abuse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Even during the trials, we had to take tremendous abuse. Like, you know, these wonderful guys, they're not legitimate people. They're horrible people. They're scum. And you have to know that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you're going to have these cases where you can't allow yourselves to be deflected. You just can't let it happen. You have so many—you have such a higher calling. And I believe that CNN and "MSDNC"—who literally write 97.6 percent bad about me—are political arms of the Democrat Party. And in my opinion, they're really corrupt and they're illegal. What they do is illegal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It makes no difference how big a victory I had—I can have the biggest victory in history; it makes no difference what kind of a failure the other side has—these people are going to go after me.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I said it during—the other night, during the big speech on Tuesday night, I said about Democrats. And I don't like that. I—I have great respect, by the way, for what Schumer did today. He went out and he said that—"I'm going to have to vote with the Republicans because it's the right thing to do." I couldn't believe what I heard. [Laughter] But, you know, I think he's going to get some credit for it. I think. Let's see what happens tonight with the big vote as it comes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But these networks and these newspapers are really no different than a highly paid political operative, and it has to stop. It has to be illegal. It's influencing judges, and it's entered—it's really changing law, and it just cannot be legal. I don't believe it's legal, and they do it in total coordination with each other.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In everything we do, we're restoring law, restoring order, and restoring public safety in America. That's what we want to do. And we're bringing honor and integrity and accountability back to the highest levels of the FBI, DOJ, and throughout our Government.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's nice to get that first month, and now we have more than a month. Now we have a month and a half, and it's going really, really well. I can tell you, as—little secret—although, the cameras are blazing back there, so it's not that much—but I think we're doing well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As you have been hearing about Ukraine, I think we're doing, now, well with Russia. We're speaking with President Putin. We want to get the war over. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's such a shame to see what's happened. A thing like that would have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And if you look at Afghanistan, that—that was probably what got Putin started, because when he looked at how horribly—horribly we looked, the—I think the most embarrassing day. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The way we got out, I think it was the most humiliating time in the history of our country— the way it happened, not that we were getting out, because we wanted to get out. But we would have gotten out with dignity and strength.

full_topic_context.text: And what a difference a rigged and crooked election had on our country, when you think about it. And the people who did this to us should go to jail. They should go to jail.

full_topic_context.text: It was going—that was heading into World War III territory, and that would have been a war like no other because of nuclear weapons and other types of weapons that—hey, people, you don't even want to know about.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, as many of you do know well, we're focused on persecuting. And these people were really focused on persecuting Republicans.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I have no higher mission as President of the United States than to end this killing and stop this lawbreaking and to making America safe again.

full_topic_context.text: We're joined today by dozens of police officers, sheriffs, and sheriff's deputies from all across the country. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're joined today by Tammy Nobles, whose 20-year-old daughter Kayla was attacked in her home 3 years ago, horrifically assaulted, and strangled to death by an illegal alien MS–13 monster set loose into our country under the open-border Biden regime.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I want you to know that we are working every day to expel these savages from our country and ensure that what happened to your loved ones will never happen again, so their legacy is going to be a great one. Thank you all very much. We appreciate it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This department will not rest until we have ended the fentanyl epidemic in America once and for all.

full_topic_context.text: I spoke with the President of Mexico—very nice woman, very fine woman—and I said, "Let me ask you, you're sending a lot of drugs into our country. We're not liking it at all. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I said, "Why are you not a consuming"—"Well, we're very close with family." I said: "So we're very close with family too.
