And she said it was—"they're rough ads."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's not often that I feel I've learned something from a phone call—[laughter]—because I've been—have—I've a lot of phone calls over my life, but I realized right then and there what a great idea that is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have hired, Susie, a great person, who did a lot of our campaign work, and we've come up with an advertising campaign that's, I think, really incredible. More than anything else, it's terrible to watch. It's terrible to watch. It's the only way it's going to work.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I would be—because we got the numbers down 18 percent. We'd have a blue-ribbon committee headed by the First Lady of the United States, who everyone loves, and some of her friends. And you know, it's—they work so hard. But it was—it's a tough—it's a tough deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're dealing with very smart and very vicious people. You know, some of those businesses, those cartels are run better than any business in America. They say they're run incredibly. Not just here, they—all over the world. They're run like a major business but, in many cases, better.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I said—we got it 18 percent down. Well, 18 percent is incredible. It's like a record, but when you think of it, it's not very much. And the way you get it down, if you want to get it down to close to 100 percent, is with the death penalty.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I think maybe America is not ready for that. China has a death penalty. Singapore has a death penalty. Various places have the death penalty. Wherever you have the death penalty, you don't have drugs, but I just don't know if this country is ready for it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I tell people, and it's always an option, but I don't know. I just don't know if you're ready for it, and that's okay. It's nothing you can do.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But what we're going to do is we're doing this campaign, and I think we can get it down 50—five-oh—percent with this campaign, because when people see all the horrible things that these drugs do to you—and we—we especially focused on fentanyl—when they see all of the horrible things that happen when you take drugs, how you look. You lose your look. Everyone is vain. They don't want to lose their look. A look is so important.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think when they see these things, they may say: "You know what? I'm going to take a pass."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But there is big danger. Pam and I were talking about it before. A lot of people are taking fentanyl and not even knowing. They think they're doing something else or maybe taking another drug, but at a much lower level, and they die.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You can put on the pin—think—think of this—the head of a pin, fentanyl, and it's too much, and it will kill the strongest person in the room. And it's amazing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we think—we're going to do this campaign. It's going to be launched fairly soon, Susie. And I think it's going to have a big impact—a big impact. I think if we got it down by another 30, 35 points—and I really believe we can. I think that's an incredible idea.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I thank the President of Mexico, actually. It was a call on tariffs, and we talked about drugs, and she gave me an idea that I think will be very successful. And based on what I saw, it's going to be amazing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under our leadership, this department is once again laser-focused on protecting the American people. We're defending our borders, our streets, our children, and our good—really, God-given—this is God-given rights and liberties once and for all. We're going to defend our country, and we're going to defend our rights.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Etched onto the walls of this building are the words English philosopher John Locke said: "Where law ends, tyranny begins." And I see that, and I saw it over the last four years when somebody was allowed to attack viciously, with this department and the FBI, his political opponent. How did that work out? Didn't work out too well. But it wasn't pleasant. It wasn't pleasant.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I was attacked by a political opponent, and probably it helped that I was attacked more than anybody in the history of our country. Alphonse Capone, the great Alphonse Capone, legendary "Scarface," was attacked only a tiny fraction of what Trump was attacked. And maybe it worked out well. I don't know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If I had to give it up, I probably wouldn't, but only because I've gotten through it. But I wonder what the difference would be. Maybe they helped get me elected by those margins—the big margins—the big mandate that we received. But you can't go after your political opponent. Nobody has ever seen anything like it, actually, and hopefully they won't see anything like it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But now, with the return of law and order, the entire world is witnessing the triumph of American justice and American freedom. That's why we're here today, gathered with people that have love for our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In the coming years, we will revive the storied legacy of this department—and it's happening right now; we can feel it—and rekindle the spirit of the great lawmen and legal lions of the past: Americans like Wyatt Earp, Eliot Ness, Frank Hamer, Rudy Giuliani—Rudy Giuliani had to suffer greatly, greatly; he was the greatest mayor in the history of our country; he had to suffer greatly—Ed Meese, Antonin Scalia, Robert Jackson, and Robert F. Kennedy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will rebuild pride in our institutions, we will restore the prestige of this great department, and we will bring back faith in our justice system for the citizens of every race, religion, color, and creed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I want to just tell you that this has been a great honor. I was asked to do it, and I said, "Is it appropriate that I do it?" And then I realized it's not only appropriate, I think it—it's really important, and I may never do it again. I may never have another chance to do it again, because this is something that I'm leaving to the greatest people I know—the best people, the smartest people, the toughest people I know—and they're going to do an incredible job. And it's an honor for me to have won this election so that I can appoint these people to do their job, and they're going to do it like you have never seen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I just want to wish all of you good luck. It's going to be an interesting journey. It's not going to be easy, but you're going to win. You're going to win, win, win and fight, fight, fight, and it's going to end up being a tremendous result for this country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So thank you all very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: God bless America. God bless you all. Thank you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, when you speak with President Putin tomorrow, what is your primary message to him? What is your main message to him?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, thank you very much. We're here to have our first board meeting—the Kennedy Center. And it's in tremendous disrepair, as is a lot of the rest of our country—most of it—because of bad management.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This is a shame, what I've watched and witnessed. They spent a fortune—$250 million—and they built these rooms that nobody is going to use, rooms underground. And I've often wondered what are the big cubes that they have outside that block the view. They're cubes with a door in them, so that people can get down to rooms that nobody is going to use. And it's a shame. It's a shame.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The other thing is, we're going to have a little problem with some people that work here. We had—Lee Greenwood wanted to sing a little song today and because of the cost in the union structure, for him to sing a song just for the Board—just a Board meeting—it was going to cost

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: $30,000. That doesn't sound too good. They wanted $30,000 to move a piano. So you can't have that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to fix it up. But it's really emblematic of our country. But the Kennedy Center—you look at the columns outside. You look at—I mean, they're supposed to be covered by something, whether it's marble or whatever—granite. They were never covered. They were painted. But bringing it to more modern times.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: A lot of money has been given to it, and the money has not been properly spent. They built rooms underground with no windows, no nothing, that will not be used ever. You're not going to have people using them. Such a waste of money. Such a terrible waste.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we'll make it—we'll bring it back. We'll make it great again. But it is so much like what I'm witnessing in other places, where you have open borders, where you have men playing in women's sports. It's all the same thing. It's all the same mentality and thinking. So I'm very disappointed when I look around.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The bottom line: It has tremendous potential. And we'll work with Congress. As you know, it's a very public—a very public facility. And we'll do what has to be done. We'll be having a meeting with the Speaker in the not-too-distant future.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think it's important to save this structure and this building. I think maybe we close up some of the work that's been done and built because it was done terribly. It was done terribly. The concept was very bad.

full_topic_context.text: The President's Message to Visitors and Patrons/Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, for Americans visiting Washington, perhaps they're thinking about seeing a show at the Kennedy Center.

full_topic_context.text: Q. What would you tell them? They've never been here before. They want to come check it out. What do you tell them?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I would say this, "Come here and watch it, and you'll see, over a period of time, it'll improve very greatly, physically." And we're going to get some very good shows.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The thing that does well are Broadway hits. And we have some beauty. I guess we have "Les Mis" coming——

full_topic_context.speaker: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Interim Executive Director Richard A. Grenell
full_topic_context.text: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Interim Executive Director Richard A. Grenell. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——and we have some others. But the Broadway hits have done very well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I'm going to spend some time. We have a good board. In the meantime, we're running the country, and we're running it well. We have tremendous things to report.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Tomorrow I'm speaking with President Putin of Russia to save some soldiers who are in deep trouble. They're captured, essentially. They're surrounded by Russian soldiers. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I believe it was—if it wasn't for me, they would be—they wouldn't be here any longer. I was able to get them not to do anything at this moment. But it's a bad situation in Russia, and it's a bad situation in Ukraine.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What's happening in Ukraine is not good, but we're going to see if we can work a peace agreement—a cease-fire and peace, and I think we'll be able to do it. I'm speaking to President Putin tomorrow morning.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I think they're doing the right thing right now, and we're trying to get a peace agreement done. We want to get a cease-fire and then a peace agreement.

full_topic_context.text: The President. Who are you with?

full_topic_context.text: Q. I'm with NBC, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Is it counter to that work towards a peace agreement to have Russia specifically attack this region so strongly?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So we're going to see how it all works out. This was Joe Biden's deal. This isn't Trump's deal. This is Joe Biden's deal.

full_topic_context.text: Q. President Trump, there's been some discussion about potentially meeting with Putin in your administration. If there is a peace deal signed, would you consider—would you be open to inviting Putin to the White House?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Two thousand people a week, sometimes, are killed, and we have to get that agreement signed. But that's the only thing I think about.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, thank you very much. Thank you very much, everyone.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'd like to start by saying that our country is doing very well. Things are, as you can see, doing quite well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Please sit down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Before we begin, I just want to announce that I signed a proclamation a few moments ago honoring the 250th anniversary of Patrick Henry's famous speech to the Second Virginia Convention in which he declared very well-known, very famous words: "Give me liberty or give me death."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Has anyone heard the phrase? I think most of you have.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And moments ago, I also signed an Executive order to dramatically increase production of critical minerals and rare earths. It's a big thing in this country. And, as you know, we're also signing agreements in various locations to unlock rare earths and minerals and lots of other things all over the world but, in particular, Ukraine. We're doing very well with regard to Ukraine and Russia. And one of the things we are doing is signing a deal very shortly with respect to rare earths with Ukraine, which they have a tremendous value in rare earth, and we appreciate that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we spoke yesterday with, as you know, President Putin and President Zelenskyy. And we would love to see that come to an end, and I think we're doing pretty well in that regard. So, hopefully we can save thousands of people a week from dying. That's what it's all about. They're dying so unnecessarily. And I believe we'll get it done. We'll see what happens. But I believe we'll get it done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Today we take a very historic action that was 45 years in the making. In a few moments, I will sign an Executive order to begin eliminating the Federal Department of Education once and for all.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it sounds strange, doesn't it? Department of Education, we're going to eliminate it. And everybody knows it's right. And the Democrats know it's right, and I hope they're going to be voting for it, because, ultimately, it may come before them. But everybody knows it's right, and we have to get our children educated.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're not doing well with the world of education in this country, and we haven't for a long time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're pleased to be joined today by the woman who I chose because she's an extraordinary person, and hopefully, she will be our last Secretary of Education—[laughter]— Linda McMahon. Linda. Thank you. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That's another interesting statement. These are very—that's an interesting opening, right? [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it's true. And we—people—you know, it's been amazing how popular this has been. I tell people that this is what I'm doing today, and they say, "Oh, that's—it's about time." Everybody says it. Republicans and Democrats have said it. And they're all saying it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Also with us are some terrific people. Governors Greg Abbott. Greg, thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Governor Ron DeSantis. Thank you very much, Ron. Mike Braun. Congratulations on your victory, Mike. That was a big one. Mike DeWine. Thank you very much, Mike.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Jeff Landry. Jeff. Thank you very much, Jeff. Bill Lee, thank you. Governors. All Governors. Brad Little. Brad, thank you very much. Where are you, Brad? Hi, Brad. Jim Pillen. Thank you very much, Jim. And Kim Reynolds.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: These are all people very interested in education. And I even see Dan Patrick over there— my friend Dan Patrick.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're joined also by Representatives Tim Walberg and Virginia Foxx, Rick Allen, Michael Rulli, and again, Dan Patrick. Thank you very much, Dan. You've been a great friend of ours.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And State Attorneys General Ken Paxton. Ken, I see you there. Andrew Bailey. Andrew. What a job you've done, Andrew. What—you have some good cases going. You've done a great job. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And cofounder of Moms for Liberty, Tiffany Justice. She's been a hard worker. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very—thank you, Tiffany.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When President Carter created the Federal Education Department in 1979, it was opposed by members of his own Cabinet, as well as the American Federation of Teachers, the New York Times editorial board, and the famed Democrat Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: History has proven them right, absolutely right. After 45 years, the United States spends more money on education by far than any other country and spends, likewise, by far, more money per pupil than any country. And it's not even close. But yet, we rank near the bottom of the list in terms of success.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's an amazing stat that's—those are two stats you don't want: the most money spent per pupil, and you're at the bottom of the list. And that's where we are, like it or not, and we've been there for a long time.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Seventy percent of eighth graders are not proficient in either reading or in math. Seventy percent. Forty percent of fourth graders lack even basic reading skills. Can't read. Students in our public elementary and middle schools score worse in reading today than when the department opened by a lot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In Baltimore, 40 percent of the high schools have zero students who can do basic mathematics—not even the very simplest of mathematics. I said, "Give me your definition of basic," and they're talking about, like, adding a few numbers together.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Despite these breathtaking failures, the department's discretionary budget has exploded by 600 percent in a very short period of time, and it employs bureaucrats in buildings all over Washington, DC. And as a former real estate person, I will tell you, I ride through the streets of Washington, and it says, "Department of Education, Department of Education." I said, "How do you fill those buildings?" It's crazy what's happened over the years.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm pleased to report that after offering these Federal employees two generous buyout options—and they were very generous—and they're good people—but they were very generous—my administration has initiated a reduction in force, and we're already cutting numbers that were really surprising to a lot that we were able to do it so successfully. And we've cut the number of bureaucrats in half. Fifty percent have taken offers, which is great. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Under the action I am taking today, a small handful of Democrats and others that we have employed for a long time—and there are some Republicans, but not too many, I have to be honest with you—but the department's useful functions and—such as—and they're in charge of them—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Pell grants, title I funding, resources for children with disabilities and special needs will be preserved. Fully preserved. They're all going to be.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, if you look at the Pell grants—supposed to be a very good program—title I funding, and resources for children with special disabilities and special needs, they're going to be preserved in full and redistributed to various other agencies and departments that will take very good care of them. And that's very important to Linda, I know, and it's very important to all of us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But beyond these core necessities, my administration will take all lawful steps to shut down the department. We're going to shut it down and shut it down as quickly as possible. It's doing us no good. We want to return our students to the States where just some of the Governors here are so happy about this. They want education to come back to them, to come back to the States, and they're going to do a phenomenal job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, if you look: Denmark, Norway, Sweden—I have to tell you—I give them a lot of credit. China is top 10, and so we can't now say that bigness is making it impossible to educate, because China is very big. But you have countries that do a very good job in education. And I really believe, like some of the Governors here today from States that run very, very well, including a big State like Texas—but States that run very well are going to have education that will be as good as Norway, Denmark, Sweden, and those top—Finland—those top countries that do so well with education. I think they'll have—they'll do every bit as well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And what do you think about that, Governor? Do you agree? Huh? I think so. Ron, do you agree? I think so. Florida. Iowa. That's right. I really believe that. They'll be as good as any of them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then you'll have some laggards, and we'll work with them. And we can all tell you who the laggards will be right now, probably, but let's not get into that. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we'll work with them, and we're going to make them—they'll do a job. I think they'll do a job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they'll go to sections of the State. For instance, New York, you'll have a Manhattan, and you'll have a Suffolk County, and you'll have Nassau County and you'll have Westchester County. You'll do four or five or six of them. You have Upstate New York. And those counties, I think, are going to do very well. And I think, ultimately, Manhattan should do very well. But we'll break it down into sections, and I think it will be really, really good. And they're going to be probably the tougher ones, but I think they have a chance to do really well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we're going to be returning education, very simply, back to the States, where it belongs. And this is a very popular thing to do, but much more importantly, it's a commonsense thing to do, and it's going to work. Absolutely, it's going to work.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I can tell you, from dealing with the Governors and others in the State, they want it so badly. They want to take their children back and really teach their children individually.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Probably, the cost will be half, and the education will be maybe many, many times better. So we look forward to this.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I want to just make one little personal statement. Teachers, to me, are among the most important people in this country, and we're going to take care of our teachers. And I don't care if they're in the union or not in the union. That doesn't matter.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we're going to take care of our teachers, and I believe the States will take, actually, better care of them than they are taken care of right now. They'll work all sorts of systems and even merit systems. Those great teachers are going to be maybe a little bit better rewarded, and maybe that's the way it should be, but the States are going to make that decision.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we're going to love and cherish our teachers, along with our children, and they're going to work with the parents, and they're going to work with everybody else. And it's going to be an amazing thing to watch, and it's really going to be something special.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, Linda, you're presiding over something that's so important, and you're going to do a fantastic job, just like you have your whole life. I knew your whole life—I've been watching you; I've been watching you for a long time. She's had nothing but success.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So it's tremendous to have you. And hopefully, you won't be there too long. [Laughter] But we're going to find something else for you, Linda. Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So this will conclude what we are talking about with respect to our most cherished group of people, and that's our children. We want to have our children well educated, and we want them to love going to school.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We have examples of it. Look at those beautiful, bright-eyed faces. Those—they are so smart. They're so smart.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And with that, I am going to come down and we're going to sign a very important document, and we're going to be on our way.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: People have wanted to do this for many, many years, for many, many decades. And I don't know—no President ever got around to doing it, but I'm getting around to doing it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, the President addressed the students seated in desks near the signing table.] Hello, everyone. Good-looking people here. Nice pen. Should I do this?

full_topic_context.speaker: Student
full_topic_context.text: Student. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Should I do it? [The students nodded.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes? Okay. I think so.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We have pens for you too. Special pens. I'll take this one out. I had one that was very lucky. I signed another document that turned out to be very good for the country. And I said, "Let's use that same pen." I don't know. Is anybody superstitious? Ron, are you superstitious? Let's use that same pen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [The President signed the Executive order.] Okay. Time to get up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Linda, come on up here. Can you come up please? Come on up here, Linda. Can you come up just to say—come on up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Education Linda E. McMahon
full_topic_context.text: Secretary of Education Linda E. McMahon. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. That's great. It's very important. You're a big factor here. Good luck.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary McMahon
full_topic_context.text: Secretary McMahon. Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Good luck, Linda. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you, Linda. Good luck.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you, everybody, very much. Good luck. We'll see you.

full_topic_context.text: Representative Elise M. Stefanik/2024 Presidential Election

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President—Mr. President, yesterday, you asked Representative Stefanik to stay in her seat. Can you explain your reason for that it? And did it have anything to do with the tight polling in the Florida district that former Representative Waltz held? Is that——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I think we're doing——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is that a factor?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, I think we had—as you know, we have a few elections going on. And she is phenomenal, number one. She is a friend of mine, and she was going to go to the United Nations, and I said, "Look, there's a lot of room for doing that or something else."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But she's very popular in her district, and I didn't want to take a chance. I don't even know who else is running. I assume somebody else would have been running. But if she runs, she can't be—you never want to say, "can't be beaten," but I think can't be beaten. She's very, very well liked and very smart.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I said: "Elise, would you do me a favor? We can—we cannot take a chance. We have a slim margin. We don't want to take any chances. We don't want to experiment." And she polls like I do. I won her district, as you know, by a lot of points. And she also does very well there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: When it comes to Florida, you have two races, and they seem to be good. It's a Trump-plus- 32 area.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The one thing is, they're spending, like, $12 million, and our candidate doesn't have that kind of money—spending much less than that, like maybe one-twelfth—about a million dollars, a little bit more than a million dollars—so the airwaves are blanketed. And you never know what happens in a case like that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I won it by 32 points. And it's very—a very strong—it used to be Democrat, but when I came along, they liked me. For whatever reason—you'll have to explain that, but they liked me, and we're way up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you don't know what happens, and then you have the second district, who seems to be in pretty good shape. But likewise, he's being outspent about five to one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we don't want to take any chances, so I went to Elise, and I said, "Elise, do you mind?" A very highly rated person, you know. She was a real leader, and she will be again. I spoke with Mike Johnson. They're going to put her in a high leadership position. But: "Will you mind staying in Congress, because we don't want to take any chances?"

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's as simple as that. It's basic politics. It's politics 101. She's very popular. She's going to win, and somebody else will probably win too, because we did very well there. I did very well there. But the word "probably" is no good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I really appreciate her doing it. She's doing me a big favor when she does it, because she was all set to go to the United Nations. And she would have dealt with Putin and Zelenskyy and everybody else, and she would have been very effective. But we really want to—don't—we don't want to take any chances, because it is tight.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.] No. Go ahead, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you, Mr. President. Have you spoken with Vladimir Putin about buying weapons from Iran and from North Korea?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Not about specifically that, no. I haven't.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Well, that seems to be an issue that you want to make important. Is the—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I'm making all issues important. You've got a lot of important issues. You also have the children issue that's important. You know, it's a lot of children are living in Russia right now. That's a horrible situation that would have never taken place if I were President, but it did, and the country is being decimated.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But you know, they're losing 2,500, on average, young men—mostly men; almost in all cases, men, actually—but young men every single week: 2,500. And they're not from our country. They're from Ukraine, and they're from Russia. But it's human lives, and if we can get it stopped—and I think we're making progress. But there's a lot of ill will between the parties. That I can tell you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. But Iran is making money. Iran is making money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Greenland/Arctic Security Cooperation

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, your Vice President—the Vice President is in Greenland right now. Do you have plans to expand U.S. military presence in Greenland? Is that part of a plan to annex the island?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, we're getting along very well with Greenland. We get along very well with Denmark. We've always had a good—Denmark does a lot of business in the United States. We don't do so much there, but they do a lot of business in the United States. And I think they want to see—I think everybody wants to see that work out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We need Greenland, very importantly, for international security. We have to have Greenland. It's not a question of, "Do you think we can do without it?" We can't. If you look at Greenland right now, if you look at the waterways, you have Chinese and Russian ships all over the place, and we're not going to be able to do that. We're not relying on Denmark or anybody else to take care of that situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we're not talking about peace for the United States. We're talking about world peace. We're talking about international security. And right now, you look at it, you have warships all over the place going through—right along Greenland. We're not going to let that happen. We cannot let that happen. Or, if it's going to happen, we have to be protective of our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you planning to expand the——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And more importantly, right now, it's really protection not only of our country, of the world. So Greenland is very important, and modern-day weaponry makes Greenland—a hundred years ago, less so. But also——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would you like to visit Greenland, Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Will you send more U.S. troops to Greenland?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. ——if you notice, also, some of those—you could call them roadways.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay? They're water roadways, but some of those areas are opening up, and they're opening up— icebreakers out there, they're opening them, and by just nature, they're opening up. And they're headed right into China, right into Russia. And we have no choice.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The answer is: He's there with his wonderful wife Usha. They're there right now. They landed a couple of hours ago. And they will represent us well. But Greenland is very important for the peace of the world—not us, the peace of the entire world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think Denmark understands it. I think the European Union understands it. And if they don't, we're going to have to explain it to them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would you like to visit Greenland—— [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine/Iran

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Iranian drones—Iranian drones are attacking Ukraine every day.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Thank you, Mr. President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Say it?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Iranian drones are attacking and killing Ukrainians every day. Why aren't you doing something about that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, we're going to see what happens with that. I'm getting reports on that, and we're looking at a report. You're right. They make a lot of drones, Iran makes a lot of drones. They make very effective drones too. They do very effectively at some things.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But Iran is very high on my list of things to watch. And as you probably know, I sent them a letter just recently, and I said, "You're going to have to make a decision one way or the other." And we're going to either have to talk and talk it out, or very bad things are going to happen to Iran, and I don't want that to happen. I don't want that to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: My big preference—and I don't say this through strength or weakness. My big preference is we work it out with Iran. But if we don't work it out, bad, bad things are going to happen to Iran.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay. Thank you very much, everybody. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Hello, everybody.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Hello, Mr. President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I hope you had a good time this weekend.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Yes, it was great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. We had a lot of very interesting things happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think we're making a lot of progress on Ukraine and Russia, and that's always conflict, but I think we're making a lot of progress getting it stopped. We just want to see thousands of soldiers a week stop dying, because they're dying at numbers that probably haven't seen since the Second World War for no reason whatsoever. It's a shame. It's a shame.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I think we are making progress. It's step by step. There's tremendous hatred between the—the leaders, if you call—call the whole situation "leaders," but I think we'll get that done.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the Middle East—a lot of things are happening with respect to Iran, and we'll see if we can get something done. And if not, it's going to be a bad situation—very, very bad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You said bombing——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Tariffs/Iran/2024 Presidential Election

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the additional oil sanctions that you mentioned today. When will they start?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So we have a couple. We have the secondary tariffs on Iran. And we'll probably give it a couple of weeks, and if we don't see any progress, we're going to put them on. We're not putting them on right now. But if you remember, I did that 6 years ago, and it worked very well, to put it mildly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And if the election weren't rigged, you would have a situation where there would be no problem with Iran today, but it was. Biden didn't know what he was doing, obviously. And we have a very rough situation in the Middle East because of that. You ended up with October 7, and you would have never had October 7 and you would have never had Russia going into Ukraine, likewise.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we're going to make a decision on secondary tariffs on Iran based on whether or not they're going to make a deal. If they're going to make a deal, then we're never going to put secondary tariffs on. We're going to hope they have a great, long, and successful life as a country, but we'll see what happens. It's very, very interesting.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I can't imagine them doing anything else but making a deal. I would prefer a deal to the other alternative, which I think everybody in this plane knows what that is, and that's not going to be pretty. And I do not prefer that. So we're going to see.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Scope of Planned Tariffs

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the tariffs that you're planning. So there are—you're expecting to hit something like 10 to 15 countries. Is that right?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No. No.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. All countries?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. All of the countries?

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is it across the board?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Not 10. I don't know who told you 10 or 15 countries.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Well, we heard that. So we heard that you were going to aim for the percent——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, you might have heard it, but you didn't hear it from me.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Okay. So how many countries will be in that initial tranche?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, let's—you'd start with all countries, so let's see what happens. There are many countries in play.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On the Russian——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I haven't heard a rumor about 15 countries—10 or 15 countries.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So you're starting with all countries?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, essentially, all of the countries that we're talking about, yes. We'd be talking about all countries. There's not a cut off.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And if you look at the history and you look at what's happened to us, you go to certain places—go to Asia, and you take a look at every single country in Asia, what they've done to the United States in trade and, by the way, in military, in a certain way—you look at—you—but take a look at trade with Asia. And I wouldn't say anybody is treated as fairly or nicely, and—but we are going to treat them—we're going to be much more generous to them in terms of heart, going to be much more generous than they were to us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. You said that you were not——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/Venezuela

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. So you said you were upset with Putin.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Are you—I just want to clarify——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Would you say your relationship with Vladimir Putin is at its lowest point right now?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No, I don't think so. I don't think—I don't think he's going to go back on his word. You're talking about Putin. I don't think he's going to go back on his word. I've known him for a long time. We've always gotten along well, despite the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's a hoax created by Clinton and Schiff and all of these lunatics. And that really was a dangerous point. That was a very dangerous thing they did to this country. It was a pure, unadulterated scam, hoax.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But no, I think—I think he'll be okay. But if he isn't—I was disappointed, in a certain way, some of the things that were said over the last day or two having to do with Zelenskyy, because when he considers Zelenskyy not credible, he's supposed to be making a deal with him, whether you like him or you don't like him. So I wasn't happy with that, but I think he's going to be good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I certainly wouldn't want to put secondary tariffs on Russia, but if they were put on, it would not be very good for them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, several reporters began asking questions at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, we put secondary tariffs on, as you know, in Venezuela, and it's had a very strong impact on Venezuela. You know that. Every ship just got out and they left. A lot of them left. They dropped the hoses right into the ocean and they left. They didn't want to be there for a minute because they didn't want those tariffs to catch on, or they didn't want me to see them there. full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Venezuelan Oil Supply

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No, we're not playing games. Okay. Any other questions?

full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir, will you clarify: Are you planning to leave office January 20, 2029, or are you saying you might not?

full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President—[inaudible]. Russian——

full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you have a deadline for Russian President Vladimir Putin?

full_topic_context.text: I know what the hell I'm doing. I know what I'm doing, and you know what I'm doing too.

full_topic_context.text: That's why you vote for me.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the chipmakers are coming in. They're all coming in. We've never had anything like this. We have investment, they think, of about seven—think of this: $7 trillion. For about a month and a half, we got seven—almost $7 trillion spoken for. Trillion.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We've never had that. I don't know if we've ever had it anytime. But if you go back and look at Biden and these other campaigns, any of them, they had—they didn't have those numbers for the year.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: These are the biggest chipmakers in the world, the biggest auto manufacturers in the world. Seven trillion dollars of investment, and that means jobs. I look at differently. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it is true that Mexico—they've stopped building plants, and those plants are now going to be built in the United States of America. So it's pretty exciting.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: All because of two things. They say—they want to be nice to me. They say: "Sir, because of November 5, the election, and because of tariffs." I said, "In that order?" full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I'm the only one that would have done the tariffs, because everybody was afraid. They were afraid of being criticized, because the globalists will go after you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: For seven decades, American ships have patrolled the seas, American troops have kept the pace and peace, and American wealth has enriched the globe. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I used to say to Angela Merkel, "Angela, how many Chevrolets do we have in Berlin?" "Why, none, Donald. None." "That's right, Angela. You got it. How many Chevrolets do you think we have in Munich, Angela?" "None, Donald." I said, "You sent us 7 million cars last year."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to start buying American-made cars or cars that are manufactured in America.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And if you can do it—not part of what I was going to say, but one of the best things that I think I've come up with is interest deductions. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I haven't really been as strong on this one, but it's only because it gets a little bit long, you know? full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I was going to say, before that—in Nevada, that when I came up with the "No tax on tips," I think that's why we won by a massive amount.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And interestingly, they came up about a month and a half later. She was making one of her few speeches. She didn't speak too much—for a reason, a good reason. [Laughter] They said, "You're a little late on that one."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Because I was worried they would copy me. You know, it was so good. You know how it actually happened? Maybe I should tell the story quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I was in my building in Las Vegas—we have a great restaurant there—and this young, beautiful waitress—and you're not allowed to say "beautiful," because that's the end of your political career. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So she came up to me, and she said: "Hello, sir. It's so nice to have you at the hotel." I said, "Thank you." I had a group of people—some political people, actually. It was very interesting.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I said, "How's everything going?" She said: "Oh, it's so tough. They're after my tips." "Who's after?" "The government. They're after my tips. Constantly, after my tips. They're after all of us for the tips."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: She said, "Sir, we should have no tax on tips." I said: "Say it again. What?" "We should have no tax"—she said it. This was my consultant: a waitress from my hotel. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I went outside. There were a lot of—we finished our wonderful meal—steak—went outside, and there were a lot of cameras, as there always are, unfortunately. Click, click, click, click, click. And we won the state by a lot. So I don't know.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I hope—I have to find that waitress and thank her. She was my consultant—[Laughter]— except I didn't pay her $2 million like the other consultants that we all get screwed by.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Even worse than the tariffs other countries impose are the nonmonetary barriers. That's a nonmonetary—these are not financial. These are other things, what they do so that you can't get your product in that country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And China, as you know, is one of the bigger offenders. It's not all China.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Look, I get along with President Xi. I have over the years, but, you know, you just—when COVID came, that was the end. That was it. That was called the "bridge too far." full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I tell that to other leaders: "You've got to fight for your country. It's—you're not going to fight for us, but we can't fight for you." We're fighting for other countries. We're trying to make them great without making us great. But those days are over.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They steal our intellectual property. They rob our trade secrets. They manipulate their currency to levels that have never been seen before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Today it was announced that China is reducing its currency. Did you see that? Big. Big. In other words, they're going to make up for it. They got every trick in the book. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You're not supposed to do that. The game isn't supposed to be played that way. It makes it very hard for us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, in the end, it's not good because they have to buy oil. See, we don't need oil. We don't need oil and gas. We have more than any other country. They have to buy it. That's where it hurts them when they do that. It costs them twice as much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they ship their products through every one of our trading partners, running up our deficits with these countries. They sell a lot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, when you put a tariff on them, they sell it, like with steel. They were dumping tremendous amounts of steel into our country during my term. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The people that like me best are the people in the steel business, but I think the auto business is going to be right there. I think chips are going to be there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I think pharmaceuticals are going to be there, because, you know, we don't make our own pharmaceuticals—drugs and other things to get better. They're made in other countries. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They put all of their research and develop money; they put everything. But what they don't tell you is that these other countries are smart. They say, "You can't charge more than $88.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Otherwise, you can't sell your product," and the drug companies listen to them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But we're going to do something that we have to do. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to be announcing very shortly a major tariff on pharmaceuticals. And they're going to be opening up their plants all over the place in our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're going to be announcing that. So that's breaking news. Ladies and gentlemen, we have breaking news. That's what's going to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: What other Presidents allow China to get away with is absolutely criminal, but I'm not like the other Presidents, and it's not going to happen under President Trump. It's just not going to happen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: After all of the abuses they've perpetrated, China is attempting to impose additional unjustified tariffs.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Just so you understand, they all got rich because of tariffs. You know, now, when we do it, "Oh, it's so terrible what Trump is doing. It's so terrible." They got rich. Name any country. What's the name of our country?" He doesn't know. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That's why additional tariffs on Chinese goods are in place, effective midnight tonight, at 104 percent. Until they make a deal with us, that's what it's going to be. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: China will now pay a big number to our Treasury. This is all taxes. And don't let them keep telling you that this is a tax on our people. I hate that. You know, they say, "It's a tax." No. Often, much of it is paid.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And, hey, look what happened during my first term. We had no inflation, and yet I took in hundreds of billions of dollars in tariffs and taxes from China. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I still got along with them, because they understood what they were doing was wrong. They understood it. Because some of the trade deals that were made by predecessors, as President, were so bad, you almost wonder who did these

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: deals. They were either crooked or stupid. They could be nothing else. They were either stupid or crooked.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's terrible, but it's all being changed. I changed a lot of it in the first 4 years, but it's all being changed.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, in the first 4 years, we had the most successful country in history in terms of economics. We had 88-percent increase in the stock markets. And I think we're going to do much better than that this time, because this time I'm doing what I want to do with respect to the tariffs. I think we're going to do much better.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And just remember the numbers. When you get up to $2 billion a day—$2 billion a day. They're saying, "Sir, can't be that, can it?" I said, "Yes, it can." It's the biggest transaction ever made. This is bigger than any deal.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You guys—some of you work for companies. Your companies are peanuts—I don't care how big they are—compared—this is the largest transaction in the history of our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And don't let some of these politicians go around saying, "You know"—because I'm telling you, these countries are calling us up, kissing my ass. They are. [Laughter] They are dying to make a deal. "Please. Please, sir, make a deal. I'll do anything. I'll do anything, sir."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And then I'll see some rebel Republican—you know, some guy that wants to grandstand, say, "I think that Congress should take over negotiations." Let me tell you, you don't negotiate like I negotiate. Congress takes over negotiating, sell America fast because you're going to go busted. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You don't—I just saw it today. A couple of your Congressmen said, "I think we should get involved in the negotiation of the tariffs." Oh, that's what I need. I need some guy telling me how to negotiate. [Laughter] Ai yai yai.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'll tell you, the happiest people in the world would be China. They wouldn't be paying 104 percent, I tell you. They'd be paying no percent. We'd be paying them 104 percent. [Laughter] That's the beauty is these guys. We got to be careful.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And even the concept of it hurts your negotiation. When they see a little story like that, the other side, you know, it hurts your negotiation. And then the fake news wants to build it up, and it has no chance anyway. But we have to remain united.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As I defend workers from unfair trade, House Republicans have a chance this week to bring trillions and trillions of dollars pouring back into America by pushing forward with the largest tax cuts in American history, which is what you're working on right now. The largest in American history.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you know, the reason we had—because we had a great first term and—amazing first term. But I saw that the other day, that we had the most successful—I mean, I knew it anyway, but I saw that we had 88-percent increase. That's a tremendous increase. Think of that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And that's with all of the difficulties and all of the fake investigations and the Adam "Shifty" Schiffs. Can you believe this guy? How can it?" It was the weirdest thing. It's a mystery.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Nobody can understand it. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But he's one of the most dishonest human beings I've ever seen. And, you know, how we can allow people like that to run in office is a shame, but we did. He was in charge of the witch hunt.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, he was in charge of the fake witch hunt with "Russia, Russia, Russia." It was a made- up story. Made-up. Think of it. They make up a story. They know it's made up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's gone on for a year and a half, two years, "Russia, Russia, Russia." I knew nothing about it. The only thing I knew was that I taxed the pipeline that I told you about, that I put all sorts of sanctions on everything else. I never had—no—they never had a problem like they had with me.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it was "Russia, Russia, Russia" constant as a method of—that was a—what they did is that was the complaint about why she lost that election, because Crooked Hillary was expected to win the election. But that was—they didn't—they didn't see what we saw. We saw the biggest crowds in history gathering, only superseded by the crowds we just had.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But here's a guy that goes out, and he goes to an intelligence hearing or whatever you might call it, and it's supposed to be secret. He'd walk out. He'd either make a call, off the record. "Off the record. This is Crooked Adam Schiff." "Shifty" Schiff. He's a "Shifty" Adam. Or he'd just go out blatantly and have a news conference, and because it had to do with me and my family, he'd go out and have a news conference, and he said—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, you've got to remember, he knows it's a hoax, because he made it up with Crooked Hillary. So he knows it's a hoax, because we're dealing with human beings on the other side. He'd say, "Donald Trump, Jr., the son of the President of the United States, will spend many years in prison because of what he's done with Russia."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, think of that statement on a human basis. I have a son—a young son, who is being told that he's going for prison on something he has—he doesn't even know what they're talking about. He said: "Dad, I don't know what's going on. They keep talking about I'm involved with Russia. I don't know anything about Russia. I swear to you, Dad."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And yet Adam Schiff goes out and makes a statement about a hoax that he made up that he knows is false. How bad a human being do you have to be? They put my son and my family through that kind of trauma. These are bad people. These are sick degenerates. And I used to be much nicer to them. I gave them the benefit of the doubt, but I've just seen too much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They make up a story about Russia. It's a hoax, and eventually—now they've all admitted it was a hoax. Onto the next one. That's "Russia, Russia, Russia." But they know it's a hoax, and they say about a young man that he's going to spend the rest of his life in prison because of what he's done with Russia. He knows it's a hoax. How bad do you have to be to have that happen to your son?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And you know, there's a bad effect on a family, a bad effect. You know, "Are you okay, Don? "I am, Dad, but I don't understand. They keep tying me to Russia. I don't know anything about Russia." He didn't know a damn thing about Russia. It's a disgraceful situation. That's why we've got to kick their asses in the midterms, and we've got to kick their asses again in 4 years.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If we slash taxes on American workers and producers, our economy will soar, jobs will surge, manufacturing will boom, and our country will prosper like never, ever before. We've got to get this big, beautiful deal done. We got to get it done and get it done now. Don't wait 2 weeks. Don't wait 2 weeks. See, bad things happen. Crazy things happen in politics, just get the damn thing done and stop showboating.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Couple of people want to—"Sir, we've got to get a little bit more." A little bit more—you know what you're going to get? End up getting nothing. You end up getting a Democrat bill or worse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In the past 11 weeks, we've already created 350,000 jobs—it's unprecedented—including 10,000 manufacturing jobs, and we haven't even started yet.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Gas prices—you know, when I came in, they said, "He campaigned on prices coming down, and prices are going up." They're not going up; they're going down. Gas prices are way down. In fact, they had something—$2.50 a gallon, I saw on television a little while ago in between my— watching my great friends on C-SPAN, I saw that the prices are down to $2.50, $2.60, $2.75. It was—when I came in office, it was $3.50, $3.75, but prices are coming down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Prices on groceries are coming down. Prices of eggs are down, like, 87 percent—87. You know, they got me with that, I told you. Before I even got in office, they would tell me about— they're down close to 87 percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And core inflation has dropped to the lowest levels in 4 years. And as I said, we had no inflation in 4 years, despite the fact that I took in hundreds of billions of dollars in tariffs, and we hadn't even started yet. Nearly $6 trillion of new investment, and that number is now revised up to about 7.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Apple, great company, is spending $500 billion because of tariffs—$500 billion, not $500 million. That's a lot. Five hundred million. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: TSMC, the biggest, most powerful chipmaker in the world—this is without that stupid CHIP Act, where they say, "Here's billions of dollars," to a company that doesn't need it. These chip companies are loaded. They give these companies billions of dollars to build a plant in the United States. They don't build them in the United States. They keep the money. It looks good. They gave them billions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: No. TSMC, I gave them no money. Great company, most powerful in the world, biggest chip company in the world. They're spending $200 billion in Arizona, building one of the biggest plants in the world, and that's without money. All I did is say, "If you build—if you don't build your plant here, you're going to pay a big tax—25, maybe 50, maybe 75, maybe 100 percent."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Nvidia is investing hundreds of billions of dollars. Johnson and Johnson is investing $55 billion. Eli Lilly is investing $27 billion. DAMAC is investing $20 billion. We have billions and billions being invested by Merck, Clarios, Stellantis, General Motors, Honda, Nissan, Hyundai. All are putting in billions and billions and billions of dollars. They're buying sites all over.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're building, because they don't want to have to pay 25- and 50-percent tariffs. They're all doing it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think they also have confidence in the country. They have a President that they have confidence in. I know many of them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: With the help of people in this room, we are one big, beautiful bill signing away from the greatest economy in the history of the world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's an overhang. You know, this bill is an overhang, because if it doesn't get signed, we will have imposed the biggest tax on the people of this country in our country's history by 40 percent—the biggest tax. Because we gave you the biggest tax cut in history; now we're giving you another, which is one of the reasons that—there are many reasons why we were so successful, but that's one of the big ones.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The other one is that 1-year deduction—all-in, 1-year deduction. So big. And I know they're working on that, the big deduction. It makes people invest. But now we're working on something that's going to, I think, blow it away. This bill is unbelievable. It's going to bring a lot of money back into our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But if we don't do it, it's going to be a disaster, and you'd just better hope that people believe that it was the Democrats' fault, because, you know, they're very good at saying it was our fault. It will be the biggest tax increase in history.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And all my life, as I watched politicians—I wasn't a politician, but I watched them, and I contributed to them a lot—contributed a lot of money over the years—but I watched it. But all my life, I'd hear politicians saying: "We are going to give you a tax cut. I will cut your taxes. We will cut your"—I never heard—they're the only party that says: "We are going to increase your taxes. Vote for me." Who the hell ever heard this? [Laughter] Only these people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're in a strange time. These lunatics go out and they tell everybody how you're going to have a big tax increase. So maybe they want the bill to fail so they can have a tax increase— maybe they'll take credit for it. But I've never heard that said. All—I've watched politics all my life. I've never seen politicians campaign on, "We're going to increase your taxes," except these crazy Democrats.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As part of this legislation, I am committed to spending cuts, and I will fight hard to include the elimination of hundreds of billions of dollars in waste, fraud, and abuse in the bill. We've already found hundreds of billions of dollars through DOGE. And Elon has been terrific. He's been really terrific. But we've found hundreds of billions of dollars of waste, fraud, and abuse.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But now we need to get the budget resolution, and we have to get it passed in the Senate. We have to bring it through the House. It's going to pass in both.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: One thing I'll say is that Thune has been great. John Thune has been great. And he's worked with your great leader hand in hand. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
