full_topic_context.text: Italy-U.S. Relations

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: In the meantime, it's an honor to have the Prime Minister of Italy with us, Prime Minister Meloni, who's doing a fantastic job. I would say that she has taken Europe by storm. And highly respected.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Everybody loves her and respects her, and I can't say that about many people. And she's become a friend, and we really have a great relationship between Italy and ourselves.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we talked about trade. We talked about many, many things during our luncheon. And she'll be saying a few words, but she's a very special person, and it's nice to have you with us.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. Thank you very much, Mr. President. Thank you for your warm welcome. Thank you for this occasion, which is aimed to strengthen our relation, our friendship that comes from very far.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. You know today is April 17, and April 17 marks the anniversary of the agreement that allowed Cristoforo Colombo——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Oh.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. ——to make his trip. And I say to remember our ancient—our—our ties, but also to remind that we both share another fight, which is the fight against woke and DEI ideology——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. ——that would like to erase our history.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: And as I know that we share lots of things on tackling illegal migration, on fighting against synthetic drugs. You know, Italy has been one of the nations——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. ——that made a plan against fentanyl, for example.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: But we have been talking about many bilateral topics and things that we can do together——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. ——about defense, about economic—about economy, about space, about energy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Italy will have to increase its LNG imports and also nuclear that we are trying to develop. I think there can be ways to work together. And the Italian enterprises will invest—as they've been doing for many years, as you know—in the next years, I think, around 10 billions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. That shows how interconnected our economies are. And that's very important, Mr. President. It's not only about Italy, it's about the entire Europe. The exchange between us is a very big one. Investments, trade—it's a topic that we are discussing in this week.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. That's right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. But, at the end of the day, look, somebody quotes me. I was saying it before. Such western nationalism—I don't know if it is the right word, but I know that when I speak about West mainly, I don't speak about a geographical space. I speak about the civilization. And I want to make that civilization stronger.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: So I think even if we have some problems—okay?—between the two shores of the Atlantic, it is the time that we try to sit down and find solutions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: So I want to thank President Trump for having accepted an invitation to pay an official visit to Rome in the near future and consider a possibility in that occasion to meet also with Europe. The goal, for me, is to make the West great again. Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Okay.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. And I think we can do it together.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. We can.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. And we will keep on work on that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: I'm going to close. I want to say only I'm proud of sitting here as Prime Minister of an Italy that, today, has very good—has a very good situation, despite the difficulties. A stable country. A reliable country. One million more jobs in the last 2 years and half.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Great.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. Inflation is going down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: So you will forgive me if I promote, a bit, my country——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Yes, please. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. ——but you're a businessman, and you understand me. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Go ahead. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. So migration flow is going down 60 percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: So we are trying to do our best, but I think we can do it even better together.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Also, on Ukraine. I will close. Together, we've been defending the freedom of Ukraine.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Together, we can build a just and lasting peace. We support your efforts—[inaudible].

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Meloni
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Meloni. You're welcome.

full_topic_context.text: President Trump. And I think we're doing well in that effort, but we want to get it done, and we'll see if we can. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think we're getting close, but we'll let you know very soon. And you've been very helpful. I appreciate it. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Secretary Rubio said that the U.S. will have to figure out whether a deal can be done between Russia and Ukraine in a matter of days or you will just move on.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes, very shortly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. How many days is that?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No specific number of days, but quickly. We want to get it done. We're talking about here people dying. And we're talking about, over there, people are dying also, like, on average, 2,500 young people, soldiers.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They're not from America, they're not from anywhere else other than Ukraine and Russia, but we want to save these lives. So it's 2,500 a week are being killed in battle. It's a vicious battle with the best equipment, the best everything, and it is brutal. Two thousand five hundred young people a week. Some of them not so young, actually. They're getting older. They're getting older by the month. But 2,500 a week, and we're going to get it stopped, ideally.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now if, for some reason, one of the two parties makes it very difficult, we're just going to say: "You're foolish. You're fools. You're horrible people," and we're going to just take a pass. But hopefully, we won't have to do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. What——

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. When you say, "Take a pass"——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. And Marco is right in saying it. We're getting—we want to see it end. Think of it. Every day, a lot of people are being killed as we talk about, you know—as they play games. So we're not going to take that, and we will see. I think we have a good chance of solving the problem, however.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters began asking questions at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: President Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin of Russia/The President's Foreign Policy/Inflation

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Is Vladimir Putin stalling, in your view, Mr. President?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I hope not. I'm going to let you know about that soon, if he is, but I hope not.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: He's got a big force out there. A big force.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It's a war that should have never happened. It would have never happened if I was President.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That's a war—and it didn't happen for 4 years. That's a war that should have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: October 7, Israel, would have never happened. Iran was broke. And now we'll see what happens with Iran. We have a lot of them out there. We have a lot of things that we're working on right now that shouldn't have happened. None of it. Ukraine would have never happened with Russia. October 7 would have never happened, so you wouldn't have had all the problems in the Middle East. The Afghanistan embarrassment—probably the most embarrassing day in the history of our country—would have never happened. Inflation would have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: By the way, prices are down. Groceries are down. Eggs, which they—you hit me so hard, I'll never forget. The first day—first week in office, they were screaming at me about eggs. I said, "What's going on with eggs?" They were doubling and tripling. I said, "I just got here." [Laughter] They were up, like, double, triple, and you couldn't get any. And they said, "You won't have eggs for Easter."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Well, you can have all the eggs you want.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Sir——

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I'll tell you, Brooke Rollins, Secretary of Agriculture, did a great job, and the egg prices are down 87 percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But nobody talks about that. You can have all the eggs you want. We have too many eggs. In fact, if anything, the prices are getting too low.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. On Iran——

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. So I just want to let you know: Prices are down. Gasoline yesterday at—in three States, hit $1.98 a gallon, and it looks like it's at a level that it hasn't seen since my days, my 4 years. So it's about $2—I'd say maybe—I think we're going to average—we're going to be averaging $2.25 very soon.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I just want to let you know, though, because I keep hearing about fraud—prices and inflation. Prices are coming down, not going up. Only the fake news says they're going up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The only thing that's even are interest rates. And if we had a Fed Chairman that understood what he was doing, interest rates would be coming down too. He should bring them down.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Yes, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Russia/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Mr. President, what do you need to see from both sides in order to keep negotiations going? What do you want to see from Russia and Ukraine?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. I have to see—my whole life has been one big negotiation, and I know when people are playing us, and I know when they're not. And I have to see an enthusiasm to want to end it. And I think I see that enthusiasm. I think I see it from both sides.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you think Russia is playing you?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. But you're going to know soon.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: U.S. Diplomatic Efforts/Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. Do you think Russia is playing you?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. No. Nobody is playing me. I'm trying to help.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, this was Biden's war. By the way, by me getting involved, you know, they'll say, "Oh, it's Trump." This is not Trump's war. This is Biden. This is a war that should have never happened. Okay?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Think of it. Those cities are crushed and crashed. And all those beautiful steeples, the most beautiful in the world—actually, the—considered the most beautiful in the world—most of them are now smashed to smithereens, as they say, and lying on the ground in a million pieces. Those towns are crushed. The whole place—it's so horrible. And millions of people are dead, far more than you think.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: That's one thing you're going to get out of this war. You're going to find out that your estimates are far lower than—it's far worse than people think.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Nobody is playing anybody. We are going to see if we can get it done. I think we have a really good chance of getting it done, and it's coming to a head right now.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Ukraine

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. If you do—[inaudible]—would you continue to support Ukraine militarily? If you do—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Say it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: Q. If you do decide to move on or take a pass, Mr. President, would you then continue to

full_topic_context.speaker: Reporter
full_topic_context.text: support Ukraine militarily?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, I'm not going to say that, because I think we're going to get it done. [Several reporters spoke at once.]

full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much. We have—Jonas Gahr Støre is here, who is the—as you know, the Prime Minister of Norway. He's a great gentleman, highly respected, beloved in his country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we've had talks on the war with Ukraine-Russia and trade. We're doing very well, I think, on both. We've had some pretty good movement in every respect. And I think we've made a long—a lot of progress, and we'll see what happens.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This next few days is going to be very important. Meetings are taking place right now. Additionally, we talked about trade, and we will definitely—we get along very well on trade.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We'll do something. But I think the Prime Minister knows that over the years the United States

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: has been very good to a lot of people, and it's time for us to benefit also.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to have a good relationship on trade, and we discussed other things also.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But, Mr. Prime Minister, it's an honor to have you at the White House. Thank you very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Støre
full_topic_context.text: Prime Minister Støre. Well, thank you, Mr. President. This is—this year is 200 years since the first immigration from Norway to the U.S.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Støre
full_topic_context.text: We come here early in your term. Appreciate that you take time. We have highlighted that very close cooperation. We are allies. We look after security in the north, in the Arctic. A lot of confidence between our services.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Støre
full_topic_context.text: We have discussed in detail the war in Ukraine. I have saluted the President for his initiative to make progress towards something that can be a cease-fire and an end to this terrible conflict. full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Støre
full_topic_context.text: And on trade, we have also emphasized that we can benefit both of us by trading and we can be complementary and we can find good solutions.

full_topic_context.speaker: Prime Minister Støre
full_topic_context.text: But first of all, I appreciate, Mr. President, the spirit and the tone of this conversation, which has been confirmation of a very strong partnership.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: President Trump. Thank you very much. Appreciate it. Any questions, please?

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will fully and permanently secure our border. We will make the largest ever investment in U.S. military and build the Golden Dome missile defense shield. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And one hour ago, I just made a speech at Selfridge Air Force—Air National Guard Base—

full_topic_context.text: —announcing that we are saving it, keeping it open, including thousands of jobs with the brand-new, state-of-the-art F–15s, which are coming to Selfridge.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we will crush violent crime and give our police the support, protection, resources, and respect they so dearly deserve. I will defend religious liberty, and I will defend the right to keep and bear arms.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will celebrate the 250th anniversary of America's founding in 2026, and we will teach our children to love our country, honor our history, and always respect our great American flag.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And one day soon, American astronauts will plant the flag on the planet Mars. It's going to happen very soon.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Every single day of my administration, we'll continue to live by the motto, "Promises Made"—and you've seen it before—"Promises Kept."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: From Marquette to Midland, from Mackinaw to Saginaw, and from Lansing to right here in Macomb County, we stand on the shoulders of red-blooded Michigan patriots—what great people; I love you, Michigan—who laid the railroads, worked the factories, tilled the field, forged the steel, fought the battles, and won the victories that built the Motor City and made the state into the pride of the America Midwest. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Michigan is the State that gave us the assembly line, Motown, Ford, General Motors, Chrysler, and put the world behind the wheel of an automobile. And under our leadership, we're making it greater every single day.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the automobile business in Michigan will soon—and it's going to happen really soon—it's already happening—they're signing left and right because of my taxation and tariff policies, which are policies of common sense and genius—be bigger and stronger and better than ever before. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It was hardworking patriots like you who built this country. And on November 5, 2024, it was hard-working patriots like you who saved our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So thanks to your help, your love, and your support, after 100 days back in the White House, America is a free, proud, and sovereign nation once more, and our magnificent destiny is closer than ever before. It's closer than ever before. You have no idea how close it is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Our golden age has only just begun. We are one people, one family, and one glorious nation under God. We will never give in. We will never give up. We will never back down. We will never, ever surrender.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will fight, fight, fight, and we will win, win, win.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Together, we will make America powerful again. We will make America wealthy again. We will make America healthy again. We will make America strong again. We will make America proud again. We will make America safe again. And we will make America great again.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I love you, Michigan. I love you. Have a good time. Thank you. God bless you all. God bless you. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: The President. Well, good morning. This is a beautiful day. We could not have asked for a more beautiful day than this, and maybe that means something that brings us a little luck.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it's a great honor, and I'm delighted to welcome you to this very special place, the White House, to celebrate the annual National Day of Prayer. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're bringing back religion in our country, and we're bringing it back quickly and strongly. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I want to thank a man of incredible faith who's with us, Speaker Mike Johnson, for being here. He's done an incredible job. Thank you, Mike, very much.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're working very hard on a great big, beautiful bill—beautiful bill. You know, so we're going to probably do that, because everyone knows what it means.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But later today I'll be going to the University of Alabama to deliver the keynote commencement address to a record crowd. They have a big crowd. This is the first time they've done that. And I'll give it a shot. All right? I hope we can entertain. I will give it a shot.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But before we begin, I want to let you know what I was just doing in a really great meeting with Speaker Johnson—we had also Majority Leader Steve Scalise; Chairman Brett Guthrie, who's a fantastic guy; and Chairman Smith, everybody knows Chairman Smith—he's the most knowledgeable person on taxes and finances there is—to be updated on the progress of the one big, beautiful bill. We love that bill.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I won't like it if it doesn't pass. Neither will you. It doesn't pass, your taxes are going to go up 68 percent. Think of it. Sixty-eight. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And that's the Democrats. That's what they'll give you. They'll vote against it. It's not even believable. It's called Trump derangement syndrome—[laughter]—because honestly, they— everything in there is good for Democrats, Republicans, and everybody else.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: These will be the biggest tax cuts in American history, with 100-percent expensing, which is something that people cannot believe they're getting. We did it in the last one, and we had the most successful economy in my first 4 years that we've ever had the history of our country, and expensing was one of the things that led to that. But it's 100-percent expensing for companies investing in America and increasing take-home pay for the typical family by thousands of dollars a year.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And to show you how middle income this is, there'll be no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax for the great seniors in Social Security. So you have no tax on Social Security for our great seniors.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we have full deduction for interest. If you buy a car that's made in America, you get an interest rate deduction. That's going to be a big—it's got to be made in America. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Things are moving along very well. And I want to thank you and this group and all of the people that are over there right now—not in the sun, they're working on the bill. It's bill—it will be the biggest bill ever passed in the history of our Congress—our Senate and Congress. That's a big achievement.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: One of the things that's very important, we'll be saving Medicaid for Americans in need. We will not let the Democrats destroy it and all the waste, fraud, and abuse that they seem to love.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they will decimate Medicaid if they get the chance. We're not going to give them that chance.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So just remember, we will be saving Medicaid and strengthening it. It will be actually very strengthened, and they are going to decimate it. We can't let it happen. full_topic_context.text: And I said, "You can't give up Bagram." They gave up Bagram. And right now China occupies Bagram. So sad. So crazy. Well, we were keeping it, but they ran out of there like—like, nobody can believe.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I think Putin saw that and he said: "Wow, this is a great time. I can go get"—because it was the apple of his eye. I could always see that. I talked to him for hours. It was the apple of his eye. But I said, "Vladimir, don't even think about it." And he wouldn't have thought about it. But when he saw that, I think that's the reason, actually, he gained some additional courage, and he went in.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Adi and Yael, I cannot imagine your pain. I just can't. The—Adi and Yael—but we're all alongside of you. We stand by you, and we're going to.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're going to do everything possible in the very short period of time. You know, as you know, things are heating up there. I got—I've gotten a lot of hostages out. We were getting nobody out. A lot of them are out, but they want to do it as slowly as possible, because they use them as pawns. It's a horrible thing, but we're working very, very hard to save your son. We have news coming out, both good and bad, but we're working very hard.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I have many parents seeing me. I was with the hostages—10 hostages I got out. They came about three weeks ago to the Oval Office right here, and they said to me—it was just terrible. And I said—interestingly, because, you know, you see—there's always some heart in somebody, you think. I said, "So you've seen, like, hundreds of Hamas, right?" "Yes, yes."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They lived in a pipe. They didn't really live in a tunnel. They lived in a pipe that was this big. They could barely breathe. It's amazing. One was in for 305 days. One was in for over 500 days. But I got them out and through very tough—it was very tough. The whole thing was very tough.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I said: "Did you ever see any love or kindness? Like did any of these people that were guarding you, the Hamas people, did they ever look at you and say, 'Don't worry, you'll be all right'? Or did they ever look at you and say, 'I'm going to sneak you a little extra bread or a little extra something for eating'? Did they ever give you any hope?" He says, "No, not one." I said, "You mean, so not one person looked at you during your 1½ years in there"—one was there longer than that; one was there a little shorter than that—different times. I said, "Not one?" "No, they used to give us a smack on the face. They would never do that. They—not one."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So there wasn't one person out of hundreds that said, "I'm going to sneak you a little bread.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm going to make sure you get home safely." Not one.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And that amazed me, because in some really bad situations, you'd have some people like that. You'd have some people like that, but not one. I was am-—and they were telling the truth. I mean, they were telling the absolute truth.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And when I talked to them about the way they suffered, it was incredible. In fact, I'd say four or five looked very, very solid and normal, and four or five looked like they'd been through hell, but they were all through the same hell.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I looked at them, and I said, "I can't imagine what you've gone through, but we're going to what we have to do." But I asked them a question. One was wearing "59," and I said, "What does 59 represent?" "That's how many are left." And I said: "All right. We'll get them out." I said, "Are they all living?" "No, 24 are living." I said, "24?" He said: "Yes, 24. Only 24." So 24 out of the 59 are living. And they knew because they had just gotten out. "And what are the others?" "The others are all dead."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I spoke to the parents of the others, and as much as you want your beautiful boy out, they want their beautiful boy—and, for the most part, as you know, boys—young boys, for the most part—but they want him out so badly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I said, "Is he okay?" "No, he's dead." But they want him out so badly, almost as much as if he were alive. It was an amazingly sad thing to see, the level of love for the children. And they didn't even view them as dead. They needed the body of their son, and they knew they were dead.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But think of that. Out of 59, you had 24 that were living. And now I understand it's not even that number. And young people don't die. They're very resilient. You know, you don't have young people dying. Young people are killed. Old people die. They can't take it. They couldn't breathe, in some cases, couldn't—they had them in a pipe closed at both ends. If you're claustrophobic, it's a big problem, and many people are claustrophobic.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But young people live. Old people die. But these were young people that were dying, so you know what—you know what took place.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: As we bow our heads this beautiful day in the Rose Garden on the National Day of Prayer, we once again trust our lives to—our liberties and our happiness to the hands of the Creator who gave them to us and who loves us—who loves us. Think of it. Where you are now and—so beautiful, but you're—it's so nice, because here you are in this unbelievable setting. I think no setting like it in the world, when you add up the importance.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I take people into the Oval Office and—the biggest people, foreign leaders, Princes, Kings, Queens, and Presidents and Prime Ministers and a couple of dictators, I guess. They don't say that. They say, "No, I'm a Prime Minister" or "I'm a President." And I say, "No, you're a dictator, but that's okay." [Laughter] But I bring them into the Oval Office, and they just want to look.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They can't believe it. It's the most important. And they all have beautiful offices. They are, in some cases, the wealthiest people in the world; in some cases, the most powerful people in the world. But they go into the Oval Office, and here you are right outside the Oval Office.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And in one way, you're so lucky, but in another way, you're all fighting for people that you know are not so fortunate right now because of people like your beautiful son, people that are being really tortured because the level of anger and meanness thrown off by human—the human being.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, they say the lions and the tigers aren't nearly as vicious as the human, because they—they only kill for food. They kill for food. They don't kill. They kill for food. The human

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: being kills for sport. They try and destroy people—killing or otherwise—for sport. And we've got some bad ones out there—really bad ones.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We have some bad ones here. We have some bad ones in this Government, but we picked good ones. But we had some bad ones in the last 4 years. The things that they did, and the things they didn't do.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Your son shouldn't have been there for long. That would have been so much easier to solve immediately, instead of years later, and it should have never happened. October 7—remember— would have never happened.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, as we bow our heads on this beautiful day, once again we have to trust our God, because our God knows exactly where we're going, what we're doing, knows every inch of our life. And may he continue to hear our prayers, to guide our steps, and build up our beloved nation to even greater heights.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're in the process of doing some great things. I get criticized no matter what, but I just go forward, because everyone knows we're right. All we're doing is what they've done to us for 40 years, but we're doing it bigger and better. That's the only thing we're doing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And now I'd like to ask our faith leaders, including some of the ones that will be our faith leaders on the Council, to come up, if you will. The ministers, rabbis, please come up. Imams, who I got to know in Michigan. I love them. They were great, by the way.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They said, "We don't want to die." I said, "You want to die?" They said, "We don't want to die." I said, "What about the 38 virgins?" They say: "That's nonsense. We don't know anything about it."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And we won the State of Michigan, Speaker, by a tremendous—and we had tremendous support. But we have some people in the audience. And, Ralph, come on up. Get up here, Ralph. If you see anybody, just get them up here, because these are people that have been just unbelievable supporters of what we're doing and doing it right.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'd like to start by asking Paula White to lead us in prayer to start off, and each person is going to say a few words and a prayer. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser to the White House Faith Office Paula White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser to the White House Faith Office Paula White-Cain. Thank you, sir. Thank you, President Trump. You are truly the greatest champion of faith we've ever had. Can someone say, "Amen"?

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser to the White House Faith Office Paula White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: Just a few words. What a sacred and historic moment to stand in the Rose Garden, in the people's house. And President Trump has graciously welcomed us in, surrounded by leaders of faith and government from every background and every tradition, to honor what anchors us all, and that is prayer.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Senior Adviser White-Cain continued her remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser to the White House Faith Office Paula White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: We call for a spiritual reset in our Nation, a return to what is right, a reverence for what is sacred, a realignment with your divine purpose. Let your favor rest upon every righteous leader. Let justice flow through our government. Let healing go to every broken place.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser to the White House Faith Office Paula White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: And we pray this boldly. We pray this strong. We pray this by faith. And I pray this in the name which is above every name, the name of Jesus. And everybody said, "Amen."

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience members
full_topic_context.text: Audience members. Amen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Great. Thank you, Paula. Great job.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Could I ask Dan to come on up and John come up? Ben, come on up here, please. You've got to be up here.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Come on, Phil. Who knew that Phil was a man of great religion? Who knew this? I watched him so long, I can't believe it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I would love to have you come up, representing your religion. Right there, representing your great—so highly respected. Please come up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Mary, come on up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'd like to have this whole first row come up, if you would. We have room—plenty of room, even if we go back. Mike, come on up. Marco, Scott, Pete, Pam. Oh, look at Howard.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Okay. That's great. That's great. Marco is doing such a good job. Get up here, please. Because somebody's keeping him—somebody's helping him. Come on up. I want to thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Marjorie. Come on up here, Marjorie.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Pastor Maldonado.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Right there.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Pastor, come on up. Come on up.

full_topic_context.text: Yes, come on. These are people that have been from the beginning.

full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Mark Burns.

full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Gary Bauer.

full_topic_context.speaker: Senior Adviser White-Cain
full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Mm-hmm. Yes.

full_topic_context.text: The President. Come on, Gary. Gary won't take up too much room. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.text: I had Ohio State here, and I had, yesterday, the Philadelphia Eagles here, so they took up a little more room than Gary. I got very good at this.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump

full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Rodney and Adonica Howard-Browne.

full_topic_context.text: Rodney, come on up. Come on up. This is built to hold a lot of people, don't worry. [Laughter]

full_topic_context.text: Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Pastor Brad and Rachel Knight.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So I could ask, please, Rabbi Levi Shemtov to come up, say a few words. Rabbi, please.

full_topic_context.text: American Friends of Lubavitch Executive Vice President Levi Shemtov. full_topic_context.speaker: American Friends of Lubavitch Executive Vice President Levi Shemtov

full_topic_context.speaker: Rabbi Shemtov
full_topic_context.text: Rabbi Shemtov. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: Rabbi Shemtov. Thank you very, very much. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker of the House of Representatives J. Michael Johnson
full_topic_context.text: Speaker of the House of Representatives J. Michael Johnson. Sure.

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker of the House of Representatives J. Michael Johnson
full_topic_context.text: Mr. President, it was in 1952 that the Reverend Billy Graham took 40,000 Americans to the east steps of the Capitol and petitioned Congress to establish this day the National Day of Prayer.

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker of the House of Representatives J. Michael Johnson
full_topic_context.text: It didn't take long. It was 2 days later, a unanimous vote in the House of Representatives. Congress worked together well because they knew that priority. They knew we're a nation of faith. It's in our DNA. We are one nation under God, as the President said.

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker of the House of Representatives J. Michael Johnson

full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker Johnson
full_topic_context.text: Speaker Johnson. Let me pray.

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker Johnson

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Speaker Johnson continued his remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker Johnson

full_topic_context.speaker: Speaker Johnson

full_topic_context.text: Audience members. Amen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you, Mike. Thank you, Mike. Bishop Robert Barron, please. Bishop. Good. Thank you.

full_topic_context.text: Bishop Robert Barron of Winona-Rochester, MN. Well, thank you very much, Mr. President, for the formation of this Commission, which I think is of extraordinary significance for our country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Bishop Robert Barron of Winona-Rochester, MN

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience members
full_topic_context.text: Audience members. Amen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Beautiful job. Beautiful. Thank you very much. I'd like to ask Imam Habash to come up please. Imam, thank you.

full_topic_context.text: U.S Air Force Chaplain Walid Habash. Well, greetings, everyone, and happy Thursday. Let us pray.

full_topic_context.speaker: U.S Air Force Chaplain Walid Habash
full_topic_context.text: Today is a great day, made even more memorable by this event.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Chaplain Habash spoke briefly in Arabic; no translation was provided. He then spoke in English as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: U.S Air Force Chaplain Walid Habash
full_topic_context.text: In the name of God, the entirely merciful, the especially merciful. O God, the source of peace, the bestower of wisdom, the one who is near to all, who call upon you with sincerity.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Chaplain Habash continued his remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: U.S Air Force Chaplain Walid Habash
full_topic_context.text: Unite us as one Nation committed to serve one another with dignity, respect, and steadfast hope in your mercy. Truly God, you are the listener of supplication, the one who responds to the call of the caller when they call upon you.

full_topic_context.speaker: U.S Air Force Chaplain Walid Habash
full_topic_context.text: [Chaplain Habash spoke briefly in Arabic; no translation was provided.] Amen, and amen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you. That was fantastic. Bishop Kelvin Cobaris, please.

full_topic_context.speaker: Pastor Kelvin L. Cobaris of Dreams United Church in Plant City, FL
full_topic_context.text: Pastor Kelvin L. Cobaris of Dreams United Church in Plant City, FL. Let's bow our heads in prayer.

full_topic_context.speaker: Pastor Kelvin L. Cobaris of Dreams United Church in Plant City, FL
full_topic_context.text: Heavenly Father, Eternal God, we gather in your majestic and presence today, grateful for the blessings and freedom and peace that you have bestowed upon each and every one of us and this great nation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Pastor Cobaris continued his remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Pastor Kelvin L. Cobaris of Dreams United Church in Plant City, FL
full_topic_context.text: So we pray that thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory forever, and that your will will be done on Earth as it is in Heaven. And we pray all of these blessings in the magnanimous, matchless name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. God's people said, "Amen."

full_topic_context.speaker: Audience members
full_topic_context.text: Audience members. Amen.

full_topic_context.speaker: Pastor Cobaris
full_topic_context.text: Pastor Cobaris. Amen.

full_topic_context.text: Senior Adviser White-Cain. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. That was something, Bishop. You're something. So thank you all. This has been an incredible day.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm going to now ask the musicians who are so wonderful and talented and loyal to our country to conclude this celebration by leading us in two more songs, and I will then simultaneously begin the process of signing the Commission and signing the Commissioners to— join me, everyone who's not on the stage that's a part of it. Please come up.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I just want to say this was a great honor. This was a great day. We could not have asked for more beautiful weather, that's for sure. And I want to thank you all for being here.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're bringing back religion in our country, and we're bringing it back, as I say, bigger and better and stronger than ever before.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Thank you all very much. Musicians, please. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Announcer
full_topic_context.text: Announcer. Ladies and gentlemen, please enjoy "Great Are You Lord," followed by "Amazing Grace.

full_topic_context.speaker: Announcer

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: On—Thursday's meeting with Russia and Ukraine is very important. I was—very insistent that that meeting take place. I think good things can come out of that meeting: stop the bloodshed of the horrible—it's a bloodbath, but 5,000—more—it's really much more—I'm trying to be conservative—more than 5,000 soldiers. Russian—they're not American soldiers. They're from Russia. They're from Ukraine, but they're people. They're human souls, and they're being killed at levels that we haven't seen since the Second World War, and it's every week. A lot of drone fighting. full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And so that's it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial_heading
full_topic_context.text: Executive Order on Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So now I'm about to depart on a historic visit—some of you are going with us—to, as I said, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and United Arab Emirates. Before I do, I'll sign one of the most consequential Executive orders in our country's history. I don't think there's ever been anything signed like this, certainly not with respect to health care. Nothing even close.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I'm delighted to be joined on this occasion by Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., who is doing a really good job, I have to tell you that; CMS Administrator, a friend of mine, Dr. Mehmet Oz, who is an amazing guy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: You know, I was telling Bobby before, Oz had a very successful show, but it hurt his reputation, because when you're in show business, it hurts your reputation a little bit. It's good for your—it's good for you, but in terms of professionalism and being a doctor, it sort of hurts your reputation. This guy went to the best schools, was the best—I mean top, top, top of the line. Then he did a television show, became a success, made a lot of money, all that stuff, but it sort of hurt him.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I did—it—and I—and you know who I compare that to? I hate to say this, but a special woman, Jeanine Pirro. She was that toughest, smartest DA maybe in our country's—in our city's and State's history—New York. She was really tough, really sharp. Then she did a show, and people didn't think of her quite the same way. She became more of an entertainment person like Oz.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Oz is not an entertainment—he's not really an entertainer, if you know the real story, and she isn't either. She is unbelievable. She was one of the strongest district attorneys in the history of New York, highly respected, very tough. Went after the drug dealers at a level that you don't see today anymore, and going to—hopefully, she's going to be—she's given up a tremendous—she's leaving the number-one show on cable television—one of the number-one shows on television,

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: period, "The Five." But they've got great people left behind, but she was a big part of it. And so I equate it to that. Jeanine Pirro is unbelievable.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary, with a reputation that's second to none, and the job he's doing already has been fantastic. Thank you, Marty.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And Director of National Institute of Health Jay Bhattacharya, who has been—as you know, from Stanford—so highly regarded, and have all been working with us very hard on this.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the question they would ask, being a little bit new to the Government aspect of it, is, "Why hasn't—why doesn't somebody fight the drug price situation?" Meaning equalization.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There's a term. It's called "equalization." Nobody wants to mention that term. And I'm not knocking the drug companies. I'm really more knocking the countries than the drug companies, because they're forced to do things.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But the drug lobby is the strongest lobby in this country, they say—the drug lobby. It's between that and lawyers, and they have a lot of power.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But starting today, the United States will no longer subsidize the health care of foreign countries, which is what we were doing. We were subsidizing others' health care—the countries where they paid a small fraction of what—for the same drug—than what we pay many, many times more for. And we'll no longer tolerate profiteering and price gouging from Big Pharma, but again, it was really the countries that forced Big Pharma to do things that, frankly, I'm not sure they really felt comfortable doing. But they've gotten away with it, these countries.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: European Union has been brutal—brutal. And the drug companies actually told me, "Sir, is it"—it was just brutal, how they forced them. And European Union is suing all our companies: Apple and Google, Meta. They're suing all our companies. They end up—they have judges that are European Union–centric, and they get rewarded $15 billion, $17 billion, $20 billion, and they use that to run their operation. Not going to happen any longer. That I can tell you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So what's been happening is, we've been subsidizing other countries throughout the world— not just in Europe, throughout the world. European Union was the most difficult, from what I understand.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I mean, I'll tell you a story. A friend of mine, who's a businessman—very, very, very top guy; most of you would have heard of him—a highly neurotic, brilliant businessman, seriously overweight, and he takes the fat shot drug. And he called me up, and he said, "President"—he calls me—he used to call me Donald. Now he calls me "President," so that's nice respect. But he's a rough guy, smart guy—very successful, very rich. I wouldn't even know how we would know this, but—because he's got common sense—"President, could I ask you a question?" "What?" "I'm in London, and I just paid for this damn fat drug I take."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I said, "It's not working." He said—[laughter]—he said: "I just paid $88. And in New York, I pay $1,300. What the hell is going on?" He said, "So I checked, and it's the same box made in the same plant by the same company. It's the identical pill that I buy in New York, and here, I'm paying $88 in London. In New York, I'm paying $1,300."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, this is a great businessman, so—but he's not familiar with this crazy situation that we have. But he was stunned. But it was just one of those stories.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I brought it up with the drug companies, represented by somebody who's very, very smart. Good person too. And we argued about it for about a half hour. And then, finally, he just said—because they can't justify it. He just said: "Look, you've got me. You've got me. I can no longer justify"—they've been—you know, they've been justifying this crap for years. They said, "Oh, it's research and development." Well, I said: "Well, research and development? Other countries should pay research and development too. It's for their benefit."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It was just one of those things. And the other countries would set a price, and they'd meet the price, and they'd say, "If you don't meet the price, you can't sell it in our country." I said, "Well, then you walk away, and, you know, they'll call you back, and they'll sell it in the country." But now they'll have to do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, for the first time in many years, we'll slash the cost of prescription drugs, and we will bring fairness to America. Drug prices will come down by much more, really, if you think—59— if you think of a drug that is sometimes 10 times more expensive, it's much more than the 59 percent. You know, it depends on the way you want to analyze it. But in one way, you could analyze it that way. But between 59 and 80 and, I guess, even 90 percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, when I worked so hard in the first term and if I got prices down—remember, I was the only one to ever get prices down for a full year, but I'd get them down like 2 percent, and I thought it was, like, a big deal. Well, we're getting them down 60, 70, 80, 90 percent, but actually, more than that, if you think about it, in the way—mathematically.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And pharma has to say, "We're sorry, but we'll not be able to do this any longer," to these company—to these countries that have been so tough. They've been very tough, nasty. It's trade. It's trade. And pharma is also very powerful. And the Democrats have protected pharma. The Democrats—this is—the Democrats have protected pharma. These are the Democrats.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And by the way, I just called the Speaker of the House, and I just called the leader—our leader in the Senate, John Thune—and Mike Johnson. Spoke to both of them. I said: "When you score, you're going to have to score two things. You're going to have to, number one, score that hundreds of billions of dollars of tariff money is coming in. But even bigger than that, you're going to have to score that your cost for Medicaid and Medicare and, just basically, pharmaceuticals and drugs is going down at a level that nobody has ever seen before."

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It will pay for the Golden Dome. I see the Golden Dome is there. See. That will easily pay for the Golden Dome, and we'll have a lot of money left over.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We need the Golden Dome, by the way, in this world. Although, this world is a lot safer today than it was a week ago and a lot safer than it was 6 months ago. We had people that had no clue what they were doing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So today Americans spend 70 percent more for prescription drugs than we spent in the year 2000. Think of that. Our country has the highest drug prices anywhere in the world by sometimes a factor of five, six, seven, eight times. It's not like they're slightly higher. They're six, seven, eight times. There are even cases of 10 times higher so that you go 10 times more expensive for the same drug. That's big numbers.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Even though the United States is home to only 4 percent of the world's population, pharmaceutical companies make more than two-thirds of their profits in America. So think of that. With 4 percent of the population, the pharmaceutical companies make most of their money, most of their profits from America. That's not a good thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Now, I think, by the way, pharmaceutical—I have great respect for these companies and for the people that run them. I really do. And I think they did one of the greatest jobs in history for their company, convincing people, for many years, that this was a fair system. It never—nobody really understood why, but I figured it out.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: For years, pharmaceutical and drug companies have said that research-and-development costs were what they are, and for no reason whatsoever, they had to be borne by America alone. Not anymore, they don't.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: This means American patients were effectively subsidizing socialist health care systems in Germany, in all parts of the European Union. They were the toughest of all. They were nasty. And I see that. I see that with trade too.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: European Union is, in many ways, nastier than China. Okay? And we've just started with them. Oh, they'll come down a lot. You watch. We have all the cards. They treated us very unfairly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: They sell us 13 million cars. We sell them none. They sell us their agricultural products. We sell them virtually none. They don't take our products. That gives us all the cards. And very unfair. So they're going to have to pay more for health care, and we're going to have to pay less. That's all it is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And believe it or not—you know, because it's really the world we're talking about, not just the European Union. But because it's the world, the numbers are, for the health care company, not as bad as you would think. They'll make the same. I think the health care companies should make pretty much the same money.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: I really don't believe they're going to—they should be affected very much, because it's just a redistribution of wealth. It's a redistribution where it could be the same top line, but it's going to be distributed differently.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Europe is going to have to pay a little bit more, the rest of the world is going to have to pay a little bit more, and America is going to pay a lot less. Again, because we—it's a much smaller population than when you think of the whole world.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So, basically, what we're doing is equalizing. There's a new word that I came up with, which I think is probably the best word. We're going to equalize, where we're all going to pay the same. We're going to pay what Europe is going to pay. We're going to all pay—now, there may be some countries in dire need, and I would be willing to sacrifice that but—and help them.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But it's called "most favored nation." We are going to pay the lowest price there is in the world. We will get—whoever is paying the lowest price, that's the price that we're going to get. So remember that. So we're no longer paying 10 times more than another country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Whoever is paying the lowest price, we will look at that price, and we will say, "That's the price we're going to pay." Most favored nations. That's what it is.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: One breast cancer drug costs Americans over $16,000 per bottle, but the same drug from the same factory, manufactured by the same company, is one-sixth that price in Australia and one- tenth that price in Sweden. One-tenth for the identical product.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: A common asthma drug costs almost $500 here in America, but costs less than $40 in the United Kingdom. So $40 in the United Kingdom, which is where this gentleman told me he paid a small amount for his shot. But think of that. So $40 versus $500 here. That's not even bad.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: There are much worse examples.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And the weight-loss drug Ozempic costs 10 times more in the United States than in the rest of the developed world. Ten times more. Why? What did we do? Suckers. But we never had a President that had the courage to do this. And nobody knew the system like I do. I mean, I've gotten to know this system so well.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I don't think it's fair that it benefits Obamacare. Obamacare is a failure. It's not a good— it's not a good health care. It works. I made it work. I had an obligation to make it work or an obligation to let it die. I chose that we had to make it work. I had to make it as good as possible.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I had a choice. I could have let it fail or make it as good as possible. "As good as possible" means it was still not very good, but it was—it survived. And we did the right thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But this makes it—just makes everything work. And I don't want to have a bad form of health care work because of the fact I was able to cut drug prices by 80 or 90 percent.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: So we're going to maybe come up with something. I think this gives the Republicans a chance to actually do a health care that's much better than Obamacare and for less money, which—if you guys would work on that, along with Congress.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But I do want to say that Democrats could have done this a long time ago. They have fought like hell for the drug companies, and they knew they were doing the wrong thing.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And it's going to be very hard. I was just telling the leader and the Speaker that—how do— it's going to be very hard for the Democrats to vote against the one big, beautiful deal—the greatest tax cuts in history, greatest everything, but now you have the big drug prices, because that's going to be included.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: It makes that whole situation different, from a scoring standpoint. I just told them. I called them up about this. I said: "I'm going to do something that's going to be very monumental, and you're going to be scoring. You'd better tell your people that this is going to score really well, and then add hundreds of billions of dollars in tariffs to your list also." But, as big as the tariffs are, this is something that really hits quickly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Five years ago, I signed an Executive order to confront this disaster, but only confront it in a minor way. It was a good confrontation, but never to this extent. And took people a little while to understand a very complicated system.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: But Joe Biden, without—any knowledge of what he was doing, terminated the policy and then pretended to negotiate under a new system. And then, you take a look, 5 out of the 10 drugs that he negotiated are now over 200-percent more expensive in America than the rest of the world and far more expensive than when he even got involved—much more expensive than when he got involved.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Joe Biden's plan was a—as you know, because you wrote about it; you don't say it very loudly—but it was a very big failure, as was his whole Presidency.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: First, I'm directing the U.S. Trade Representatives and Department of Commerce to begin investigations into foreign nations that extort drug companies by blocking their products unless they accept bottom-line and very low dollar amounts for their product, unfairly shifting the cost burden onto American patients. And we'll be taking a look at that very strongly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The biggest thing we're going to do is, we're going to tell those countries, like those represented by the European Union, that the—you know, that game is up. Sorry. And if they want to get cute, then they don't have to sell cars into the United States anymore. It's a very big subject.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And they won't get cute, because I'll defend the drug companies from that standpoint. They were given a price by the European Unions and other countries: "This is what you do. This is what we're going to pay. We're not going to pay any more. Let America pay the difference," because there was a big short fall. "Let America pay it." And that's what we did, but we're not doing it anymore.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Next, my administration will secure what we're calling "most-favored-nations drug pricing." The principle is simple: Whatever the lowest price paid for a drug in other developed countries, that is the price that Americans will pay. And we're using the term "other developed countries" because there are some countries that need some additional help, and that's fine. I think that's very good.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: Some prescription drug and pharmaceutical prices will be reduced almost immediately by 50 to 80 to 90 percent. Big Pharma will either abide by this principle voluntarily or we'll use the power of the Federal Government to ensure that we are paying the same price as other countries.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: To accelerate these price restrictions and reductions, my administration will also cut out the middlemen. We're going to totally cut out the famous middlemen. Nobody knows who they are, middlemen. They've—I've been hearing the term for 25 years, "middlemen." I don't know who they are, but they're rich, that I can tell you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We're going to cut out the middlemen and facilitate the direct sale of drugs at the most- favored-nation price, directly to the American citizen. So we're cutting out, Bobby, the middleman. It's so important, right? They've got to do that. They get——they're worse than the drug companies. They don't even make a product and they make a fortune. That's—very smart businesspeople, that I can tell you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: If companies make no significant progress toward most-favored-nation pricing—which we will insist that they do, so I think I'm wasting time talking about it. We're going to insist upon it, and we'll insist—and we're going to help the drug companies with the other nations, because those other nations do a lot of trading with us. They need our trade, just like China needed us very badly. They need us just as badly.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We will do whatever we have to with trade, just like we did some great things with trade with India and Pakistan. It really helped the situation—a very heated situation. Could have lost millions of people. More than millions. I mean, many millions of people. And they want to do business with America. But we never used our powers that way. We never knew how. We never had people that knew how to do that.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: We'll also open up America's market to safe and legal imports of affordable drugs from other countries, putting dramatic downward pressure on prices. And if necessary, we'll investigate the drug companies. And we'll, in particular, investigate the countries that are doing this, and we will add it onto the price that we charge them for doing business in America. In other words, we'll add it onto tariffs if they don't do what is right, which is everybody should equalize. Everybody should say—pay the same price.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And special interests may not like this very much, but the American people will. I mean, I am doing this for the American people. I'm doing this against the most powerful lobby in the world, probably—the drug lobby—drug and pharmaceutical lobby. But it's one of the most important orders, I think, that's ever been signed, certainly with regard to health care or health, in the history of our country, and it's an honor to be a part of it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: And I'd like to ask Robert F. Kennedy to say a few words, please. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr
full_topic_context.text: Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. Thank you, Mr. President. This is an extraordinary day. This is an issue that—you know, I grew up in the Democratic Party, and every major Democratic leader for 20 years has been making this promise to the American people. This was the fulcrum of Bernie Sanders's runs for Presidency, that he was going to eliminate this discrepancy between Europe and the United States. But, as it turns out, none of them were doing it. It's one of these promises that politicians make to their constituents, knowing that they'll never have to do it. And the reason they'll never have to do it is because they know that Congress is controlled in so many ways by the pharmaceutical industry.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [At this point, Secretary Kennedy continued his remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr
full_topic_context.text: We now have a President who is a man of his word, who has the courage. President Trump was taking money from the pharmaceutical industry too. I think they gave you $100 million—

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Yes.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Kennedy
full_topic_context.text: Secretary Kennedy. ——but he can't be bought, unlike most of the politicians in this country.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Kennedy
full_topic_context.text: And he is standing here for the American people. I don't know what—you know, there's— there's writers, like Elizabeth Warren or Robert Reich, who are saying that President Trump is on this side of the oligarchs. There has never been a President more willing to stand up to the oligarchs than President Donald Trump.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Secretary Kennedy continued his remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Kennedy
full_topic_context.text: So I am—I'm just so grateful to be here today. I never thought that this would happen in my lifetime.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Kennedy
full_topic_context.text: I have a couple of kids who are Democrats, are big Bernie Sanders fans, and when I told them that this was going to happen, they had tears in their eyes because they thought, "This is never going to happen in our lifetime." And we finally have a President who is willing to stand up for the American people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Kennedy
full_topic_context.text: Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Secretary Kennedy
full_topic_context.text: And, Dr. Oz.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Mehmet Oz
full_topic_context.text: Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Mehmet Oz. Thank you, Secretary Kennedy.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Mehmet Oz
full_topic_context.text: This is the most powerful Executive order on pharmacy pricing and health care ever in the history of our Nation, and it's only happening because we have a President with the fortitude, the guts to stand up to the withering criticism and lobbying that's going to occur soon as folks hear about the Executive order.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Mehmet Oz
full_topic_context.text: So, on behalf of the child in Philadelphia who's got an autoimmune disease with a thousand- dollar-a-month drug, or the older woman in Los Angeles who's on a blood thinner who can't afford her co-pay, I want to thank President Trump. God bless you for having the guts to take on this industry.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Mehmet Oz
full_topic_context.text: Thank you, sir.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. I appreciate it.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator Oz
full_topic_context.text: Administrator Oz. So let's talk about the details a little bit. And this is primarily about equalization, as President Trump said. It's about fairness.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator Oz
full_topic_context.text: Think of NATO as a metaphor. When President Trump said, "You've got to pay a little more so it makes sense for all of us," they came up, and the European countries contributed. The same thing, we believe, will happen in this situation.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator Oz
full_topic_context.text: Most people who have thought about this process agree that it is patently unfair to tolerate the numbers that Secretary Kennedy and President Trump have reflected to you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Editorial
full_topic_context.text: [Administrator Oz continued his remarks, concluding as follows.]

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator Oz
full_topic_context.text: But the fact that, in my lifetime, as Secretary Kennedy said, for the first time, we have a thoughtful and aggressive approach, thanks to President Trump, on taking on the special interests, I—should give all Americans confidence that this is an administration that stands for fairness and should chill the waters for those who believe they can push us away from our North Star, which is to take care of the American people.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator Oz
full_topic_context.text: Mr. President, God bless you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Trump
full_topic_context.text: The President. Thank you very much. Thank you.

full_topic_context.speaker: Administrator Oz
full_topic_context.text: Administrator Oz. Jay, you want to go next?

full_topic_context.speaker: National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya
full_topic_context.text: National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya. Sure.

full_topic_context.speaker: National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya
full_topic_context.text: So I teach economics at Stanford as well as health policy, and one thing that's really, really simple in economics is that when you have a persistent price difference for the same product between two countries, there is something deeply wrong.
